literal_comparison_clauses.text:
# 1. Introduction

Classification provides the semantic organization through which documents are grouped into meaningful categories.

Within the Documentation Framework, Classification supports:

- organization;
- navigation;
- governance;
- discovery.

Classification is independent of the physical location of documents.

The Classification architecture therefore requires more than a formal model.

It also requires practices that preserve semantic clarity, structural consistency, maintainability and long-term architectural integrity.

Classification Best Practices defines recommended practices for designing, using, maintaining and evolving the Classification component.

This document is **informative**.

It provides guidance rather than introducing additional normative requirements beyond those established by the Classification architecture, constraints and specification.

**Current advisory context and sourced duties.**

This entire guide remains informative,including imperative wording,examples,workflows and checklists. It creates no independent normative mandate or violation from recommendation omission. Actual applicable owner requirements retain their own source/edition/scope/authority;they do not become optional because this guide says should. Reference/current04-Reference fits consultation responsibility,not authority by label. Local working Draft correction is not canonical adoption.

---

# 4. Nature of Best Practices

Best practices provide recommendations rather than independent architectural requirements.

The distinction is:

**Received unnamed visual in §4 (span 1 in original order).** Exact received wording is retained as qualified evidence and illustration.

```text

       Classification Architecture
                    │
                    ▼

             Normative Rules
             │
             ├── Schema
             ├── Constraints
             ├── Lifecycle
             └── Specification
          
              Best Practices
                    │
                    ▼

       Recommended Ways of Applying
               Those Rules

```

**Current recommended relation scope:** Consultation roles and actual sourced requirements versus informative application advice;no authority by label/order,new mandate or completed conformance.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation and authority limit |
|---|---|
| Classification Architecture | Actual responsible source/role to consult for identified editions,scope,authority and applicable clauses;title/Type/directory or reading order alone creates no normative priority,completed implementation or canonical acceptance. Best Practices does not add or waive its real requirements. |
| Normative Rules | Actual applicable owner requirement/definition/rule/set/source editions,scope,applicability,authority,precedence and evidence. Known duties remain with genuine gaps;this guide creates no new rule,complete catalog,priority,waiver or implemented result. |
| Schema | Actual structural source/role and responsible known obligations/general multiplicity-field-population gaps. Not authority by name,universal fields/role tree or complete representation conformity from citation. |
| Constraints | Actual applicable owner requirement/definition/rule/set/source editions,scope,applicability,authority,precedence and evidence. Known duties remain with genuine gaps;this guide creates no new rule,complete catalog,priority,waiver or implemented result. |
| Lifecycle | Actual subject-specific state/use/transition/history role or illustrative independent dimension under actual owner context. Classification Element/definition/assignment,document Workflow,extension/proposal/decision,term/R/result/finding/Milestone states differ;no universal machine/aliases or performed event. |
| Specification | Actual scoped normative integration/consultation role where its declaration applies,not authority by title or complete accepted catalog. In semantic examples this label is a generic knowledge category,not a fifth primary Type or allocated Class. |
| Best Practices | Explicitly informative recommendation/consultation role. Advice creates no independent requirement or violation from omission;actual sourced mandates retain their own authority. Not approval,permission or full implementation evidence. |
| Recommended Ways of Applying | Explicitly informative recommendation/consultation role. Advice creates no independent requirement or violation from omission;actual sourced mandates retain their own authority. Not approval,permission or full implementation evidence. |
| Those Rules | Actual applicable owner requirement/definition/rule/set/source editions,scope,applicability,authority,precedence and evidence. Known duties remain with genuine gaps;this guide creates no new rule,complete catalog,priority,waiver or implemented result. |


Best practices should therefore guide decisions without creating an alternative Classification model.

**Current advisory context and sourced duties.**

The received role diagram illustrates consultation roles,not authority inherent in Architecture,Schema,Specification or Type Reference.

| Concern | Actual authority boundary | Advisory consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Best Practices recommendation | Explicitly informative here;actual adoption of a particular requirement would need its own responsible contract | Recommend sound application without creating new mandates or violations from omission |
| Actual sourced requirement | Identify responsible source/definition/rule edition,scope,applicability and authority | Preserve its actual mandatory force;should wording here waives none |
| Normative or informative source role | Authority follows actual declarations/incorporation,not title,directory,Type or diagram order | Consult actual owner clauses;do not infer precedence from role labels |
| Real conflict / missing authority | Actual Specification-owned precedence and Governance/necessary revision apply under Constraints54/56/59 | Unknown scope/priority is unresolved,not a new rule,waiver or automatic success |

No new requirement is allocated by this table.

---

# 6. Treat Classification as Knowledge Structure

Classification should be treated as a semantic structure rather than merely a filing mechanism.

A document's Classification should communicate something meaningful about the knowledge represented by that document.

The Framework defines documentation as a structured representation of knowledge and documents as coherent units of knowledge.

Therefore, Classification should answer questions such as:

- What kind of knowledge does this document represent?
- What role does the document play?
- What architectural context does it belong to?
- How does it relate to other classified knowledge?

**Current advisory context and sourced duties.**

All four questions remain recommended semantic inquiry,not a required physical field catalog or allocated population. Current Family is component/admitted documentary-area membership,primary Type exactly one uniform Architecture/Structure/Behavior/Reference responsibility,Class separate optional defined nonconflicting meaning. Actual scheme/definition/assignment context still matters.

---

# 8. Avoid Classification by Appearance

Classification should not be based solely on superficial characteristics.

For example, documents should not be classified differently merely because they are:

- Markdown files;
- PDF files;
- source files;
- generated files.

The relevant question is what the document represents, not how it is physically represented.

**Current advisory context and sourced duties.**

Representation labels do not decide meaning or current Type. Actual equivalent content/subject/source edition and responsible representation/Profile/Instance duties need checking;format conversion or generated-file presence alone proves no full conformity,canonical approval or installed capability.

---

# 9. Define Before Classifying

A Classification Element should be defined before it is broadly used.

The definition should establish its intended meaning and context.

A useful sequence is:

**Received unnamed visual in §9 (span 2 in original order).** Exact received wording is retained as qualified evidence and illustration.

```text

               Requirement
                    │
                    ▼

                 Concept
                    │
                    ▼

                Definition
                    │
                    ▼

          Classification Element
                    │
                    ▼

                  Usage

```

**Current recommended relation scope:** Recommended definition-before-broad-use inquiry,not automatic canonical permission,allocated member or complete operational workflow.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation and authority limit |
|---|---|
| Requirement | Selected recommended need/concept/definition/subject/use concern requiring actual semantic identity,source edition,context and responsible authority/state/use evidence for real claims. Not allocated DF identity/fields,canonical approval or performed assignment from sequence. |
| Concept | Selected recommended need/concept/definition/subject/use concern requiring actual semantic identity,source edition,context and responsible authority/state/use evidence for real claims. Not allocated DF identity/fields,canonical approval or performed assignment from sequence. |
| Definition | Selected recommended need/concept/definition/subject/use concern requiring actual semantic identity,source edition,context and responsible authority/state/use evidence for real claims. Not allocated DF identity/fields,canonical approval or performed assignment from sequence. |
| Classification Element | Selected recommended need/concept/definition/subject/use concern requiring actual semantic identity,source edition,context and responsible authority/state/use evidence for real claims. Not allocated DF identity/fields,canonical approval or performed assignment from sequence. |
| Usage | Selected recommended need/concept/definition/subject/use concern requiring actual semantic identity,source edition,context and responsible authority/state/use evidence for real claims. Not allocated DF identity/fields,canonical approval or performed assignment from sequence. |


This reduces the risk of Classification emerging implicitly from usage.

**Current advisory context and sourced duties.**

The selected definition-before-use sequence is advice,not a complete permission/workflow or actual allocated Element. Actual definition/source edition,applicability,authority/state/use and required approval/conditions/effective adoption still govern actual broad/canonical use. Authorized working proposals/Drafts may prepare correction without false canonicality.

---

# 10. Prefer Existing Concepts

Before creating a new Classification Element, determine whether an existing element already represents the intended concept.

The preferred decision process is:

**Received unnamed visual in §10 (span 3 in original order).** Exact received wording is retained as qualified evidence and illustration.

```text

             New Requirement
                    │
                    ▼

            Existing Element?
                    │
             ┌──────┴──────┐
             │             │
            Yes            No
             │             │
             ▼             ▼

           Reuse       Define New

```

**Current recommended relation scope:** Reuse/define inquiry branches need actual semantics/authority/evidence,not names or missing lookup as automatic identity/decision.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation and authority limit |
|---|---|
| New Requirement | Selected recommended need/concept/definition/subject/use concern requiring actual semantic identity,source edition,context and responsible authority/state/use evidence for real claims. Not allocated DF identity/fields,canonical approval or performed assignment from sequence. |
| Existing Element? | Selected reuse/definition inquiry or branch. Actual definition/edition/context/equivalence/authority evidence is needed;names or unknown lookup alone prove no duplicate,new allocation,actual decision/permission or completed evaluation. |
| Yes | Selected reuse/definition inquiry or branch. Actual definition/edition/context/equivalence/authority evidence is needed;names or unknown lookup alone prove no duplicate,new allocation,actual decision/permission or completed evaluation. |
| No | Selected reuse/definition inquiry or branch. Actual definition/edition/context/equivalence/authority evidence is needed;names or unknown lookup alone prove no duplicate,new allocation,actual decision/permission or completed evaluation. |
| Reuse | Selected reuse/definition inquiry or branch. Actual definition/edition/context/equivalence/authority evidence is needed;names or unknown lookup alone prove no duplicate,new allocation,actual decision/permission or completed evaluation. |
| Define New | Selected reuse/definition inquiry or branch. Actual definition/edition/context/equivalence/authority evidence is needed;names or unknown lookup alone prove no duplicate,new allocation,actual decision/permission or completed evaluation. |


This supports the Single Source of Truth principle, which requires each architectural concept to have one authoritative definition and discourages duplicated definitions.

**Current advisory context and sourced duties.**

Reuse needs actual equivalence of definition/source edition,scope/context and authority;matching names or absent lookup evidence alone proves neither reuse nor a new concept. Existing Element?/Yes/No are reasoning branches,not actual decisions,outcomes or key allocation.

---

# 11. Avoid Semantic Duplication

Do not introduce multiple Classification Elements merely because different authors use different terminology.

For example:

**Received unnamed visual in §11 (span 4 in original order).** Exact received wording is retained as qualified evidence and illustration.

```text

    Architectural Decision
    Architecture Decision
    Architecture Design Decision

```

**Current recommended relation scope:** Unallocated terminology comparison for same/related/distinct concepts,not new primary Types or actual alias registry.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation and authority limit |
|---|---|
| Architectural Decision | Unallocated example terminology for same/related/distinct meaning inquiry,not additional primary Type values or automatically registered aliases. Actual definition/source/context/authority determines semantic distinction,not spelling alone. |
| Architecture Decision | Unallocated example terminology for same/related/distinct meaning inquiry,not additional primary Type values or automatically registered aliases. Actual definition/source/context/authority determines semantic distinction,not spelling alone. |
| Architecture Design Decision | Unallocated example terminology for same/related/distinct meaning inquiry,not additional primary Type values or automatically registered aliases. Actual definition/source/context/authority determines semantic distinction,not spelling alone. |


should not automatically become three distinct Classification Elements.

First determine whether they represent:

- the same concept;
- related concepts;
- genuinely distinct concepts.

**Current advisory context and sourced duties.**

All three received decision names are unallocated terminology examples,not primary Type values or an accepted synonym registry. Actual same/related/distinct meaning needs responsible definition/edition/context/evidence;advice performs no merge,rekey,alias allocation or semantic identity deletion.

---

# 12. Distinguish Synonyms from Concepts

Different names may refer to the same concept.

Where this occurs, the Classification Dictionary should identify the canonical terminology.

Classification should not encode vocabulary variation as semantic variation unless the concepts are genuinely different.

**Current advisory context and sourced duties.**

Canonical term,name,display label,definition/source edition,semantic identity and represented record differ. Actual Dictionary authority/definition and permitted synonyms must substantiate a terminology claim;names alone do not create a complete vocabulary or transfer domain ownership.

---

# 14. Avoid Overly Broad Categories

A Classification Element should not become a generic container for unrelated concepts.

For example:

**Received unnamed visual in §14 (span 5 in original order).** Exact received wording is retained as qualified evidence and illustration.

```text

    Miscellaneous
    Other
    General
    Various

```

**Current recommended relation scope:** Illustrative broad names with actual semantic-justification exception,not universal forbidden values or measured constraint violations.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation and authority limit |
|---|---|
| Miscellaneous | Illustrative broad-category labels,not universally forbidden/reserved values or accepted population. Actual justified semantic purpose/definition/authority matters;advice alone proves no violation. |
| Other | Illustrative broad-category labels,not universally forbidden/reserved values or accepted population. Actual justified semantic purpose/definition/authority matters;advice alone proves no violation. |
| General | Illustrative broad-category labels,not universally forbidden/reserved values or accepted population. Actual justified semantic purpose/definition/authority matters;advice alone proves no violation. |
| Various | Illustrative broad-category labels,not universally forbidden/reserved values or accepted population. Actual justified semantic purpose/definition/authority matters;advice alone proves no violation. |


should be avoided as canonical categories unless their semantic purpose is explicitly justified.

Broad categories reduce the information value of Classification.

**Current advisory context and sourced duties.**

Miscellaneous/Other/General/Various are example labels,not reserved or forbidden universal values. Actual explicitly defined semantic purpose and authority matter;advice against broad categories alone establishes no constraint violation or allocated vocabulary.

---

# 15. Avoid Overly Narrow Categories

The opposite problem is excessive specialization.

A new Classification Element should provide meaningful semantic value.

Do not introduce a new category merely because two documents differ in a minor detail.

The goal is a useful semantic structure rather than maximum fragmentation.

**Current advisory context and sourced duties.**

Granularity advice creates no numeric threshold or automatic reject/approve outcome. Actual meaningful distinction/context/authority and user needs should support a proposal;current optional defined Class and uniform primary Type do not permit arbitrary new role values.

---

# 16. Maintain Appropriate Granularity

Classification granularity should be consistent.

Conceptually:

**Received unnamed visual in §16 (span 6 in original order).** Exact received wording is retained as qualified evidence and illustration.

```text

                Too Broad
                    │
                    ▼

            Useful Granularity
                    │
                    ▼

              Too Fragmented

```

**Current recommended relation scope:** Qualitative granularity concerns,not universal numeric thresholds,state transitions or completed quality metrics.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation and authority limit |
|---|---|
| Too Broad | Qualitative recommended granularity/heuristic concern,not measured implementation state,numeric threshold,canonical permission or severity/outcome enum. Actual need/context/authority/evidence remain. |
| Useful Granularity | Qualitative recommended granularity/heuristic concern,not measured implementation state,numeric threshold,canonical permission or severity/outcome enum. Actual need/context/authority/evidence remain. |
| Too Fragmented | Qualitative recommended granularity/heuristic concern,not measured implementation state,numeric threshold,canonical permission or severity/outcome enum. Actual need/context/authority/evidence remain. |


The appropriate level depends on:

- the purpose of Classification;
- the information being represented;
- discovery requirements;
- governance requirements;
- maintenance cost.

**Current advisory context and sourced duties.**

Too Broad/Useful Granularity/Too Fragmented are qualitative heuristics,not measured current architecture states,universal cardinalities or severity. All five purpose/information/discovery/governance/cost concerns remain recommended actual context,with no automatic threshold or completed check.

---

# 17. Keep Hierarchy Meaningful

Any actual explicitly defined scheme hierarchy should communicate its responsible structural meaning;documentary Family,Type and Class are not universally a specialization chain.

For example:

**Received unnamed visual in §17 (span 7 in original order).** Exact received wording is retained as qualified evidence and illustration.

```text

            Family
            │
            └── Type
                │
                └── Class

```

**Current recommended relation scope:** Historical role-tree example;current complementary membership/uniform Type/optional Class and actual separately defined scheme hierarchy apply.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation and authority limit |
|---|---|
| Family | Received historical/conditional role-tree/direction position. Current Family is real component/admitted documentary-area membership,not universal semantic parent owning primary Type. Actual scheme hierarchy needs responsible definitions;no component/key/population allocated. |
| Type | Received historical/generic role/example position,not an allocated Family-specific responsibility. Actual primary document Type is exactly one uniform Architecture/Structure/Behavior/Reference across Families;actual valid-use context does not create a fifth value. |
| Class | Received historical/conditional role-tree position. Current Class is separate optional explicitly defined nonconflicting meaning,not universal Type child,mandatory field/value,unrestricted string or known complete vocabulary/count. |


is received historical role-tree evidence,not the current universal primary-role model. Actual scheme-specific refinement needs an explicit responsible definition.

A hierarchy should not exist merely because a tree structure is convenient.

**Current advisory context and sourced duties.**

Current complementary membership Family,uniform primary Type and optional defined Class do not impose a universal specialization tree. The exact received drawing is historical evidence;an actual separately defined scheme may have hierarchy under responsible rules,not from this recommendation.

---

# 18. Avoid Artificial Hierarchies

Do not create intermediate Classification Elements solely to make a tree deeper.

For example:

**Received unnamed visual in §18 (span 8 in original order).** Exact received wording is retained as qualified evidence and illustration.

```text

            Family
            │
            └── Group
                │
                └── Category
                    │
                    └── Type
                        │
                        └── Class

```

**Current recommended relation scope:** Historical/generic intermediate-tree anti-pattern,not actual allocated components/fields or current required role hierarchy.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation and authority limit |
|---|---|
| Family | Received historical/conditional role-tree/direction position. Current Family is real component/admitted documentary-area membership,not universal semantic parent owning primary Type. Actual scheme hierarchy needs responsible definitions;no component/key/population allocated. |
| Group | Hypothetical intermediate semantic concept/position in an anti-pattern,not automatically allocated architectural component,field,Level or actual required hierarchy. Real defined meaning/context/authority is needed. |
| Category | Hypothetical intermediate semantic concept/position in an anti-pattern,not automatically allocated architectural component,field,Level or actual required hierarchy. Real defined meaning/context/authority is needed. |

# 88. Extension Practices

This document constitutes the normative specification of the Classification component within the Documentation Framework.

It consolidates the architectural principles, concepts, model, elements, schema, lifecycle, validation, governance, relationships, constraints, extensibility and terminology defined throughout the Classification documentation family into a single authoritative specification.

This document defines the contractual requirements that every Classification implementation shall satisfy in order to conform to the Documentation Framework.

Classification is an architectural mechanism for organizing documents according to meaningful semantic categories.

It is independent of physical document storage, implementation technology and repository structure.

**Current governing scope.**

This remains a normative consolidated Specification by its explicit declaration and incorporation,not by Type Reference or title. Actual working source/definition/rule/set editions,scope/applicability,authority,conditions/evidence and mandatory coverage govern claims. Draft/canonical wording does not prove a complete approved population,effective canonical adoption,publication,Baseline or global integration. Adopted ReviewPolicy permits this authorized working correction;actual responsible mandates remain independently applicable. Reference/current04-Reference fits primary consultation responsibility.

# 5. Specification Principles

This specification is founded upon the following principles.

**Current governing scope.**

All seven original principle subjects remain. They apply under actual source/definition/scope authority,ordinary preservation and necessary assessed revision§38;they are not a complete populated architecture or automatic exemption from cross-owner mandates.

---

## 5.1. Architectural Consistency

Classification shall conform to the architecture of the Documentation Framework.

Classification is an architectural component and shall preserve the architectural boundaries defined by the Framework.

**Current governing scope.**

Actual component boundaries,domain/common interfaces and provider duties are real. Ordinary conformity does not permit ownership takeover;necessary assessed role/interface mandate revision needs actual prior/new authority§38 and cannot silently waive unchanged external restrictions.

---

## 5.2. Semantic Consistency

Classification Elements shall have stable and unambiguous semantic meanings.

Equivalent concepts shall not be represented as independent canonical Classification Elements without an explicit semantic justification.

**Current governing scope.**

Actual identified concept/definition/source edition/context meaning and canonical authority support uniqueness. Real synonyms/labels/representation copies alone are not competing canonical concepts. Necessary assessed revision preserves required old interpretation without a permanent all-time freeze or manufactured scope tags hiding conflict.

---

## 5.3. Technology Independence

Classification shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

The meaning of a Classification Element shall not depend on:

- programming language;
- storage technology;
- repository;
- serialization format;
- documentation tool;
- rendering engine.

The architectural concepts of the Framework are explicitly required to remain independent from implementation technologies.

**Current governing scope.**

All six listed implementation environments remain examples of what cannot alone determine meaning. Actual concrete source bytes/representations/Schema/effective Profile/Instance/reference/index/access/retrieval/freshness/history and provider requirements remain claim-relevant. Neutral semantics are not full physical or current-use conformity.

---

## 5.4. Canonical Definition

Every canonical Classification concept shall possess one authoritative definition.

The Classification Dictionary provides the authoritative terminology reference for the component.

**Current governing scope.**

Canonical Element authoritative-definition obligations remain,including§15 ten minimum subjects. A term heading or glossary definition is not automatically canonical adoption,complete Element entry/population or Metadata field allocation. Actual term/name/definition/identity/state/source editions and responsible authority/evidence must support each claim.

---

## 5.5. Explicit Architecture

Classification semantics shall be explicitly defined.

Critical semantics shall not depend exclusively on:

- directory structure;
- filename conventions;
- implementation behavior;
- undocumented assumptions.

The Framework favors explicit architectural relationships over implicit conventions.

**Current governing scope.**

All four explicit-semantics concerns remain;directory/file/tool conventions cannot silently supply critical meaning. Real explicit identity/reference/placement/representation contracts and actual bytes still matter. Explicit relation definitions/assertions differ from documentary reading order and indispensable providers;no complete DAG from a diagram.

---

## 5.6. Controlled Evolution

Classification shall evolve only through the lifecycle, validation and governance mechanisms defined by the Documentation Framework.

**Current governing scope.**

Actual required lifecycle/validation/Governance mandates retain force,including conditions/fulfillment and separate effective operations. Working proposal/Draft correction may prepare change without false canonicality;real actors/guards/routes/record/effective authority for an operation remain necessary and are not invented here.

---

## 5.7. Traceability

Classification changes shall remain historically traceable.

The evolution of Classification shall preserve sufficient information to determine what changed, why it changed and which architectural decision authorized the change.

**Current governing scope.**

Required history retains actual prior/new source/definition/rule/set/relationship/assignment/state/decision/condition/result editions and needed pinned context. Interpretation,original conformity,current use and retrieval differ;actual later earlier-contract reassessment preserves observations rather than backdating new rules or erasing failures.

# 1. Introduction

This document provides examples illustrating the application of the Classification component of the Documentation Framework.

The examples demonstrate how the concepts, elements, schema, lifecycle, validation, governance, relationships, constraints and extensibility mechanisms defined by the Classification documentation family may be applied.

The examples are intentionally illustrative.

They do not define additional Classification requirements.

Where an example appears to conflict with a normative requirement, the applicable normative document takes precedence.

---

# 5. Example 1 — Basic Classification

Consider a document describing the architectural structure of a software system.

The document may be assigned to a Classification Element representing architecture.

Conceptually:

```text

                 Document
                    │
                    ▼

        Classification Assignment
                    │
                    ▼

               Architecture

```

The Classification assignment establishes that the document belongs to the semantic category represented by `Architecture`.

The document's physical location does not determine this Classification.

For example, the document could be stored at:

```text

    /docs/architecture.md

```

or:

```text

    /project/design/system-architecture.md

```

without changing its Classification.

---

# 6. Example 2 — Hierarchical Classification

A Classification hierarchy may be represented as:

```text

            Documentation
            │
            ├── Architecture
            │   ├── Principles
            │   ├── Concepts
            │   └── Design
            │
            ├── Development
            │   ├── Coding
            │   ├── Testing
            │   └── Build
            │
            └── Operations
                ├── Deployment
                ├── Monitoring
                └── Maintenance

```

In this example:

- `Documentation` is a broader Classification Element;
- `Architecture` is a specialization;
- `Principles` is a further specialization of `Architecture`;
- `Concepts` is a further specialization of `Architecture`.

The hierarchy expresses semantic specialization.

It is not merely a directory structure.

---

# 7. Example 3 — Parent and Child Elements

Consider:

```text

            Architecture
            │
            └── Architectural Principles

```

Here:

```text

    Parent =  Architecture
    Child  =  Architectural Principles

```

The child represents a more specific semantic concept than the parent.

A valid hierarchical relationship therefore expresses:

```text

            Architectural Principles

             IS A SPECIALIZATION OF

                  Architecture

```

It would not be appropriate to create the relationship merely because the two documents happen to be stored in the same directory.

---

# 8. Example 4 — Classification Elements

A fictional Classification model may contain:

| Identifier | Name | Parent |
|------------|------|--------|
| CLS-ARCH | Architecture | — |
| CLS-ARCH-PRN | Architectural Principles | CLS-ARCH |
| CLS-ARCH-CON | Architectural Concepts | CLS-ARCH |
| CLS-DEV | Development | — |
| CLS-DEV-TST | Testing | CLS-DEV |

The identifiers provide stable identity.

The names provide human-readable terminology.

The parent relationship provides semantic structure.

---

# 9. Example 5 — Classification Assignment

Suppose the following document exists:

```text

    Document ID: DOC-001
    Title: Architectural Principles

```

The document may receive:

```text

    Classification:
        Architecture

```

The assignment can conceptually be represented as:

```text

            DOC-001
            │
            └── classified-as ──► Architecture

```

The Classification assignment does not change the identity of `DOC-001`.

It provides semantic categorization.

---

# 10. Example 6 — Multiple Classification Assignments

A document may legitimately participate in more than one Classification context when the Classification Schema permits multiple assignments.

For example:

```text

    Document: Testing Strategy

```

may be associated with:

```text

    Development
    Testing
    Quality

```

Conceptually:

```text

                             ┌─────►  Development
                             │
            Testing Strategy ├─────►  Testing
                             │
                             └─────►  Quality

```

Whether multiple assignments are permitted is determined by the applicable Classification Schema and Constraints.

This example therefore demonstrates a possible use, not a universal rule.

---

# 11. Example 7 — Classification and Document Identity

Consider:

```text

    Document ID: DF-CLS-015
    Title: Classification Examples
    Classification: Classification

```

The two concepts have different responsibilities.

```text

            Document Identity
            │
            └── identifies the document

            Classification
            │
            └── categorizes the document

```

Changing the Classification does not create a different document identity.

Likewise, changing the document identity does not automatically redefine its Classification.

---

# 12. Example 8 — Classification and Metadata

Consider a document with the following metadata:

```text

    Document ID: DOC-017
    Title: Deployment Architecture
    Author: Example Author
    Status: Approved
    Classification: Architecture

```

The fields have different responsibilities.

```text

    Document ID
        ─────►  identifies the document

    Title
        ─────►  names the document

    Author
        ─────►  provides descriptive information

    Status
        ─────►  represents lifecycle information

    Classification
        ─────►  provides semantic categorization

```

Classification should not be used as a replacement for general Metadata.

---

# 13. Example 9 — Classification Schema

A simplified Classification Schema might specify:

```text

    ClassificationElement
        Identifier
        Name
        Definition
        Parent
        LifecycleState

```

A document assignment may then be represented conceptually as:

```text

    ClassificationAssignment
        Document
        ClassificationElement

```

The schema defines the permitted structure.

It does not define the meaning of every individual Classification Element.

That meaning is provided by the applicable definitions.

---

# 14. Example 10 — Cardinality Constraint

Suppose a Classification Schema specifies:

```text

    Document
        ClassificationElement
            Cardinality:  1..*

```

This means that every classified document must have at least one Classification assignment.

For example:

```text

            Document A
            ├── Architecture
            └── Design

```

satisfies the example cardinality.

A document with:

```text

            Document B
            └── no Classification

```

does not satisfy it.

The actual cardinality applicable to a Classification implementation is determined by its normative Schema and Constraints.

---

# 15. Example 11 — Invalid Classification Reference

Suppose a document contains:

```text

    Classification: UnknownCategory

```

but `UnknownCategory` is not defined by the Classification Schema.

The assignment is invalid.

Conceptually:

```text

                 Document
                    │
                    ▼

             UnknownCategory
                    │
                    X

               Not defined

```

Validation should detect the invalid reference.

---

# 16. Example 12 — Invalid Hierarchy

Consider:

```text

            Architecture
            │
            └── Testing

```

If the Classification Model defines `Testing` as belonging to `Development`, then assigning it directly beneath `Architecture` may violate the applicable structural or semantic constraints.

The problem is not necessarily the names.

The problem is that the relationship does not conform to the defined Classification Model.

---

# 17. Example 13 — Semantic Duplication

Consider two Classification Elements:

```text

    CLS-001 — Architecture
    CLS-002 — System Architecture

```

Suppose both are defined as:

> Documentation describing the architectural structure of a system.

If no meaningful semantic distinction exists, the model contains potential semantic duplication.

The preferred approach is to determine whether:

- the concepts are genuinely different;
- one should be a specialization of the other;
- one is a synonym;
- one should be removed.

The Classification Dictionary should record the resulting canonical terminology.

---

# 18. Example 14 — Meaningful Specialization

Consider:

```text

            Architecture
            │
            ├── Software Architecture
            │
            └── Deployment Architecture

```

This can be a meaningful hierarchy because the concepts have distinguishable semantic scopes.

The parent expresses a broader concept.

The children express specific architectural domains.

---

# 19. Example 15 — Non-Hierarchical Relationship

Not every relationship between Classification Elements is hierarchical.

Consider:

```text

            Security
            │
            └── related-to ──► Compliance

```

The relationship indicates semantic association.

It does not imply:

```text

    Security IS A Compliance

```

or:

```text

    Compliance IS A Security

```

The relationship type therefore matters.

---

# 20. Example 16 — Relationship Definition

A relationship may be defined conceptually as:

```text

    Relationship Type:
        related-to

    Source:
        Security

    Target:
        Compliance

    Meaning:
        Security and Compliance are semantically associated.

```

This is an explicit relationship.

Its semantics do not need to be inferred from document location or naming conventions.

---

# 21. Example 17 — Lifecycle

A Classification Element may progress through a controlled lifecycle:

```text

                 Proposed
                    │
                    ▼

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

For example:

```text

    Architecture
        State: Active

```

Later:

```text

    Architecture
        State: Deprecated

```

Eventually:

```text

    Architecture
        State: Retired

```

The exact lifecycle and permitted transitions are defined by the Classification Lifecycle.

---

# 22. Example 18 — Deprecating a Classification Element

Suppose:

```text

    CLS-OLD — Technical Documentation

```

is replaced by more precise categories:

```text

    Architecture
    Development
    Operations

```

The old element may become:

```text

    Lifecycle State: Deprecated

```

New documents should use the replacement elements.

Existing documents may continue to retain the historical classification where required for traceability.

---

# 23. Example 19 — Retired Classification Element

Suppose:

```text

    CLS-OLD — Technical Documentation

```

eventually becomes:

```text

    Lifecycle State: Retired

```

Historical assignments may still contain:

```text

    Classification: CLS-OLD

```

provided that the historical information is preserved.

Retirement therefore does not necessarily mean deletion.

---

# 24. Example 20 — Validation

Consider the following Classification:

```text

    Document:
        DOC-100

    Classification:
        Architecture

    Architecture:
        Design

```

Validation may evaluate:

```text

    [PASS] Classification Element exists
    [PASS] Parent exists
    [PASS] Hierarchical relationship is valid
    [PASS] Cardinality satisfied
    [PASS] Lifecycle state valid

```

The resulting Classification is conformant with the tested rules.

---

# 25. Example 21 — Validation Failure

Consider:

```text

    Document:
        DOC-101

    Classification:
        Unknown

```

Validation may produce:

```text

    [FAIL] Classification Element does not exist

```

A second example may be:

```text

            Architecture
            │
            └── Testing

```

where the hierarchy violates the Classification Schema.

Validation may produce:

```text

    [FAIL] Invalid parent-child relationship

```

Validation identifies the violation.

It does not silently modify the Classification.

---

# 26. Example 22 — Classification Constraint

Suppose the Classification model defines:

```text

    A child element shall have exactly one parent.

```

The following structure is therefore invalid:

```text

             Architecture
             │
             ├── Design
             │
             └── Testing

                    ▲
                    │
       Development ─┘

```

if `Testing` is required to have exactly one parent.

The constraint prevents ambiguous hierarchy.

---

# 27. Example 23 — Governance of a New Element

Suppose a new concept is proposed:

```text

    AI Architecture

```

A controlled governance process may be:

```text

                 Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

             Semantic Review
                    │
                    ▼

               Model Review
                    │
                    ▼

            Constraint Review
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approval
                    │
                    ▼

             Dictionary Entry
                    │
                    ▼

      Active Classification Element

```

The element becomes canonical only after the applicable governance process has approved it.

---

# 28. Example 24 — Rejected Classification Proposal

Suppose the proposed element is:

```text

    Software Docs

```

A review determines that the concept duplicates an existing element:

```text

    Software Documentation

```

The proposal may therefore be rejected.

The rejection preserves semantic consistency by preventing unnecessary duplication.

---

# 29. Example 25 — Classification Extension

Suppose the core Classification contains:

```text

            Development
            │
            ├── Coding
            └── Testing

```

An extension introduces:

```text

            Development
            │
            ├── Coding
            ├── Testing
            └── Build

```

This can be a valid extension if:

- `Build` represents a distinct concept;
- the extension point permits it;
- the schema permits it;
- constraints remain satisfied;
- governance requirements are met.

The extension does not redefine `Coding` or `Testing`.

---

# 30. Example 26 — Invalid Extension

Suppose an extension attempts to redefine:

```text

    Testing

```

from:

> Activities concerned with verifying software behavior.

to:

> All activities related to software development.

This is not merely an extension.

It changes the semantic meaning of an existing canonical element.

Such a change must therefore be treated as an explicit Classification change and governed accordingly.

---

# 31. Example 27 — Backward Compatibility

Suppose version 1 defines:

```text

    Architecture
    └── Deployment

```

Version 2 introduces:

```text

            Architecture
            │
            ├── Software Architecture
            │
            └── Deployment Architecture

```

If the former `Deployment` element is replaced, the migration should preserve the ability to interpret existing assignments.

For example:

```text

            Deployment
            │
            └── replaced-by  ─────►  Deployment Architecture

```

The exact migration mechanism is implementation dependent.

The semantic requirement is preservation of historical meaning.

---

# 32. Example 28 — Classification Independent of Storage

The same document may be stored in different physical locations:

```text

    Repository A
        /docs/architecture.md

```

or:

```text

    Repository B
        /knowledge/design/architecture.md

```

The Classification may remain:

```text

    Architecture

```

The physical location does not define the semantic classification.

---

# 33. Example 29 — Classification Independent of Format

A document may exist as:

```text

    architecture.md
    architecture.html
    architecture.pdf

```

If these represent the same document and semantic content, conversion of the representation does not inherently constitute a Classification change.

The Classification remains:

```text

    Architecture

```

unless a deliberate Classification decision changes it.

---

# 34. Example 30 — Classification and Versioning

Consider:

```text

    Document:
        DOC-200

    Version:
        1.0

    Classification:
        Architecture

```

A later version may be:

```text

    Document:
        DOC-200

    Version:
        2.0

    Classification:
        Architecture

```

The document version does not inherently require a Classification change.

Classification should change only when the document's semantic classification changes according to the applicable rules.

---

# 35. Example 31 — Classification Change

Suppose a document originally describes architecture:

```text

    Document:
        DOC-201

    Classification:
        Architecture

```

A later revision changes its purpose so that it becomes a deployment procedure.

The Classification may change to:

```text

            Operations
            │
            └── Deployment

```

Such a change should be treated as a Classification change rather than an incidental metadata update.

---

# 36. Example 32 — Traceable Classification Change

A Classification change may be recorded conceptually as:

```text

    Change ID:
        CLS-CHG-001

    Element:
        Deployment

    Change:
        Reclassified as Deployment Procedure

    Reason:
        Document scope changed

    Decision:
        Approved

    Effective Version:
        2.0

```

The exact change-record mechanism is outside the scope of this example.

The important property is traceability.

---

# 37. Example 33 — Dictionary Entry

A canonical Dictionary entry may conceptually be represented as:

```text

    Term:
        Architecture

    Identifier:
        CLS-ARCH

    Definition:
        Classification category for documentation concerning
        the architectural structure and design of a system.

    Status:
        Active

    Related Terms:
        Architectural Principles
        Architectural Concepts
        Design

```

The Dictionary provides terminology and semantic definition.

The Classification Schema provides structural rules.

---

# 38. Example 34 — Canonical Term and Synonym

Suppose:

```text

    Canonical Term:
        Architecture

    Synonym:
        System Architecture

```

If both terms refer to the same concept, `System Architecture` should not automatically become a second Classification Element.

The Dictionary can record the synonym.

This prevents unnecessary semantic duplication.

---

# 39. Example 35 — Deprecated Term

Suppose:

```text

    Preferred Term:
        Deployment Architecture

    Deprecated Term:
        Deployment Design

```

The deprecated term remains recognizable for historical interpretation but should not normally be used for new definitions.

---

# 40. Example 36 — Classification Granularity

Consider two possible structures.

### 40.1. Structure A

```text

            Development
            │
            ├── Coding
            ├── Testing
            ├── Unit Testing
            ├── Integration Testing
            ├── Test Case Creation
            ├── Test Data Preparation
            └── Test Execution

```

### 40.2. Structure B

```text

            Development
            │
            ├── Coding
            └── Testing

```

Neither structure is universally correct.

The appropriate granularity depends on whether each level represents a meaningful semantic distinction.

Classification should avoid unnecessary Classification Inflation while providing sufficient semantic precision.

---

### 40.1. Structure A

```text

            Development
            │
```

The appropriate granularity depends on whether each level represents a meaningful semantic distinction.

Classification should avoid unnecessary Classification Inflation while providing sufficient semantic precision.

Consider:

```text

            Architecture
            │
            └── Architecture Document
                │
                └── Architecture Document Version
                    │
                    └── Architecture Document Version 1

```

If these elements do not represent distinct semantic concepts, the hierarchy is unnecessarily deep.

The additional elements introduce structural complexity without providing meaningful semantic information.

A more meaningful structure could be:

```text

            Architecture
            │
            ├── Architectural Principles
            ├── Architectural Concepts
            ├── System Architecture
            └── Deployment Architecture

```

Each specialization can represent a distinct semantic category.

# 43. Example 39 — Classification Relationship to Knowledge

Classification can contribute semantic information to a broader knowledge structure.

For example:

```text

            Document
            │
            ├── classified-as  ─────►  Architecture
            │
            └── references  ─────►  System Design

```

Classification provides categorization.

The broader relationship structure can represent additional semantic connections.

The responsibilities remain distinct.

---

# 44. Example 40 — Classification and Automation

An automation process may validate a collection of documents:

```text
                Documents
                    │
                    ▼

        Classification Validation
        │
        ├── Valid
        ├── Invalid Element
        ├── Invalid Relationship
        └── Constraint Violation

```

The automation performs validation.

It does not redefine the Classification model.

The rules remain defined by the Classification architecture and specification.

A simplified complete example may be represented as:

```text

            │
```

- the element is active;
- the assignment is permitted by the Schema;

# 46. Example 42 — Complete Classification with Relationships

```text
                │

                                        │
                                        ├── Coding
                                        └── Testing
```

The hierarchy and the `related-to` relationship have different semantics.

The hierarchy represents specialization.

The relationship represents association.

The examples in this document can be summarized by the following principle:

> Classification examples should demonstrate semantic organization without becoming an alternative source of architectural rules.

Examples should make the Classification architecture easier to understand, apply and verify.

When creating additional Classification examples:

1. Use terminology defined by the Classification Dictionary.

# 10. Architectural Principles

The Metadata component shall conform to the following principles.

## 10.1. Technology Independence

Metadata shall not depend on implementation technologies.

---

## 10.2. Content Independence

Metadata shall remain independent of document content.

---

## 10.3. Repository Independence

Metadata shall not depend on repository organization.

---

## 10.4. Storage Independence

Metadata shall not depend on storage technologies.

---

## 10.5. Format Independence

Metadata shall not depend on document formats.

---

## 10.6. Explicit Semantics

Every Metadata element shall possess a single, well-defined meaning.

---

## 10.7. Single Source of Truth

Each Metadata concept shall possess one authoritative definition.

---

## 10.8. Extensibility

The Metadata architecture shall support future Metadata extensions without compromising existing Metadata definitions.

---

## 10.9. Backward Compatibility

Metadata evolution shall preserve compatibility with previously established Metadata whenever possible.

---

# 11. Architectural Constraints

The Metadata component shall satisfy the following architectural constraints.

- Metadata shall remain independent of implementation.
- Metadata shall remain independent of programming languages.
- Metadata shall remain independent of tooling.
- Metadata shall remain independent of repositories.
- Metadata shall remain independent of storage mechanisms.
- Metadata shall remain independent of serialization formats.
- Metadata shall not duplicate responsibilities belonging to other architectural components.

---

# 12. Relationship with Other Components

Metadata collaborates with other components while preserving strict responsibility boundaries.

| Component | Relationship |
|-----------|--------------|
| Document Identity | Consumes Metadata to describe document identity. |
| Classification | Consumes Metadata to organize documents. |
| Templates | Define how Metadata is represented in documents. |
| Workflow | Consumes Metadata during lifecycle management. |
| Policies | Uses Metadata for governance decisions. |
| Baselines | Preserve Metadata across framework evolution. |
| Registry | Indexes Metadata for document discovery. |
| Relationships | Connect Metadata across architectural entities. |
| Knowledge Graph | Uses Metadata as semantic nodes and properties. |
| Validation | Verifies Metadata compliance. |
| Automation | Produces and consumes Metadata during automated processes. |

---

# 13. Architectural Evolution

The Metadata component evolves incrementally according to the Metadata Roadmap.

Its evolution follows the progression:

1. Core Metadata
2. Structural Metadata
3. Lifecycle Metadata
4. Governance Metadata
5. Traceability Metadata
6. Discovery Metadata
7. Automation Metadata

Each stage extends the Metadata architecture without redefining previously established concepts.

---

# 4. Scope

The component's scope includes identity concepts, models, elements/schema, constraints, identity lifecycle, validation, governance, typed relationships, assessed extensibility, specifications and examples. Detailed sources retain their responsibilities; this architecture does not invent a canonical merged field catalog or certify all peer requirements.

For applicable normalized documents, logical identity remains associated with the same document across ordinary content/descriptor, classification, representation, repository and document-edition changes. Exact edition coordinates, document Status, identity-record assignment/preservation/retirement evidence, maturity and Baseline membership are separate facts. A mutable state record is not a replacement for the stable identity key.

Unassigned concerns a pre-allocation subject, not an already assigned Domain+Identifier key. Retirement preserves allocated-number reservation, document association/history and reference interpretation; it does not guarantee a running resolver or retrievable content. Document lifecycle and identity-record lifecycle can have distinct subjects/contracts. The source does not prescribe a universal transition or permission graph.

DID-003/004/005/006/010/014 currently disagree on reference cardinality, mandatory State/Canonical Reference fields and identity state terminology. Those actual claims are preserved in §12.3 for full owner cycles. The architectural distinctions here neither merge incompatible schemas nor silently remove/add their mandatory fields. No Metadata Dictionary Element, Profile or canonical state record is fabricated.

---

# 5. Out of Scope

The following roles are separate from document identity semantic ownership. Area labels, registered capability contracts and operational executors are identified separately; naming an owner proves no implemented service.

| Received responsibility | Responsible contract/role | Operational or semantic boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Document metadata | Metadata plus applicable semantic domain owners | Dictionary defines, Schema organizes, Profile constrains and Instance supplies values under one effective Profile; descriptive representation does not replace identity |
| Document classification | Classification | Family/Type and other category meanings remain mutable and separately owned |
| Registry management | Registry | Catalog/lookup contracts and provenance; actual registration/lookup executed by an applicable system/process |
| Discovery services | Discovery area: Registry, Relationships, Knowledge Graph, Navigation, Search | Area groups capabilities; it is not another component or mandatory routing intermediary |
| Workflow management | Workflow and applicable Policies | Subject-specific transitions/rules; DMS/tool/manual operation, not an implemented DF workflow engine |
| Version control | Documentary edition contracts versus source-control systems/adapters | Version/Revision/Status semantics follow applicable governance/edition contracts; repository commits and Source Control Integration adapters do not define them |
| Repository management | DMS or other applicable external system | Organization, storage, permissions and physical-location execution |
| Storage technologies | Applicable implementations/external systems | Persistence mechanisms preserve applicable representation/provenance requirements |
| Identifier generation algorithms | Applicable allocation executor | Generate/allocate under identity-domain rules and collision/reservation evidence; no algorithm supplied here |
| Persistence mechanisms | Applicable implementation/external system | Store identity/edition/context records without acquiring identity semantics |

Governance is an area grouping Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines; it is not a single invented component owning all operational management. Reviews records examined scope/results; Baselines defines immutable selected exact approved editions and context. CMS change evidence does not substitute for documentary approval or snapshot inclusion.

---

# 7. Core Architectural Characteristics

Within its declared allocation/preservation contract, an assigned logical identity shall be unique for the document in its domain, stable through normal evolution, and never reassigned to a different document. Domain qualification is required to interpret uniqueness; an identifier string alone is not universally unique across unregistered domains.

Immutability concerns the assigned Domain+Identifier key under its applicable contract, not every mutable record about that identity. Identity-state evidence, references, location, descriptors and exact-edition coordinates can evolve under their own owner rules without automatically replacing the key. References and aliases interpret an existing logical document; they do not license another document to reuse its identity. Allocated and retired identities remain reserved.

Preserve valid assigned identity during ordinary classification, repository, format, lifecycle and edition changes. If a necessary authorized schema/ID migration would change an otherwise immutable representation/allocation contract, first assess and explicitly reconcile the governing previous/new rules with responsible identity/domain sources. Record old→new mappings, same-document continuity, aliases/reservations, collisions, historical/reference/context effects, exact source editions, affected consumers and transition verification before coordinated application. Preserve original representations and historical immutable snapshot selections; never retarget old members or reassign retired allocations to another document. No blanket permission for arbitrary identity changes or two contradictory governing rules for one operation is introduced. This localized UPDATE performs no migration.

Long-term understandable/referenceable identity is a requirement and design objective supported by qualified domain/canonicalization and actual preservation/resolution evidence. It guarantees neither universally understood bare strings nor future content availability. Exact-edition references additionally identify the intended Version/Revision and relevant bytes/context; logical identity alone selects neither an exact edition nor Baseline membership.

---

# 9. Component Relationships

The following are scoped architectural contract declarations for documentary uses. They do not establish an operational service call, every-component routing requirement or complete dependency graph.

| Consumer | Provider | Required contract/use | Source/scope boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metadata | Document Identity | Identity of the normalized document described | DID-009 §5.1 declaration; descriptive values retain their own semantic owners |
| Classification | Document Identity | Identity of the normalized document being classified | DID-009 §5.2; category/definition entity identity is a separate qualified contract |
| Templates | Document Identity | Identity of normalized Template documentation/document instances | DID-009 §5.3; Template definition/instance keys are not automatically DF document IDs |
| Registry | Document Identity | Logical document identity for a document catalog entry | DID-001 §9.4; source-edition provenance and exact lookup context required |
| Relationships | Document Identity | Identity of document endpoints | DID-001 §9.5; other endpoint kinds use their own domain contracts |
| Knowledge Graph | Document Identity | Logical document node identity | ARC-005 §12; typed edges remain Relationships records, not document identities |
| Baselines | Document Identity | Logical member identity | ARC-005 §12; exact edition/descriptive/context evidence additionally required |
| Workflow | Document Identity | Identified normalized document subject | DID-009 §6.1; applicable transition execution remains with the actual process |

## 9.1. Metadata

Identity identifies the logical document; Metadata defines/represents descriptors and owner meanings. Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance roles remain separate under one effective Profile. Identity data can be represented descriptively without transferring identity semantics or creating missing Metadata Element/catalog records.

**Unresolved reciprocal declarations:** supplied README states Document Identity→Metadata for descriptive concepts, while DID-009 §§5/10 states Metadata→Document Identity and no dependency on consuming components. Both source claims remain visible as required-dependency evidence pending owner/context/interface reconciliation. Distinguish core identity meaning from identity-record descriptor use, but do not silently downgrade a genuinely required contract into navigation or declare the apparent cycle resolved. Different stated uses alone do not prove operational independence or global acyclicity. Full Metadata/DID source cycles must establish the actual required scopes and cycle treatment under ARC-004.

## 9.2. Classification

Classification owns category meanings and uses identity when categorizing a normalized document. Current Family/Type/Component labels are independent from stable allocation series and do not automatically reconstruct an assigned valid ID. Classification definitions and their own lifecycle/keys are different subjects from document editions; their actual identity contracts need qualification. Nominal CLS-003/CLS-001 collision reconciliation remains scheduled, not corrected by this source.

## 9.3. Templates

Templates owns reusable documentary structures and definition/instance contracts. A normalized document describing or applying a Template can require document identity; Template entities and graph/relationship identifiers are not thereby allocated normalized document IDs. Templates consumes appropriate owner meanings without redefining document identity, Metadata or Classification. Source presence and using a Template prove neither consistency nor approved publication.

## 9.4. Registry

Registry catalogs/looks up identified documentary entities or editions under declared provenance and freshness/current-historical-snapshot context. It does not redefine identity. A document lookup needs its domain/canonical key; an exact-edition lookup additionally needs edition/context evidence. No universal Registry intermediary, implemented resolver or persistent content availability is implied.

## 9.5. Relationships

Relationships owns typed connection records and provenance; Document Identity owns the contract for document endpoints. Other endpoint kinds use their own qualified identity domains. Canonical document reference validity requires the intended document/edition context and actual evidence; logical reference preservation does not imply live-content retrieval. Required edges remain required even when their data comes through a projection; a reference label cannot conceal a genuine cycle.

## 9.6. Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph projects identified entities and Relationships records with source/edition provenance and refresh limits. Document nodes use document identity; graph edges or non-document entities need appropriate other contracts. Projections do not create competing identity/relationship authority or certify complete network correctness. No Registry→Graph→Baseline execution chain is prescribed.

## 9.7. Governance

Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines define documentary transition, decision, review and snapshot requirements; actual operation remains with DMS/tool/manual processes and CMS change scope. Identity-record lifecycle, document Status/Version/Revision, maturity, review, validation, approval, publication and membership are distinct. A state list alone is neither a universal permission graph nor an implemented workflow.

Baselines selects an explicitly identified immutable set of exact approved document editions with relevant pinned relationship context or traceable verification evidence. Identity alone cannot select an exact member; eligibility, consistency and actual inclusion remain separate checks. Draft successors neither inherit membership nor retarget older snapshots. Retired identities preserve reservations/history without implying current document publication or resolver availability.

## 4.2. Identifier



### 4.2.1. Purpose

Identifier is the canonical representation of assigned identity under its governing domain/canonicalization rules. The logical document, qualified key, rendered string and any permitted alias are distinct. Alternative representations must identify the intended existing key; they do not license another document to reuse it.

For this corpus, the domain is **Documentation Framework**, represented by **DF**. The adopted identifier convention is **DF-SSS-NNN**, where SSS is a registered uppercase three-letter stable allocation series and NNN is a positive three-digit allocation001–999. Full qualified identifiers, not numeric suffixes alone, determine collisions. The series records its allocation origin; current Family, Type, Component, path, Version/Revision and Status do not regenerate an assigned ID.

000 is not allocated and is not a README code. Gaps do not prove availability; allocated and retired numbers remain reserved. Allocation requires explicit series records and checks of relevant current/historical/reserved identities and references. At999, register an unused three-letter continuation series with traceability; do not widen syntax or recycle silently. Policy§4 and DID-001/003/004 establish these corpus rules. This schema integrates their scoped representation; other domains require explicit rules and no new allocation or migration occurs here.

Canonical interpretation states the responsible domain/rules and intended existing target. Alias/canonicalization handling must be explicit and preserve historical interpretation. Neither this format nor a syntax match proves allocation, uniqueness, a running resolver or retrieval availability.

---

### 4.2.2. Cardinality

```text
Exactly one
```

One canonical identifier representation per applicable assigned identity. Domain qualification remains required. Multiple aliases or physical representations do not create multiple logical document identities or erase the canonical interpretation requirement.

---

### 4.2.3. Characteristics

- **Mandatory:** a canonical identifier represents the applicable assigned identity.
- **Unique:** the qualified Domain+Identifier shall identify the intended document; actual collision/reservation coverage is recorded separately.
- **Immutable:** ordinary content/classification/status/edition/repository changes preserve the assigned key under its governing contract.
- **Permanent:** preserve same-document association and allocated/retired reservations; never reassign to another document.

Deterministic interpretation is a governed representation requirement, not proof of an implemented generator/resolver. Necessary contract/migration changes require the prior/new assessment in §11 rather than silent reallocation.

---

# 6. Logical Relationships

The second view preserves the same three subjects as the received relationship diagram. It qualifies direction, authority and subject; it is not a mandatory object layout, operational call chain or required-dependency graph.

<!-- original-section-view: 6 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §6 — Logical relationships and owner boundaries.**

| From | Relation kind | To | Meaning / boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Assigned Document Identity | belongs within | Identity Domain | One governing allocation/preservation scope |
| Assigned Document Identity | is represented through | Identifier | One canonical interpretation under domain rules |
| Identity Reference | targets | Intended Document Identity / exact edition | Incoming0..N population; connection records remain with their relationship owner |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

Minimal key/association scope is distinct from the complete subject claimed by other specifications. The following records actual peer requirements; it neither deletes mandatory peer fields nor invents an accepted merged record/state machine.

| Subject | This source's retained view | Actual responsible peer clauses | Remaining integration obligation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Domain / Identifier | Assigned governing qualification and canonical representation | DID-003 §§4–6; DID-004 §§4/7; DID-014 §§7–8 mandatory Domain/Identifier | Preserve qualified key and explicitly governed corpus representation/other domains |
| Identity References | Optional incoming associations0..N | DID-003 §§5.4/6; DID-004 §§4.5/7.5 | Connection ownership,typed target and exact-edition evidence; not a mandatory key field |
| Identity State / Lifecycle State | Not introduced as a merged key field by this source | DID-014 §§7–8 mandates State/Lifecycle State; DID-006 §§4–8 defines Unassigned/Assigned/Preserved/Retired for its lifecycle subject | Reconcile field/record subject,authority,vocabulary and transitions with owners; no implicit removal or universal-state approval |
| Canonical Reference | Not equated with optional plural Identity References | DID-014 §§7–8 makes Canonical Reference mandatory | Reconcile representation/field versus association meaning and mandatory scope; omission from this selected view does not waive the peer requirement |

DID-004 retains Active/Archived/Deprecated as historical candidate terminology; these are not automatically equivalent to DID-006 lifecycle states or document-edition Draft/Review/Approved/Published/Archived status. Unassigned concerns pre-allocation, not an already assigned key. State,Status,exact edition,maturity,approval and Baseline membership require their proper subject/owner evidence. This source-local schema correction does not complete DID-006/014 cycles,authorize disregarding mandatory claims or certify integrated conformity. Contradictory complete-record claims require a coordinated owner decision before claiming a fully reconciled implementation contract.

---

# 8. Schema Constraints

The following requirements concern the stated assigned key and incoming-association subjects. Requirement text is not execution evidence. Record responsible contracts/editions,artifacts/domain/context,executor,coverage,observations and unresolved conditions for any claimed check.

---

## 8.1. Identity Domain

- A governing domain shall qualify every applicable assigned key; pre-allocation subjects and excluded functional files differ.
- Ordinary evolution preserves the assigned domain/key association under its governing contract.
- Domain qualification,owner,rules and namespace/collision/reservation coverage shall be explicit; a domain declaration does not prove actual uniqueness.
- A necessary migration affecting the governing contract requires §11 prior/new reconciliation and continuity checks before application; no silent domain reassignment is authorized.

---

## 8.2. Identifier

- Each applicable assigned identity has one canonical identifier representation under its domain rules.
- Full qualified key uniqueness requires actual allocation/collision/reservation evidence; matching syntax alone does not prove it.
- Assigned identifiers remain stable across ordinary classification,content,edition,location and document-status changes; current Family/Type does not reconstruct allocation series.
- Allocated and retired identifiers shall never be reassigned to another document. Preserve old representations,reservations and historical references/snapshot selections through any necessary governed transition.
- Apply §4.2 corpus syntax and canonicalization scope; no new series,identifier,alias or migration is created by this UPDATE.

---

## 8.3. Identity References

- A valid document-targeting reference identifies its intended existing qualified document or exact edition/context; other endpoint kinds follow their own contracts.
- Incoming population remains optional0..N; an identity does not need an incoming reference merely to exist.
- References never allocate or redefine their target and remain external to the identifier.
- Connection records retain their relationship owner and provenance; mutations do not automatically change the target key.
- Record dangling,ambiguous,stale or unavailable references as actual observations; preserve historical interpretation and never silently retarget. Identity stability alone guarantees no live-content retrieval or universal future reference validity.

---

# 11. Extensibility

Schema evolution shall preserve same-document assignment,non-reuse and compatible meaning where feasible. Additional roles may be introduced only through an explicit responsible contract and impact assessment,not by treating a picture or Metadata representation as an automatically registered field.

Before a necessary normative change or path/identity migration:

1. Identify the prior/new governing rules,source editions,rationale,affected owners/consumers and actual required dependencies.
2. Assess compatibility,mandatory-field/State/Canonical Reference effects,record populations,canonical representation/aliases and reference targets; retain unresolved peer claims visibly.
3. Record exact old→new mappings,collision/reservation/history checks,same-document continuity and relevant exact-edition/snapshot contexts. Preserve old evidence and never retarget immutable historical snapshot members or reassign retired IDs.
4. Establish transition verification and coordinated propagation before claiming integrated conformance. A local source update does not approve peers or execute migration.

For changed working document editions,compatible correction retains Version,compatible additive capability increments minor,incompatible contract change increments major and resets minor to0. Each persisted changed edition increments Revision monotonically across Versions. Unchanged-source validation changes neither coordinate and is recorded centrally. Those documentary coordinates do not define all other entities' allocation/lifecycle.

DID-014 §14's received additive/backward-compatible-only extension rule remains a real peer contract requiring scheduled reconciliation with the controlled-evolution approach;it is not silently waived by this source. No blanket permission to mutate assigned identity is introduced. This UPDATE executes no allocation,series registration,alias or migration.

---
