### 5.1.1. Dependency

Metadata→Document Identity remains the required declaration for identification of the applicable assigned normalized document described.

The functional DID README also states: “The Document Identity component depends on the Metadata component for the canonical definition of metadata concepts used to describe document identity.” Retain Document Identity→Metadata as an actual reciprocal required claim, not optional navigation. The exact README bytes/edition evidence and comparison source hashes are in the REVIEW/UPDATE map.

Responsible owners must reconcile which indispensable concepts/interfaces are required by identity core versus descriptive records, their exact governing editions and actual use. Different scope names alone do not dissolve a real required cycle. This UPDATE corrects the blanket denial of consumer dependencies; it does not certify that these reciprocal requirements are independent or globally reconciled.

---

## 5.2. Classification

Classification owns category meaning, distinct from the key of a classified normalized document.

---

### 5.2.1. Dependency

Classification→Document Identity is the required document-identification contract for an applicable assigned normalized document receiving classification. It is not a requirement that each category/definition/assignment entity has a DF document key.

---

### 5.2.2. Purpose

Classification categorizes the intended document under its own contracts. Family/Type/Component changes do not regenerate the stable allocated series/key. A category entity's identity and a normalized document describing that category are different subjects. Classification does not redefine document-key meaning.

---

# 7. Relationships with Discovery Components

The five original Discovery responsibilities remain separate from identity allocation and actual runtime delivery. Logical contracts may constrain projections and interfaces; actual availability, freshness and results need observations.

---

## 7.1. Registry

Registry→Document Identity is the required identification contract for document registrations. Registry owns registration/index records; Document Identity owns the underlying document-key meaning. Registry→Metadata is a selected descriptor contract in ARC-005§12. Repeated records/copies do not alone prove duplicate allocation. Record exact source editions, intended target/context, provenance and freshness. Registration is not allocation, approval or a mandatory intermediary for every consumer.

---

## 7.2. Relationships

Relationships owns connection type, direction, endpoints and connection records. For a document endpoint use the intended qualified document or exact edition/context under §4.4; other typed endpoints follow their own contracts. No rule here forces all possible associations to be document-to-document. Mutable connections do not redefine the key, and canonical endpoints alone do not prove a valid connection or permanently available target.

---

## 7.3. Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph owns logical node/edge projection and representation contracts; storage/runtime technologies remain implementation choices. Knowledge Graph→Document Identity for document-node meaning and Knowledge Graph→Relationships for typed connections are selected required contracts in ARC-005§12. Neither is eliminated by calling the graph a projection.

Keep authoritative keys/connection sources distinct from projected records/properties. Nodes and properties may change while preserving intended qualified identity. Retain source edition/context, derivation, provenance, freshness and observed limitations. Projection does not allocate a new document identity, acquire connection authority or prove every peer representation is synchronized.

---

## 7.4. Navigation

Navigation uses intended identity and context to locate an applicable document or edition under its navigation contract. It can derive links and presentation records while preserving authoritative target meaning; the received prohibition on creating identity information means no competing allocation/semantic invention, not a ban on derived representation. Navigation does not guarantee successful current retrieval, require a universal Registry route or authorize silent retargeting.

---

## 7.5. Search

Search→Document Identity is the required identification contract for document-targeting search results. Other indexed entities retain their own endpoint contracts. Search owns query/result behavior, not document-key meaning. Record actual indexed source editions/context, target interpretation, freshness and result/retrieval observations. An index match does not prove allocation, complete population coverage, full identity validity or future availability.

---

# 10. Dependency Overview

The received overview mixed semantic provision, component collaboration and area order. Replace its untyped arrows with this typed view while preserving all nine original labels. It is not a mandatory serial pipeline.

<!-- original-section-view: 10 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §10 — Scoped dependency and collaboration overview.**

| Original subject | Kind / relation to Document Identity | Direction / boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Document Identity | Semantic owner/provider and actual declared consumer | Provides document-key meaning; reciprocal Metadata requirement remains unresolved |
| Metadata | Descriptor owner / required consumer and provider claims | Metadata→Document Identity (§5.1.1); Document Identity→Metadata (functional README) |
| Classification | Category owner / required document-key consumer | Classification→Document Identity for applicable classified document (§5.2.1) |
| Registry | Registration owner / required document-key consumer | Registry→Document Identity for document registrations (§7.1) |
| Relationships | Connection owner / document endpoint consumption | Relationship semantics remain with Relationships; intended document endpoints use identity contracts (§7.2) |
| Knowledge Graph | Logical projection owner / required document-node consumer | Knowledge Graph→Document Identity; typed connections also require Relationships (§7.3) |
| Governance | Area: Workflow, Policies, Reviews, Baselines | Documentary state/rule/review/exact-snapshot contracts, not one component or an executor (§6) |
| Automation | Area: five registered components | Applicable checking/generation/verification contracts, not obligatory routing (§8) |
| Integration | Area: five registered components | Actual scoped exchange/adapter contracts, not an obligatory final stage (§9) |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

Required dependency direction is consumer→provider. Foundation, Architecture, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Automation and Integration form the architectural support order under ARC-004/005; they are not a universal serial chain. Same-Layer required contracts need explicit scope/interfaces and no required cycles. Semantic ownership, documentary reference, projection, data flow and operational execution are different relations.

Selected actual requirements also include Registry→Metadata (descriptors), Knowledge Graph→Relationships (typed connections), Workflow→Metadata (state/edition), Workflow→Policies (rules), Baselines→Document Identity (logical member) and Baselines→Metadata (exact edition/pinned context), under ARC-004§§12–13 and ARC-005§12/selected component clauses. These are selected declarations, not a complete graph or supplied implementation interfaces.

The former blanket claim “Document Identity has no dependency on the consuming components” is not accepted as the current general rule: the actual README declares the reciprocal Metadata requirement. Preserve both claims and exact source evidence; responsible owner/interface reconciliation is pending. Core-versus-descriptor naming, changing relation labels or omitting an indispensable edge does not prove acyclicity. No global DAG certification follows from this source-local correction. Received view text/digest remains external evidence at this original section.

# 1. Purpose

This is the working normative specification of Document Identity for its explicitly declared documentary/domain subjects and applicable owner contracts. It consolidates scoped requirements and source roles without replacing every detailed owner definition or claiming an implemented, approved or globally reconciled component.

Two conformance subjects are distinguished. **K — assigned document key** is the governing qualified Domain+Identifier and its same-logical-document association. **R — supporting assigned identity record** represents that assigned subject with the five mandatory roles in §7, including a responsible lifecycle assertion and canonical-target descriptor. K is not a container of every mutable record or connection; R is not a new allocated document identity. Pre-allocation is a separate subject, not an assigned R whose key is absent.

This edition makes an explicit local normative decision about the previously unqualified mandatory-record and evolution clauses; the prior/new map and exact affected peer editions are retained externally and in §§7/14/20. It does not silently delete received State/Canonical Reference requirements or equate them with optional incoming relationships. Detailed serialization, canonical Metadata Element/Profile registration and complete owner/consumer propagation are not fabricated.

Normative authority follows actual applicable source declarations, subject/context and common Architecture/Policy, not Type Reference, a title, citation or received Canonical naming. DID-012 remains non-normative advice; current DID-011 architectural/evolution requirements and DID-013 qualified definitions have their own applicable roles (§§15/17). A local source correction or validation is distinct from implemented conformity, formal approval, publication and exact Baseline inclusion.

---

# 7. Canonical Elements

The five received rows remain mandatory for a **complete supporting assigned identity record R** claimed under this V2.0 R1 working specification. This is an explicit correction of the received unqualified every-identity composition: it separates the logical assigned key K from supporting record/assertion/descriptor roles. It does not make State or Canonical Reference optional to pass a complete-R claim, nor add them as immutable coordinates of K.

| Element | Qualified description / subject | Mandatory for complete assigned R |
|---|---|---|
| Document Identity | Intended assigned logical document K and same-document association represented by this record; not a second allocated identity or required recursive object field | Yes |
| Identifier | Canonical identifier interpretation/representation qualifying the intended K under responsible rules | Yes |
| Identity Domain | Governing semantic/allocation/preservation scope qualifying K | Yes |
| Identity State | Supporting actual lifecycle assertion for the assigned subject, mapped to Lifecycle State in §8 with responsible event/decision/source evidence | Yes |
| Canonical Reference | Supporting descriptor identifying the intended canonical qualified document target, or declared exact edition with required coordinates/bytes/context; it may reuse governed key rendering without an additional runtime locator | Yes |

**State role.** Identity State and Lifecycle State are controlled names for the same R assertion role here, not universal aliases for Metadata State or document Status. In assigned-R scope, Assigned, Preserved or Retired is interpreted under actual DID-006 subject/event/decision rules and its selected eight-transition contract. Unassigned denotes pre-allocation and is not an assigned R with a nonexistent K. No global permission graph or undocumented edge is granted. Supporting assertion records can change while K remains stable.

**Canonical-target role.** Canonical Reference states the intended target/interpretation and applicable source/context evidence; it is not a promised permanently available URL or a new independent identity allocation. It can concern K as a logical document, or an explicitly selected edition with additional context. A complete R needs this descriptor role, but it does not require an incoming Relationships record: external incoming document-reference population remains0..N under DID-003/005. Descriptor presence, connection validity and observed retrieval are separate checks; a historical intended target can remain interpretable while live content is unavailable. Never silently create/retarget K or immutable snapshot members.

A consumer checking only K can report that narrower coverage; it cannot call a missing-State/Canonical-Reference record a fully conformant R or infer full implementation conformance. Conversely, a pre-allocation or non-document subject is not an invalid assigned R merely because it is outside that declared claim. Full conformance needs explicit applicable subject/rule inventory (§§15/18), actual checks and unresolved-authority limits.

No implementation claiming complete R may remove an applicable mandatory role. These are logical record responsibilities, not a newly registered Metadata Element/Profile, prescribed serialization, actual populated record or approved merged implementation schema. The current working contract uses existing DID-006 assertion and DID-009/013 document-target meanings; it does not manufacture missing canonical catalogs or imply peer rollout.

**Prior/new authority and affected sources.** V1.0 R0 §§6–8 declared universal composition/mandatory State/Canonical Reference without these subjects. V2.0 R1 retains all five Yes requirements but qualifies complete assigned-R scope, Identity State↔Lifecycle State and canonical descriptor versus incoming association. DID-003/004/005/006/013 and affected consumers require comparison/propagation at their exact recorded editions. DID-005§6's selected key/association view is not silently overwritten or a waiver of R obligations. Their prior references and unresolved-field notes remain historical/current source evidence until a separately traced update qualifies them. This local decision is explicit; full owner-source agreement, canonical field registration and implementation transition are not certified.

---

# 12. Relationship Specification

All nine received subjects remain with actual semantic/record and area/component roles. Required dependencies mean consumer→provider with explicit contract/scope, source editions and interfaces; documentary authority reference, semantic association, projection, navigation and execution are different relations.

| Original subject | Kind | Qualified relationship / owner boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Metadata | Component | Descriptor/model/schema/profile/instance owner; Metadata→Document Identity for identity of the applicable normalized document described; reciprocal requirement below remains |
| Classification | Component | Category/assignment owner; applicable classified-document key consumption does not allocate DF IDs to every category/entity |
| Templates | Component | Template definition/instance contracts; applicable normalized Template-document key consumption differs from every template entity/output |
| Registry | Component | Registration/index owner; intended qualified key/edition/context and source/freshness evidence; registration is not allocation or a mandatory intermediary |
| Relationships | Component | Typed connection/endpoint/provenance owner; document endpoints consume identity meanings, other endpoint kinds retain theirs |
| Knowledge Graph | Component | Logical node/edge projection/properties with authoritative identity/connection source/context and refresh limits; no competing authority or complete graph proof |
| Governance | Area | Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines documentary contracts; actual management/decision executor and CMS scope separate |
| Automation | Area | Validation, Metadata Generator, Registry Generator, Documentation Generator and Consistency Verification capabilities; actual input/output/rule/observation/executor evidence |
| Integration | Area | Source Control Integration, CI/CD Integration, IDE Integration, Documentation Platform Integration and AI Integration optional adapters; actual authorization/mappings/contributors/checks required |

The functional DID README states: “The Document Identity component depends on the Metadata component for the canonical definition of metadata concepts used to describe document identity.” Current DID-009§5.1.1/§10 retains Document Identity→Metadata alongside Metadata→Document Identity. Preserve both actual required declarations pending responsible core-versus-descriptor/interface/source-edition reconciliation. Different scope names, projection or navigation relabelling do not dissolve a genuine required cycle.

The received all-relationships-unidirectional-towards-Identity claim is replaced, not accepted as the current general rule. Ownership/authority and typed association are not required edges; actual indispensable providers remain required even through projections. Apply ARC-004/005 support order and same-Layer explicit-interface/cycle rules; these do not require every earlier provider or a serial pipeline. No complete globally acyclic graph or integrated consumer compatibility is certified. Repeated descriptors, aliases, copies/editions and projection records are not alone duplicate allocations or semantic ownership transfer.

---

# 14. Extensibility Specification

**Current V2.0 R1 decision.** Ordinary compatible implementation extensions preserve applicable owner meanings, mandatory requirements and assigned same-document continuity. Necessary normative/foundational/responsibility/interface revision is permitted only through actual assessed common Architecture AP-015–018 and responsible change authority; it is not falsely labelled compatible merely because it is called an extension.

All five received extension subjects remain:

| Original condition | Current qualified application |
|---|---|
| preserve backward compatibility | Preserve compatible meaning where feasible for ordinary extension; necessary incompatibility requires explicit actual prior/new authority/rationale/consumer and transition evidence |
| preserve canonical identity semantics | Ordinary implementations do not silently replace owner meaning; necessary normative revision is separately assessed, not an arbitrary key reassignment |
| preserve interoperability | Evaluate actual provider/consumer/adapter/source editions and transition checks; no completed global rollout inferred |
| preserve mandatory constraints | Ordinary additions do not waive applicable requirements; necessary normative changes explicitly identify old/new mandates, authority, compatibility and affected exact sources before propagation |
| remain additive | Prefer additive compatible change when it meets the actual need; not an absolute prohibition on necessary justified normative revision |

**Received restriction and affected sources.** V1.0 R0 required every extension to be additive/backward-compatible and stated “Core identity semantics are not extensible.” That exact prior claim remains in original/map/diff/history evidence. This V2.0 R1 replaces this specification's absolute extension-only prohibition with the scoped ordinary-extension/necessary-revision contract above under common architecture. It does not leave the old absolute clause simultaneously governing the same current operation, silently rewrite the past or grant arbitrary mutation of an assigned K.

DID-005§11, DID-010§12, DID-011§§4.2/9 and DID-013§9 currently cite that received restrictive claim or its unresolved authority. Their exact current bytes/editions/hashes are in the affected-source map. They are not edited or automatically revalidated here; their prior-source references and pending notes must be qualified through a separately traced propagation step before claiming integrated agreement. Other K/R field/interface and consumer decisions likewise need actual reconciliation. The current local decision and remaining propagation are separate facts.

For any necessary term/mandate/owner/normative/domain/path/representation transition:

1. Preserve original exact artifacts, rules/editions, actual observations and failed checks. Identify prior/new meaning or mandate, actual responsible authority, intended subject/domain/context, need, alternatives and rationale.
2. Assess exact semantic/record owners, consumers and indispensable consumer→provider interfaces, mandatory field/state/reference/lifecycle effects and actual reciprocal/cycle claims. Resolve governing authority for the actual operation before asserting broader conformity; do not rename away a real required edge.
3. Record compatibility and exact old→new role/term/key/alias mappings, domain qualification, collisions/reservations/history, same-document continuity and intended reference/exact-edition/pinned-snapshot effects. Never reassign allocated/retired K to another document or silently retarget immutable historical members.
4. Apply only the separately authorized scoped change with actual contributor/event provenance, coordinated transition evidence and working edition/history. Compatible correction retains Version; compatible additive capability increments minor; incompatible contract/convention change increments major and resets minor to0. Every persisted changed document edition increments Revision monotonically across Versions; other entity allocation/lifecycle contracts remain separate.
5. Validate resulting exact artifacts/editions in the subsequent appropriate operation, recording actual checks/executor/observations/coverage/remaining peer work. Unchanged-source validation increments neither source coordinate; later changed bytes need their own assessment. Preserve earlier pending/failed events rather than rewriting them as historical success.

This UPDATE changes documentary requirements only. It executes no identity/domain migration, owner transfer, allocation, retirement, implementation rollout, formal approval, publication or Baseline selection.

# 1. Introduction

This document defines the roadmap strategy adopted by the Documentation Framework.

Rather than describing the architecture itself, this document defines how the framework evolves over time and how future work is organised.

The roadmap establishes a structured view of planned development while preserving the architectural principles defined throughout the Documentation Framework.

---

# 2. Purpose

The purpose of the roadmap is to organise the evolution of the framework in a predictable and maintainable manner.

It provides a common planning structure for all framework components while allowing each component to evolve independently.

The roadmap therefore represents the planning layer of the Documentation Framework.

It is not part of the conceptual architecture.

---

# 3. Relationship with the Layered Architecture

The Documentation Framework is organised as a layered architecture.

Each layer defines a specific architectural responsibility.

The roadmap intentionally mirrors this organisation.

However, an important distinction must be made.

The layered architecture describes:

> **What the framework is.**

The roadmap describes:

> **How the framework will evolve.**

Although both structures share the same organisation, they serve different purposes.

---

# 4. Architectural Separation

The Roadmaps directory intentionally exists outside the numbered architectural layers.

This decision reflects an important architectural principle.

The roadmap is not another framework layer.

Instead, it is a management structure responsible for planning the evolution of every layer.

Conceptually.

```text

                    Architecture
                    │
                    ├── Foundation
                    ├── Architecture
                    ├── Documentation
                    ├── Governance
                    ├── Discovery
                    ├── Automation
                    └── Integration


                    Roadmaps
                    │
                    ├── Foundation Roadmaps
                    ├── Architecture Roadmaps
                    ├── Documentation Roadmaps
                    ├── Governance Roadmaps
                    ├── Discovery Roadmaps
                    ├── Automation Roadmaps
                    └── Integration Roadmaps

```

The roadmap reflects the architecture.

It does not belong to it.

# 1. Introduction

The Classification Roadmap defines the implementation and evolution strategy for the **Classification** component of the Documentation Framework.

Classification provides a structured mechanism for categorizing documents according to their defined characteristics, purposes and architectural roles.

Within the Documentation Framework, Classification establishes a consistent semantic structure for organizing documents without becoming responsible for document identity, metadata management or document content.

---

# 4. Architectural Position

Within the Documentation Framework, Classification belongs to the **Documentation Layer**.

Conceptually:

```text

                         Documentation Layer

                    ┌────────────────────────────┐
                    │ Metadata                   │
                    │ Document Identity          │
                    │ Classification             │
                    │ Templates                  │
                    └────────────────────────────┘

```

Classification provides a semantic organization mechanism for documents.

It remains independent from the physical representation and storage of documents.

## 2. Normalized documents and functional files

Every file named README.md, CHANGELOG.md or ArchitecturalMilestones.md in this corpus is a non-normalized functional file. It retains its name and does not require Document ID, Family, Type, Component, Version, Revision, Status or Baseline by virtue of document normalization. Do not infer a finding from absence of those fields. Do not automatically delete legitimate existing information.

These files remain in inventories, SHA-256 manifests, content reviews and applicable structural, terminology, reference and consistency checks. CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md retain their own entry/milestone IDs, states, dates and historical conventions. Their maintenance is not conditional on normalized document metadata.

The input corpus comprises 79 documents within normalization scope and 8 non-normalized files. Two normalized review documents are introduced by Step 3. Machine-readable exports attached to DF-RVW-002 are representations of its inventories and matrices, not independent normalized documents or new authorities. Each export identifies its parent document and edition in its manifest or accompanying report.

## 3. Classification contract

### 3.1. Uniform Type

Type identifies the primary responsibility of every normalized document and uses exactly one value from {Architecture, Structure, Behavior, Reference}. There are no special Type values for Foundation, Architecture, global roadmaps or review artifacts.

| Type | Primary responsibility |
|---|---|
| Architecture | Foundations, principles, concepts, conceptual models/elements and architectural decisions. |
| Structure | Organization, composition, schemas, structural relationships, restrictions and element catalogs. |
| Behavior | Processes, lifecycle, validation, governance, extensibility and planned evolution. |
| Reference | Consultation, terminology, consolidated specifications, examples, recommendations and historical records. |

Use the spelling Behavior. Base, Core, Schema, Dictionary and Lifecycle are not additional Type values. A historical evolution account is Reference; a process or evolution plan is Behavior. Assess content and primary responsibility rather than filename or directory alone. Normative or informative authority is established by explicit statements/references, never by Type=Reference alone. Validation is not approval.

### 3.2. Family and Component

| Document category | Family | Component |
|---|---|---|
| Belongs to a component | Canonical component name | Same canonical name, when the field is used. |
| Foundation without a component | Foundation | Absent/not applicable. |
| Architecture without a component | Architecture | Absent/not applicable. |
| Global roadmap or global implementation strategy | Roadmap | Absent/not applicable. |
| This review's policy/report | Reviews | Reviews. |

Roadmap is an explicitly scoped documentary planning area for global, non-component plans. It reuses the received Family value in DF-RDM-001/002, not an invented component or Layer. These two documents use Type=Behavior. The existing Component=Documentation Framework in DF-RDM-002 must be assessed and removed from its working header in the scheduled UPDATE: the framework is the container, not a component of itself.

Component roadmaps belong to the component they plan and therefore use Family=component, Type=Behavior and matching Component, regardless of central storage under Roadmaps. Current component names are Metadata, Document Identity, Classification and Templates. DocumentIdentity is a directory alias, not a competing canonical component name.

Do not remove Component indiscriminately. The global roadmap decision is localized and does not remove it from component documents. Family/Type changes do not determine document identity or structural Layer allocation.

### 3.3. Class

Class remains a separate, optional semantic dimension. This policy does not create a complete Class vocabulary or make it mandatory. Retain received values as evidence, then assess each use in its document cycle. A value that merely repeats Type or misstates authority must be reconciled with evidence. New review artifacts omit Class because no additional distinction is needed. Optional does not mean unrestricted: any value used must have an explicit, non-conflicting definition.

## 4. Identity convention for this corpus and review artifacts

### 4.1. Representation and uniqueness

The identity domain is Documentation Framework. Its representation prefix is DF. A working normalized document identifier follows DF-SSS-NNN, where SSS is a registered three-letter uppercase allocation-series code and NNN is a three-digit positive allocation number, 001–999. The full identifier is unique within the domain. Numbers are allocated within a series; equal numeric suffixes across different series are not collisions.

Series codes are stable allocation namespaces, not the document's current Family, Type, component, location, version or revision. Preserve existing valid identifiers when those characteristics change. A series' original purpose is recorded for traceability, but it does not recalculate an existing document ID after reassignment/reclassification.

| Series | Received origin/purpose | Step 3 action |
|---|---|---|
| FND | Foundation documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| ARC | Framework Architecture documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| MTD | Metadata documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| DID | Document Identity documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| CLS | Classification documents | Preserve unambiguous allocations; resolve the nominal CLS-003 collision. |
| TPL | Templates documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| RDM | Planning documents | Preserve allocations even when Family becomes a component name. |
| RVW | Review policy and consolidated review report | Allocate 001 to this policy and 002 to DF-RVW-002 after collision checks. |

This is a corpus convention, not a format imposed on identities in other domains or an identifier-generation implementation. Scheduled reconciliation of DF-DID-005/010/014 owns its integration into the identity contract. Foundation and Classification must qualify the earlier Family/Type-based convention accordingly.

### 4.2. Allocation, reservations and retirement

New allocation requires an explicit series record and collision scan of headers, filenames, references, historical/reserved records and this review's allocation register. Do not reuse allocated/retired numbers. A gap does not prove availability; when allocation history is unavailable, record that limitation and use a documented allocation decision rather than infer a historical reservation. Missing IDs are not assigned to the eight functional files excluded in §2.

000 is not allocated under this working convention; it is not implicitly a README code. RVW-001/002 are the only new allocations at Step 3; no future numbers are reserved. At 999, do not widen the syntax or silently recycle: register another unused three-letter series with traceable continuation and preserve all old IDs. A new domain is a separate semantic decision, not a shortcut for renumbering this corpus.

Maintain an allocation register in DF-RVW-002's exports, including series, number, identifier, path, allocation status and evidence. Retired IDs remain reserved. The source archive and the input manifest preserve received declarations, including invalid ones; preservation is evidence, not acceptance of a collision.

### 4.3. Localized correction and historical syntax

No general ID migration is required by the adopted classification change. The nominal DF-CLS-003-ClassificationModel.md wrongly declares DF-CLS-001 and repeats the Architecture prose. Its correction is pending a distinct document recovery/update and path-scoped map. It is not a global DF-CLS-001→DF-CLS-003 replacement or an alias that makes one identifier resolve to two documents.

Operational references must resolve to the intended final identity/path after a coordinated correction. Historical examples such as META-DCL-001, or earlier roadmap forms containing RDM as an extra segment, must be explicitly qualified where historical or revised where they purport to prescribe the current working convention. Do not rewrite history as if the new convention had always existed.

Metadata Element IDs, document IDs, finding IDs, CHANGELOG numbers and Milestone IDs are separate entities. Creating this policy does not assign Metadata Element IDs or create element lifecycle/publication records.

### 5.1. Received evidence

The 79 in-scope input documents declare Version 1.0 and Baseline 1.0; 73 declare Revision 0 and six Foundation documents do not declare Revision. ### 5.2. Edition successors

Version uses the observed major.minor numeric form. Revision is a monotonic integer per document across version changes during this review.

| Change | Version action | Revision action |

Explain compatibility per UPDATE. Changing a classification label does not automatically change Version; replacing what a classification/schema contract permits may be incompatible even if no IDs change. Assess changes to identity syntax/resolution separately from a filename correction. Do not reset an existing Revision counter on Version changes during this review. Future alternative numbering requires a traceable policy change, not an implied reset.

Each completed persisted working edition with changed content receives its successor. Draft editing before an edition is finalized is preparation, not evidence of completed intermediate editions. If a validated/finalized edition needs a correction, create another successor and retain the failed validation event. No source revision is incremented merely to record this policy's adoption.

### 5.3. Working lifecycle and Baseline

Edited working documents start at Status=Draft, including successors of received Approved/Canonical documents. A subsequent explicit submission may use Review; formal approval/publication requires its own decision/evidence. Leave untouched source statuses unchanged. Canonical in a received header is preserved as historical evidence, not automatically granted to a successor or silently converted into Approved.

A newly created or modified working edition has Baseline=Not assigned unless its exact inclusion is evidenced. Record original Status and Baseline in the edition history and input manifest. Do not change the original Baseline snapshot. Draft is a lifecycle state; Not assigned is an explicit absence marker in the human-readable working header, not a new Baseline identifier.

At Step 3 creation, this policy and DF-RVW-002 were Draft, Version 1.0, Revision 1, Baseline Not assigned. Current working coordinates follow their headers and exact edition histories. Passing their scoped checks does not approve/publish them or place them in a Baseline. The conventions for these working headers do not populate the canonical Metadata Dictionary or create a Metadata Profile lifecycle event by implication.

A user who actually edits document content is recorded as an author when that contribution and identity are established. Permission, instructions, approval or file custody alone do not prove an authored contribution. Their remaining discrepancies are recorded in DF-RVW-002, rather than reported as integrated consistency.

Where received documents conflict with the user's adopted rules, the adopted rules govern the working review. The received rule remains preserved as input/historical evidence and is pending reconciliation; it is not a second governing rule for the same working operation. No completed rollout across existing sources is claimed by creating this policy.

### 7.1. Cumulative documentary authorship

The normalized document header's **Author** field lists all evidenced authors who contributed to the document, including its original author and contributors to later editions. Use **semicolon followed by a space (`; `)** between distinct authors. Preserve established names and role qualifications; retain first evidenced contribution order and do not duplicate an author for each revision. Example: `Arnaldo Figueira; Codex — AI assistant`.

Carry forward evidenced original/prior authors when preparing a successor. Record each later contributor when that contribution is supported by source history, exact edition/diff evidence or explicit reliable attribution. Preserve edition history separately so the cumulative header does not imply that every listed author performed every change. When original authorship is absent or unknown, list only known contributors and retain that limitation; do not guess an author from ownership, filename, user identity or authorization. A later substantiated attribution receives a traceable correction.

A user who actually edits document content is recorded as an author when that contribution and identity are established. Permission, instructions, approval or file custody alone do not prove an authored contribution. Later disk changes must be examined as resulting bytes with attribution evidence; earlier validation results do not automatically apply. The author list is provenance, not a blanket assignment of approval or responsibility for consequences of every later final product.

### 7.2. Event-specific CHANGELOG authorship

The CHANGELOG **Author** column records the evidenced contributors who performed that particular event, using the same `; ` separator when the event has multiple authors. It is not copied automatically from the cumulative document header. Use `Codex — AI assistant` for events performed solely by this assistant; do not attribute the event to the user merely because the user authorized it. Preserve historical event authors rather than retroactively adding every document author to each row.

For each update, record source path/ID, old/new edition, material change, finding, validation state, report/diff link and Milestone in the Description. Append a later validation event rather than rewriting a pending-validation update into a historical success. Do not log future intentions as completed changes.

### 7.3. Milestone scope and history

Preserve M0–M7. Create M8–M14 for the review's verifiable results, with the existing Not Started/In Progress/Completed milestone states and O/S/C record states. A milestone's state derives from its own records for its declared work scope. Completion of a historical implementation milestone is not closure of a new review milestone.

M8 establishes the received corpus, including explicit limitations. M9 establishes this review's policy, artifact identities, central tracking and scoped checks. M10 covers Foundation cycles; M11 Architecture cycles; M12 the four input Documentation components; M13 localized identity/path/reference reconciliation; M14 integrated validation and final delivery. M9 excludes propagation into all domain sources, which is assigned to M10–M13.

No estimated completion date is invented. Completion dates are actual dates when criteria are satisfied. No new Blocked/Not applicable milestone state is introduced; describe blockers or non-applicable migration scope in the relevant milestone's evidence. A review Milestone=Completed means its documentary criteria were met, not approval, publication, release or Baseline membership.

# 7. Conceptual Entities

The Metadata Model is composed of the following conceptual entities.

## 7.1 Metadata

Represents the complete descriptive information associated with a document.

Metadata is composed of Metadata Elements.

---

## 7.2 Metadata Element

Represents one descriptive property of Metadata.

Each Metadata Element has one semantic meaning.

Metadata Elements are defined independently.

---

## 7.3 Metadata Value

Represents the value assigned to a Metadata Element for a specific document.

Values instantiate Metadata Elements.

---

## 7.4 Metadata Schema

Represents the formal organization of Metadata Elements.

The Schema determines which Metadata Elements may appear within a Metadata instance.

---

## 7.5 Metadata Profile

Represents a specialization of a Metadata Schema for a particular category of documents.

Profiles constrain, but do not redefine, the underlying Metadata Schema.

---

## 7.6 Metadata Instance

Represents the complete Metadata associated with one individual document.

Each Metadata Instance conforms to exactly one Metadata Profile.

---

# 8. Conceptual Relationships

The Metadata Model defines the following relationships.

| Source | Relationship | Target |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| Metadata | is composed of | Metadata Elements |
| Metadata Element | possesses | Metadata Value |
| Metadata Schema | defines | Metadata Elements |
| Metadata Profile | specializes | Metadata Schema |
| Metadata Instance | conforms to | Metadata Profile |
| Metadata Instance | contains | Metadata Values |

---

# 5. Definition

A Metadata Schema is the canonical structural definition of Metadata.

It defines how Metadata Elements are organized, grouped and composed.

The Schema establishes structural consistency while remaining independent of implementation.

---

# 7. Schema Composition

The Metadata Schema is composed of Metadata Elements organized into logical groups.

```text

                    Metadata Schema
                    │
                    ├── Metadata Group
                    │   ├── Metadata Element
                    │   ├── Metadata Element
                    │   └── Metadata Element
                    │
                    ├── Metadata Group
                    │   ├── Metadata Element
                    │   └── Metadata Element
                    │
                    └── Metadata Group
                        ├── Metadata Element
                        ├── Metadata Element
                        └── Metadata Element

```

Grouping exists solely to organize Metadata.

Groups do not modify the semantics of Metadata Elements.

---

# 8. Metadata Groups

Metadata Elements may be organized into conceptual groups.

Typical groups include:

- Identity Metadata
- Descriptive Metadata
- Structural Metadata
- Lifecycle Metadata
- Governance Metadata
- Traceability Metadata
- Discovery Metadata
- Automation Metadata

The Metadata Schema defines the grouping mechanism.

Individual Metadata Profiles determine which groups are applicable.

---

# 13. Structural Constraints

The Metadata Schema shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 13.1. Canonical Organization

There shall be one authoritative Metadata Schema.

---

## 13.2. Structural Independence

The Schema shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 13.3. Semantic Preservation

Structural organization shall not modify Metadata semantics.

---

## 13.4. Extensibility

The Schema shall permit new Metadata Elements without restructuring the existing architecture.

---

## 13.5. Stability

The Schema shall evolve incrementally while preserving compatibility.

---

# 15. Metadata Instance Conformance

Every Metadata Instance shall conform to exactly one Metadata Profile.

A Metadata Instance is considered structurally valid when:

- all required Metadata Elements are present;
- no prohibited Metadata Elements are present;
- structural rules defined by the Metadata Profile are respected.

Semantic validation is outside the scope of this document.

---

# 4. Dictionary Principles

The Metadata Dictionary follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Canonical Definition

Every Metadata Element shall possess one authoritative definition.

---

## 4.2. Semantic Stability

Metadata definitions shall remain stable throughout their lifecycle.

---

## 4.3. Uniqueness

Each Metadata Element shall appear exactly once in the Metadata Dictionary.

---

## 4.4. Technology Independence

Metadata definitions shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 4.5. Traceability

Changes to Metadata definitions shall remain historically traceable.

---

# 5. Purpose of a Dictionary Entry

Each Dictionary Entry defines one Metadata Element.

A Dictionary Entry provides the complete architectural description of that Metadata Element independently of any implementation.

---

# 6. Dictionary Organization

The Metadata Dictionary is organized as a collection of Dictionary Entries.

Conceptually.

```text

                    Metadata Dictionary
                    │
                    ├── Dictionary Entry
                    │
                    ├── Dictionary Entry
                    │
                    ├── Dictionary Entry
                    │
                    └── ...

```

Each Dictionary Entry describes one Metadata Element.

---

## 6.5. R-005 — Profile Compliance

Metadata shall satisfy the requirements of the applicable Metadata Profile.

# 7. Structural Requirements

Metadata shall satisfy the following structural requirements.

- Metadata shall be organized through Metadata Schemas.
- Metadata Profiles shall specialize Metadata Schemas.
- Metadata Instances shall conform to Metadata Profiles.

- Every Metadata Element shall possess one canonical meaning.
- Semantic definitions shall remain stable.
- Equivalent Metadata Elements shall not coexist.
- Metadata terminology shall remain consistent.
- Metadata interpretation shall be deterministic.

# 1. Introduction

The Metadata Roadmap defines the implementation and evolution strategy of the Metadata component within the Documentation Framework.

Metadata represents one of the fundamental architectural components of the framework.

As established in the Design Rationale, the explicit separation between document content and Metadata constitutes one of the first and most important architectural decisions of the Documentation Framework.

This roadmap describes how the Metadata component should evolve while preserving that architectural principle.

---

# 4. Architectural Position

Within the Documentation Framework, Metadata belongs to the Documentation Layer.

Conceptually.

```text

                         Documentation Layer

                    ┌───────────────────────────┐
                    │ Metadata                  │
                    │ Document Identity         │
                    │ Classification            │
                    │ Templates                 │
                    └───────────────────────────┘

```

Metadata provides the descriptive information required by nearly every other architectural component.

---

# Classification Component

> **Documentation Framework — Documentation Component**

> The architectural component responsible for defining, organizing, assigning and governing the semantic classification of documents within the Documentation Framework.

# 1. Overview

The **Classification** component defines how documents are organized into semantic categories according to a defined classification model.

Classification provides a semantic mechanism for organizing documents within the Documentation Framework while remaining independent of their physical representation.

The component establishes the concepts, models, elements, structures, rules and governance required to define and maintain classification systems.

---

# 2. Purpose

The purpose of the Classification component is to provide a consistent and controlled mechanism for classifying documentation.

Classification enables documents to be organized according to their semantic characteristics rather than according to their physical location.

The component provides the architectural foundation required for:

- semantic organization;
- document discovery;
- document grouping;
- classification-based relationships;
- validation;
- governance;
- automation.

---

# 3. Architectural Position

Classification belongs to the **Documentation Layer** of the Documentation Framework.

Conceptually:

```text

                         Documentation Layer

                    ┌───────────────────────────┐
                    │ Metadata                  │
                    │ Document Identity         │
                    │ Classification            │
                    │ Templates                 │
                    └───────────────────────────┘

```

Classification works together with Metadata and Document Identity while maintaining its own architectural responsibility.

---

# 4. Responsibility

The Classification component is responsible for:

- defining classification concepts;
- defining classification models;
- defining classification elements;
- defining classification schemas;
- defining classification assignments;
- defining classification relationships;
- defining classification constraints;
- defining classification lifecycle;
- defining classification validation;
- defining classification governance;
- defining classification extensibility;
- defining authoritative classification terminology.

Classification does not define:

- document identity;
- document metadata in general;
- document templates;
- document workflows;
- physical repository organization.

Those responsibilities belong to other components of the Documentation Framework.

---

# 5. Architectural Independence

Classification is independent of the physical representation of documentation.

The semantic organization defined by Classification shall not depend on:

- directory structures;
- filenames;
- repositories;
- storage technologies;
- document formats;
- implementation technologies.

A physical organization may reflect conceptual distinctions established by Classification, but the physical representation does not define those distinctions.

The relationship is therefore:

```text

         Classification Semantics
                    │
                    ▼

       Architectural Representation
                    │
                    ▼

          Physical Representation

```

and not:

```text

          Physical Representation
                    │
                    ▼

         Classification Semantics

```

---

# 6. Relationship with Other Components

## 6.1. Metadata

Metadata provides descriptive information about documents that may participate in classification.

Classification uses that information without redefining the responsibility of Metadata.

---

## 6.2. Document Identity

Document Identity provides the logical identity of the documents to which classifications may be assigned.

Classification does not establish document identity.

---

## 6.3. Templates

Templates may define standardized structures for representing classification information.

Classification defines the semantic classification model rather than the template used to represent it.

---

## 6.4. Workflow

Workflow may use classification information when determining or controlling document processes.

Classification does not define workflow behavior.

---

## 6.5. Policies

Policies may establish rules governing the use or administration of classifications.

Classification provides the classification structures to which such policies may apply.

---

## 6.6. Registry and Discovery

Classification may provide semantic information used by Registry and Discovery mechanisms to organize and locate documentation.

---

## 6.7. Knowledge Graph

Classification concepts and relationships may contribute semantic information to the Knowledge Graph.

---

# 7. Documentation Structure

The Classification component is defined through the following documents:

| Order | Document | Description |
|------:|----------|-------------|
| 1 | DF-CLS-001 — Classification Architecture | Defines the architectural position, responsibility and boundaries of Classification. |
| 2 | DF-CLS-002 — Classification Concepts | Defines the fundamental concepts of Classification. |
| 3 | DF-CLS-003 — Classification Model | Defines the conceptual model governing classification. |
| 4 | DF-CLS-004 — Classification Elements | Defines the elements that constitute a classification system. |
| 5 | DF-CLS-005 — Classification Schema | Defines the formal structure of classification systems. |
| 6 | DF-CLS-006 — Classification Lifecycle | Defines the lifecycle of classification structures and assignments. |
| 7 | DF-CLS-007 — Classification Validation | Defines classification validation and conformance rules. |
| 8 | DF-CLS-008 — Classification Governance | Defines governance and control of classification systems. |
| 9 | DF-CLS-009 — Classification Relationships | Defines relationships between classification elements and related entities. |
| 10 | DF-CLS-010 — Classification Constraints | Defines constraints that preserve classification integrity. |
| 11 | DF-CLS-011 — Classification Extensibility | Defines mechanisms for extending classification systems. |
| 12 | DF-CLS-012 — Classification Best Practices | Documents recommended practices for classification design and maintenance. |
| 13 | DF-CLS-013 — Classification Dictionary | Defines authoritative Classification terminology. |
| 14 | DF-CLS-014 — Classification Specification | Consolidates the normative Classification specification. |
| 15 | DF-CLS-015 — Classification Examples | Provides representative examples of Classification usage. |

---

# 8. Documentation Progression

The documentation follows four major stages.

## 8.1. Conceptual Foundation

```text

    DF-CLS-001
    DF-CLS-002
    DF-CLS-003

```

Defines the architectural and conceptual foundations of Classification.

## 8.2. Structural Definition

```text

    DF-CLS-004
    DF-CLS-005

```

Defines the elements and structures used to represent classifications.

## 8.3. Operational Definition

```text

    DF-CLS-006
    DF-CLS-007
    DF-CLS-008
    DF-CLS-009
    DF-CLS-010
    DF-CLS-011

```

Defines lifecycle, validation, governance, relationships, constraints and extensibility.

## 8.4. Consolidation and Reference

```text

    DF-CLS-012
    DF-CLS-013
    DF-CLS-014
    DF-CLS-015

```

Provides best practices, terminology, normative specification and examples.

---

# 9. Classification Model

The Classification component establishes a conceptual distinction between:

```text

                    Classification System
                    │
                    ├── Classification Model
                    │
                    ├── Classification Elements
                    │
                    ├── Classification Relationships
                    │
                    ├── Classification Constraints
                    │
                    └── Classification Assignments

```

The detailed definitions of these concepts belong to the respective Classification specifications.

---

# 10. Classification and Metadata Type

Metadata `Type` may participate in classification.

However, the semantic meaning of `Type` remains defined by Metadata.

Classification shall not redefine Metadata `Type` merely to support its own model.

The relationship between `Type`, semantic classification and physical organization shall be addressed consistently across the Documentation Framework.

In particular, the existence of physical directory distinctions shall not be interpreted as evidence that those directories define the semantics of `Type`.

---

# 11. Validation

Classification shall support validation at multiple levels:

1. element existence;
2. structural validity;
3. value validity;
4. semantic validity;
5. cross-element consistency;
6. cross-document consistency;
7. architectural consistency.

The detailed validation rules are defined by **DF-CLS-007 — Classification Validation**.

---

# 12. Governance

Classification systems shall be subject to controlled governance.

Governance concerns include:

- ownership;
- responsibility;
- approval;
- change control;
- review;
- publication;
- deprecation;
- retirement.

The detailed governance model is defined by **DF-CLS-008 — Classification Governance**.

---

# 13. Extensibility

Classification shall support controlled evolution.

Extensions may include:

- new classification categories;
- new classification elements;
- new attributes;
- schema extensions;
- new relationships;
- additional classification models.

Extensions shall preserve established semantics and maintain compatibility with existing classification definitions where required.

The detailed extensibility model is defined by **DF-CLS-011 — Classification Extensibility**.

---

# 14. Authoritative Specification

The complete normative definition of Classification is consolidated in:

**DF-CLS-014 — Classification Specification**

The other Classification documents provide the concepts, models, structures, rules and supporting material from which the specification is established.

The specification is therefore the authoritative reference for the complete Classification component.

---

# 15. Examples

Representative examples are maintained separately in:

**DF-CLS-015 — Classification Examples**

Examples are intended to demonstrate the application of the Classification specification without becoming normative definitions themselves.

---

# 16. Roadmap

The development sequence of the Classification component is defined by:

**DF-RDM-030 — Classification Roadmap**

The roadmap describes the progressive development of the component but does not itself define the Classification architecture.

---

# 17. Design Principles

The Classification component follows the following principles:

- **Semantic Independence** — Classification represents semantic organization rather than physical storage.
- **Architectural Separation** — Classification maintains clear boundaries with other Documentation Framework components.
- **Explicit Semantics** — classification concepts shall have explicit and unambiguous meanings.
- **Consistency** — classification definitions shall remain internally and cross-component consistent.
- **Traceability** — classification changes shall remain traceable.
- **Controlled Evolution** — classification systems shall evolve through defined lifecycle and governance mechanisms.
- **Extensibility** — classification shall support controlled extension.
- **Single Source of Truth** — authoritative classification concepts shall have a single canonical definition.
- **Technology Independence** — classification shall not depend on implementation technologies.

---

# 18. Component Completion

The Classification component is considered architecturally complete when its documentation establishes:

- the architectural responsibility of Classification;
- its fundamental concepts;
- its conceptual model;
- its elements;
- its schema;
- its lifecycle;
- its validation rules;
- its governance;
- its relationships;
- its constraints;
- its extensibility mechanisms;
- its best practices;
- its authoritative terminology;
- its normative specification;
- representative examples.

---

# 19. Future Evolution

Future versions of the Classification component may introduce additional capabilities such as:

- advanced taxonomy models;
- ontology-based classification;
- semantic classification;
- automated classification;
- AI-assisted classification;
- classification quality metrics;
- interoperability mechanisms;
- semantic impact analysis.

Such extensions shall preserve the architectural boundaries and principles established by the Documentation Framework.

---

# 20. Change History

| Date | Version | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| 2026-08-09 | 1.0 | Initial Classification component README. |

---

**End of Document**

---

# Metadata Component

> **Documentation Framework — Documentation Component**

---

> The architectural component responsible for defining, organizing, governing and standardizing the metadata that describes documents within the Documentation Framework.

---

# Overview

The **Metadata** component defines the canonical metadata architecture of the Documentation Framework.

It establishes the concepts, structures, lifecycle, governance and specifications required to describe documents in a consistent, technology-independent and architecturally stable manner.

Metadata provides the common semantic foundation upon which the remaining Documentation Framework components are built.

---

# Purpose

The Metadata component is responsible for defining:

- the Metadata architecture;
- Metadata concepts;
- Metadata models;
- Metadata elements;
- Metadata schemas;
- Metadata validation;
- Metadata governance;
- Metadata extensibility.

The component does **not** define:

- document content;
- document storage;
- repositories;
- workflows;
- permissions;
- implementation technologies.

---

# Responsibilities

The Metadata component is responsible for:

- defining canonical Metadata concepts;
- defining Metadata Elements;
- defining Metadata Schemas;
- defining Metadata Profiles;
- defining Metadata Relationships;
- defining Metadata Constraints;
- defining Metadata Lifecycle;
- defining Metadata Validation;
- defining Metadata Governance;
- defining Metadata Extensibility;
- maintaining the Metadata Dictionary;
- publishing the Metadata Specification.

---

# Component Scope

The Metadata component defines **what metadata is** and **how it is architecturally described** within the Documentation Framework.

It does not define:

- how documents are managed;
- how repositories operate;
- how metadata is physically stored;
- how metadata is implemented;
- how metadata is exchanged between systems.

Those responsibilities belong to other Documentation Framework components.

---

# Architectural Position

Within the Documentation Framework architecture, Metadata is a **Documentation Component**.

Conceptually.

```text

					Documentation Framework
					│
					├── Foundation
					├── Architecture
					├── Documentation
					│   ├── Metadata
					│   ├── Document Identity
					│   ├── Classification
					│   └── Templates
					│
					├── Governance
					├── Discovery
					├── Automation
					├── Integration
					├── Resources
					├── Guides
					└── Reference

```

Metadata provides the semantic foundation for multiple Documentation Framework components while remaining independent of their individual responsibilities.

---

# Document Organization

The Metadata component documentation is organized into four architectural areas.

```text

					Metadata/
					│
					├── README.md
					│
					├── 01-Architecture/
					│
					├── 02-Structure/
					│
					├── 03-Behavior/
					│
					└── 04-Reference/

```

Each directory groups documents according to a specific architectural responsibility.

---

# Document Map

## 01 — Architecture

Defines the conceptual foundation of the component.

| Document | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| DF-MTD-001 | Metadata Architecture |
| DF-MTD-002 | Metadata Concepts |
| DF-MTD-003 | Metadata Model |
| DF-MTD-004 | Metadata Elements |

---

## 02 — Structure

Defines how metadata is structurally organized.

| Document | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| DF-MTD-005 | Metadata Schema |
| DF-MTD-009 | Metadata Relationships |
| DF-MTD-010 | Metadata Constraints |

---

## 03 — Behavior

Defines how metadata evolves and is governed.

| Document | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| DF-MTD-006 | Metadata Lifecycle |
| DF-MTD-007 | Metadata Validation |
| DF-MTD-008 | Metadata Governance |
| DF-MTD-011 | Metadata Extensibility |

---

## 04 — Reference

Provides the normative specification and supporting reference material.

| Document | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| DF-MTD-012 | Metadata Best Practices *(Informative)* |
| DF-MTD-013 | Metadata Dictionary *(Reference)* |
| DF-MTD-014 | Metadata Specification *(Normative)* |
| DF-MTD-015 | Metadata Examples *(Informative)* |

---

# Recommended Reading Order

The Metadata documentation has been designed for incremental reading.

```text

			   Architecture
					│
					▼
			     Concepts
					│
					▼
				  Model
					│
					▼
				 Elements
					│
					▼
				  Schema
					│

			  Relationships
					│
					▼
			   Constraints
					│
					▼
				Lifecycle
					│
					▼
				Validation
					│
					▼
				Governance
					│
					▼
			  Extensibility
					│
					▼
			    Dictionary
					│
					▼
			   Specification
					│
					▼
			  Best Practices
					│
					▼
				 Examples

```

Although each document may be consulted independently, this sequence provides the most comprehensive understanding of the component.

---

# Architectural Dependencies

The Metadata component depends upon the architectural foundation of the Documentation Framework.

## Foundation

- DF-FND-001 — Framework Manifest
- DF-FND-004 — Architectural Blueprint
- DF-FND-006 — Design Rationale

## Architecture

- DF-ARC-001 — Architecture Overview
- DF-ARC-002 — Architectural Principles
- DF-ARC-003 — Architectural Concepts
- DF-ARC-004 — Architectural Layers
- DF-ARC-005 — Architectural Components

---

# Related Components

The Metadata component collaborates with multiple Documentation Framework components.

| Component | Layer | Relationship |
|-----------|-------|--------------|
| Document Identity | Documentation | Uses metadata to describe and preserve document identity attributes. |
| Classification | Documentation | Uses metadata to classify and categorize documents. |
| Registry | Discovery | Uses metadata to register and discover documentation assets. |
| Relationships | Discovery | Uses metadata to describe relationships between documents. |
| Knowledge Graph | Discovery | Uses metadata to build semantic knowledge networks. |
| Workflow | Governance | Uses metadata during documentation lifecycle management. |
| Policies | Governance | Defines policies governing metadata usage and quality. |
| Baselines | Governance | Uses metadata to describe baseline composition and evolution. |

Metadata remains independent and does not assume the responsibilities of these components.

# Document Identity Component

> **Documentation Framework — Documentation Component**

---

> The architectural component responsible for defining, assigning, preserving and governing the permanent identity of documents within the Documentation Framework.

---

# Overview

The **Document Identity** component defines the canonical identity model of the Documentation Framework.

It establishes the concepts, structures, lifecycle, governance and specifications required to uniquely identify documents throughout their entire lifetime, independently of their content, storage location or implementation technology.

Document Identity provides the persistent identification foundation upon which document traceability, governance and discovery are built.

---

# Purpose

The Document Identity component is responsible for defining:

- the Document Identity architecture;
- Document Identity concepts;
- Document Identity models;
- Document Identity elements;
- Document Identity schemas;
- Document Identity lifecycle;
- Document Identity validation;
- Document Identity governance;
- Document Identity extensibility.

The component does **not** define:

- document metadata;
- document content;
- document classification;
- repositories;
- workflows;
- implementation technologies.

---

# Responsibilities

The Document Identity component is responsible for:

- defining canonical Document Identity concepts;
- defining Document Identity Elements;
- defining Document Identity Schemas;
- defining Identity Relationships;
- defining Identity Constraints;
- defining the Identity Lifecycle;
- defining Identity Validation;
- defining Identity Governance;
- defining Identity Extensibility;
- maintaining the Document Identity Dictionary;
- publishing the Document Identity Specification.

---

# Component Scope

The Document Identity component defines **what a document identity is** and **how it is architecturally described** within the Documentation Framework.

It does not define:

- document metadata;
- document lifecycle management;
- repository organization;
- document storage;
- document implementation;
- document classification.

Those responsibilities belong to other Documentation Framework components.

---

# Architectural Position

Within the Documentation Framework architecture, Document Identity is a **Documentation Component**.

Conceptually.

```text

                    Documentation Framework
....................│
                    ├── Foundation
                    ├── Architecture
                    ├── Documentation
                    │   ├── Metadata
                    │   ├── Document Identity
                    │   ├── Classification
                    │   └── Templates
                    │
                    ├── Governance
                    ├── Discovery
                    ├── Automation
                    ├── Integration
                    ├── Resources
                    ├── Guides
                    └── Reference

```

Document Identity provides the permanent identification model used throughout the Documentation Framework while remaining independent of document content and implementation.

---

# Document Organization

The Document Identity component documentation is organized into four architectural areas.

```text

                    DocumentIdentity/
                    │
                    ├── README.md
                    │
                    ├── 01-Architecture/
                    │
                    ├── 02-Structure/
                    │
                    ├── 03-Behavior/
                    │
                    └── 04-Reference/

```

Each directory groups documents according to a specific architectural responsibility.
