# 7. Classification Context

**Received conceptual diagram retained at its original section; current interpretation is qualified below.**

```text
          Classification Context
                    │
                    ▼

           Classification Value

```

| Original label | Current typed interpretation / limit |
|---|---|
| Classification Context | Governing interpretation/source/definition/edition/time/usage context required by the claim, not a mandatory physical tuple |
| Classification Value | Interpreted semantic value/representation under actual role/scheme/context, not a label, category identity or completed assignment by itself |

**Relation scope:** Context governs value interpretation; no universal field set or mandatory serialization is imposed.

Classification Context identifies the governing interpretation of a value or assignment: the intended scheme/domain and responsible definition meanings, with source/edition/time/usage or other context required by the actual claim. It is conceptual interpretation, not a prescribed record-field catalog or universal mandatory tuple.

Identical labels in different declared contexts need not identify the same category. A label, alias, category identity, interpreted value and actual assignment are not interchangeable. Context needed for a current usage decision may differ from the evidence preserving a historical definition/assignment or pinned snapshot. Missing applicable context is an evidence/authority limitation to assess, not permission to guess a meaning.

---

# 8. Classification Scheme

**Received conceptual diagram retained at its original section; current interpretation is qualified below.**

```text
                    Classification Scheme
                              │
                              ├── Category
                              ├── Category
                              └── Category

```

| Original label | Current typed interpretation / limit |
|---|---|
| Classification Scheme | Governed semantic organization/interpretation of actual categories, not universal physical structure or an implemented classifier |
| Category | Governed semantic category/option in context; placeholder/definition presence does not prove complete admitted population, approval or assignment |

**Relation scope:** Selected scheme/category membership, not complete population, fixed cardinality or one mandatory taxonomy.

A Classification Scheme is a governed semantic organization of categories in a declared interpretation context. Its three received subjects remain:

- a classification domain;
- the categories belonging to that domain;
- the semantic interpretation of those categories.

The tree shows selected scheme/category membership, not universal physical containment, one permitted taxonomy or fixed multiplicity. Formal structural and cardinality rules belong to applicable Model/Schema/Constraints owners. Current CLS-005§34 does not establish complete cardinality; authentic Model content is unavailable. This synopsis does not fill either gap or redefine the uniform normalized-document Type vocabulary through a local scheme.

---

# 9. Classification Element

**Received conceptual diagram retained at its original section; current interpretation is qualified below.**

```text
                    Classification
                    │
                    ├── Element
                    ├── Element
                    └── Element

```

| Original label | Current typed interpretation / limit |
|---|---|
| Classification | Classification domain meaning/organization in this selected conceptual view, not an allocated service or actual completed assignment |
| Element | Conceptual role/dimension here; actual peer umbrella uses need mapping, not a new Metadata Element or component allocation |

**Relation scope:** Conceptual role composition, not architecture-component or Metadata Element allocation.

A Classification Element is a conceptual classification role or dimension used to express a governed distinction. Here Family, Type and Class are distinguishable roles; a particular defined category, interpreted value and actual document assignment are not silently the same entity. An Element is not an automatically allocated architectural component or Metadata Element.

Received peers use Classification Element as a broader umbrella in some category/assignment definitions. This edition states its working conceptual distinction and preserves those actual uses for precise owner reconciliation (§44), not a claim that all detailed Model/Elements/Dictionary meanings already agree. Detailed CLS-004 and schema/constraint contracts retain actual applicability; no new field ID, complete structure or cardinality is invented.

---

# 10. Classification Value

**Received conceptual diagram retained at its original section; current interpretation is qualified below.**

```text
         Classification Element
                    │
                    ▼

          Classification Value

```

| Original label | Current typed interpretation / limit |
|---|---|
| Classification Element | Conceptual role/dimension here; actual peer umbrella uses need mapping, not a new Metadata Element or component allocation |
| Classification Value | Interpreted semantic value/representation under actual role/scheme/context, not a label, category identity or completed assignment by itself |

**Relation scope:** Role/value interpretation, not automatic category identity, assignment or one-to-one physical structure.

A Classification Value is interpreted semantic value in an applicable classification role/context. Its representation may select a defined category under actual scheme/schema rules; a lexical string alone is not the category identity, complete semantic definition or evidence that an assignment occurred.

A Family role, for example, can be represented by an admitted component or documentary-area value for a normalized document. Current Family is not an arbitrary broad domain label or stable document-ID series. Scheme/definition/source context determines interpretation. Actual Dictionary§6.6 also describes value assigned to a document or context; that unchanged wording is mapped as a related use rather than silently merged into a new accepted universal model.

---

# 11. Classification Category

**Received conceptual diagram retained at its original section; current interpretation is qualified below.**

```text
                  Classification Scheme
                            │
                            ├── Category A
                            ├── Category B
                            └── Category C

```

| Original label | Current typed interpretation / limit |
|---|---|
| Classification Scheme | Governed semantic organization/interpretation of actual categories, not universal physical structure or an implemented classifier |
| Category A | Governed semantic category/option in context; placeholder/definition presence does not prove complete admitted population, approval or assignment |
| Category B | Governed semantic category/option in context; placeholder/definition presence does not prove complete admitted population, approval or assignment |
| Category C | Governed semantic category/option in context; placeholder/definition presence does not prove complete admitted population, approval or assignment |

**Relation scope:** Selected category membership; A/B/C are placeholders, not accepted entries, allocations or an exhaustive scheme.

A Classification Category is a defined semantic option within a declared scheme/context. It has governed meaning rather than being an arbitrary textual label. Category A/B/C are received conceptual placeholders, not actual allocations, accepted vocabulary entries or proof that three categories exhaust a scheme.

An applicable value may express/select a category; an Element supplies the classification role, and an Assignment records the actual association for the intended subject. No universal one-to-one cardinality or physical schema is inferred. Dictionary§6.5 currently calls a Category a semantic grouping represented by an Element; that precise owner terminology remains an explicitly mapped related use pending coordinated Model/Elements/Schema/Dictionary reconciliation.

---

# 12. Family

**Received conceptual diagram retained at its original section; current interpretation is qualified below.**

```text
                    Family
                    │
                    ├── Document
                    ├── Document
                    └── Document

```

| Original label | Current typed interpretation / limit |
|---|---|
| Family | Current normalized-document component/admitted-area dimension; prior broad-domain labels are explicitly historical |
| Document | Applicable intended logical-document subject; actual key/edition/context/assignment evidence differs from file existence or physical containment |

**Relation scope:** Document grouping is retained while the old broad-domain Family meaning is explicitly replaced for current normalized documents.

**Current working definition.** For normalized documents, Family identifies canonical component membership or an explicitly admitted non-component documentary area under common Architecture and Review Policy3. Component documents use their actual canonical component name; admitted Foundation, Architecture and global Roadmap cases follow their stated Policy scope. A current Family is not a directory, arbitrary domain label or document allocation-series code.

**Received meaning and historical context.** V1.0 R0 defined Family as a broad documentary domain and asked “What broad documentary domain does this document belong to?” That exact prior definition/question and the received META example remain history/maps. META's introduction as a historical broad-domain grouping explains the earlier convention; it does not prescribe the current normalized-document contract or prove new allocation/approval. This V2.0 R1 replaces that unqualified current definition locally, with affected peer propagation explicit in §44.

---

# 13. Type

**Received conceptual diagram retained at its original section; current interpretation is qualified below.**

```text
                    Family
                      │
                      ├── Type
                      ├── Type
                      └── Type

```

| Original label | Current typed interpretation / limit |
|---|---|
| Family | Current normalized-document component/admitted-area dimension; prior broad-domain labels are explicitly historical |
| Type | Current uniform primary responsibility Architecture/Structure/Behavior/Reference; prior Family specialisation is not imposed |

**Relation scope:** Family→Type records the prior specialisation view; current Type responsibility is uniform across Families.

**Current working definition.** Type identifies exactly one primary documentary responsibility using Architecture, Structure, Behavior or Reference, uniformly across Families. Concepts, Model, Elements, Schema, Dictionary, Lifecycle, Base/Core and historical codes are not additional Type values merely because a source title or directory uses them. Historical consultation is Reference; a process or planned evolution is Behavior. Type=Reference by itself neither creates nor removes normative authority or approval.

**Received meaning and historical context.** V1.0 R0 treated Type as a more specific classification within Family and asked “What specific kind of document exists within this Family?” The Family→Type picture and META-DCL example remain exact received evidence. In that historical convention META and DCL had their recorded roles; they are not the current governing Family/Type vocabulary or document-ID construction rule. Current Type meaning is not redefined per Family. Applicable usage constraints need responsible context without silently creating another Type enumeration or universal specialisation hierarchy.

---

# 14. Class

**Received conceptual diagram retained at its original section; current interpretation is qualified below.**

```text
    Family
    Type
    Class

```

| Original label | Current typed interpretation / limit |
|---|---|
| Family | Current normalized-document component/admitted-area dimension; prior broad-domain labels are explicitly historical |
| Type | Current uniform primary responsibility Architecture/Structure/Behavior/Reference; prior Family specialisation is not imposed |
| Class | Separate optional explicitly defined non-conflicting distinction; no mandatory field, complete enumeration or universal subordinate position |

**Relation scope:** Distinct dimensions with optional defined Class; not a mandatory tuple or universal hierarchy.

Class remains a separate optional semantic dimension. When used, it needs an explicit non-conflicting definition in the actual context. Optional does not mean an unrestricted string or a substitute for the governing Type responsibility.

The received nature/role description and Family/Type/Class labels remain mapped, but cannot be used to duplicate Type's responsibility without an actual additional defined distinction. No complete Class enumeration, mandatory Class value, universal Type→Class hierarchy or fifth Type is created here. Other exact peers that put Class within Type or use different role wording retain those clauses pending source-qualified reconciliation; this edition does not claim an accepted merged schema.

---

# 15. Family, Type and Class

**Received conceptual diagram retained at its original section; current interpretation is qualified below.**

```text
                    Classification
                    │
                    ├── Family
                    │   └── broad documentary domain
                    │
                    ├── Type
                    │   └── specific documentary kind
                    │
                    └── Class
                        └── documentary nature or role

```

| Original label | Current typed interpretation / limit |

| Classification | Classification domain meaning/organization in this selected conceptual view, not an allocated service or actual completed assignment |
| Family | Current normalized-document component/admitted-area dimension; prior broad-domain labels are explicitly historical |
| broad documentary domain | Received descriptive label retained as prior conceptual wording; current meanings are §§12–15, not simultaneous contradictory definitions |
| Type | Current uniform primary responsibility Architecture/Structure/Behavior/Reference; prior Family specialisation is not imposed |
| specific documentary kind | Received descriptive label retained as prior conceptual wording; current meanings are §§12–15, not simultaneous contradictory definitions |
| Class | Separate optional explicitly defined non-conflicting distinction; no mandatory field, complete enumeration or universal subordinate position |
| documentary nature or role | Received descriptive label retained as prior conceptual wording; current meanings are §§12–15, not simultaneous contradictory definitions |

**Relation scope:** Prior broad/specific/nature-role labels remain mapped; current Family/Type/optional-Class meanings supersede conflicting current interpretation.

The three dimensions remain conceptually distinguishable, not a universal hierarchy. Current normalized-document Family is component/admitted area, Type is uniform primary responsibility and Class optional explicitly defined additional meaning.

The received descriptive labels “broad documentary domain”, “specific documentary kind” and “documentary nature or role” are preserved as prior conceptual descriptions in the diagram/map. They do not simultaneously govern the same current Family/Type meanings. The prior progressively-more-specific Family/Type interpretation is replaced in this working edition; actual other hierarchical relationships require their own scheme/type/context/owner rules. Complete formal Model and cardinality are not supplied by this selected view.

---

# 16. Classification Assignment

**Received conceptual diagram retained at its original section; current interpretation is qualified below.**

```text
                Document
                    │
               assignment
                    │
                    ▼

           Classification Value

```

| Original label | Current typed interpretation / limit |
|---|---|
| Document | Applicable intended logical-document subject; actual key/edition/context/assignment evidence differs from file existence or physical containment |
| assignment | Actual intended subject-to-value/category association under responsible rules/definition/usage/decision context; not automatic from an arrow |
| Classification Value | Interpreted semantic value/representation under actual role/scheme/context, not a label, category identity or completed assignment by itself |

**Relation scope:** Actual documentary assignment association requires governing rules/context/authority/evidence; no execution from a drawn arrow.

A Classification Assignment is the actual governed association of an intended document with an interpreted classification value/category under an applicable scheme/definition context. It does not redefine that meaning. Actual evidence identifies the intended subject, governing rules/source editions and required definition edition/time/usage/decision context without inventing a universal storage tuple.

For an applicable assigned normalized document, use its governing qualified K; a document-edition-specific claim needs the additional edition/bytes/context. Category, definition, value representation, assignment record and document identity are distinct subjects. Other entity identity contracts are not automatically DF document IDs. A drawn arrow or a supplied value does not itself authorize or prove assignment, migration or membership.

---

```text
                    │
                    ▼

                Documents

```

| Original label | Current typed interpretation / limit |

| Classification Category | Governed semantic category/option in context; placeholder/definition presence does not prove complete admitted population, approval or assignment |
| contains | Received relation/question label typed by this section; semantic identity, interpretation, association, representation, required contract and execution are not interchangeable |
| Documents | Applicable intended logical-document subject; actual key/edition/context/assignment evidence differs from file existence or physical containment |

**Relation scope:** Semantic membership rather than physical containment or guaranteed present/future usage validity.

Membership is the semantic consequence of an actual valid applicable assignment, not physical containment. The contains arrow is a governed semantic association about intended documents, not a directory, complete population listing or allocation engine.

Ordinary movement may preserve assignment meaning while actual reference validity, usage conditions, representations, index freshness and provider interfaces still need checks. Definition lifecycle, current assignment permission and preserved historical/pinned interpretation differ: a deprecated/retired definition does not automatically erase historical meaning or prove current use valid. Responsible rules/authority/context decide the actual claim; no automatic migration, reassignment or silent snapshot retargeting follows.

A Classification Dimension is a conceptual aspect through which a declared scheme/context expresses a distinction. The three received labels remain, with current normalized-document Family/Type/optional-Class meanings in §§12–15; they do not impose the old Family-dependent hierarchy or a mandatory three-field record.

Other actual dimensions require their responsible explicit definitions, contexts, structural/usage constraints and change authority. Adding one does not implicitly add another Type, allocate Metadata fields or fill missing cardinality. The intended formal Model is unresolved, so this document does not claim its complete dimensional model is already supplied or approved.

# 29. Classification Constraint

The three received constraint examples remain with qualified applicability:

| Received subject | Current qualified meaning / limit |

| whether a value may be assigned; | Actual admitted category/value and intended assignment subject/context/source rules, authority and observations determine whether use is permitted. |
| whether a Type is valid within a Family; | Current uniform Type meaning is not a Family-specific specialisation vocabulary; actual contextual usage constraints may not silently redefine that meaning. |
| whether a classification combination is permitted. | An applicable combination needs the responsible schema/constraints/context and actual observations; no universal tuple, cardinality or Model is fabricated. |

Detailed rules belong to actual CLS-010/Schema/Validation owners. Missing/unperformed/conflicting authority is not itself an observed violation or broad success. Current received peer Family/Type constraints remain exact evidence pending separately traced propagation, not claimed already aligned.

---

# 30. Classification Lifecycle

The four received lifecycle terms remain, with definition/action/usage scope explicit:

| Received subject | Current qualified meaning / limit |
|---|---|
| introduced; | Introduced describes an introduction action/concept here, not a silently registered state or automatic alias for Defined. |
| active; | Active refers to definition availability in actual owner context; not document Status, approval or permission from the label alone. |
| deprecated; | Deprecated preserves historical recognition with applicable restrictions/warnings for new/current use; actual rules decide the result. |
| retired. | Retired concerns definition availability under its responsible contract; it does not erase historical assignment meaning, retire document K or release an allocated key. |

Current CLS-006§20 explicitly calls Defined/Active/Deprecated/Retired proposed states of the classification definition. Its §§7–8 distinguish definition lifecycle from document classification usage. This Concepts comparison does not promote that proposal to implemented/approved lifecycle or silently rename introduced as Defined; exact owner applicability/authority remains necessary. Definition state, assignment usage, document Status, identity R assertion, finding state and Milestone state differ. No transition permission, actual retirement or automatic migration is granted; CLS-006§43 explicitly does not establish automatic migration.

---

# 31. Classification Governance

All five received governance subjects remain as distinct concerns:

| Received subject | Current qualified meaning / limit |
|---|---|
| ownership; | Responsible classification semantic/record owners in actual context; not authorship or custody alone. |
| authority; | Actual governing rule/change/decision authority for the declared operation, with exact sources and limits. |
| approval; | A real acceptance/approval decision under applicable Governance rules; not inferred from validation, definition presence or a diagram. |
| change control; | Actual prior/new impact, compatibility/version, mappings/history and coordinated transition evidence under §33. |
| maintenance responsibilities. | Responsible preservation/usage/provenance duties for definitions and assignments, not an installed executor or new component. |

Classification supplies its own domain lifecycle/usage/governance conditions. Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines supply common area contracts; actual authorized DMS/tool/manual decisions/execution and CMS change scope are separate. The received Governance-distinct-from-Classification phrase excludes takeover of the common process, not Classification's own domain rules. Validation is evidence, not permission, formal approval, publication or exact eligible approved-edition/pinned-context Baseline selection. Draft successors inherit no original approval/membership.

# 32. Classification Validation

# 5. Entity Relationships

Relationships below express qualified conceptual associations. Their direction and population subject are explicit; they are not operational calls or every-component routing requirements. Exact valid target, canonical interpretation and required-use evidence remain distinct. §6 preserves and reconciles the received cardinality interpretations within this local Model scope.

---

## 5.1. Document → Document Identity

An applicable **assigned normalized logical document** has one valid assigned document identity under its declared document/domain contract. The requirement does not imply that a pre-allocation subject already has a key or that excluded functional files cannot exist without normalized metadata.

DID-006 §5.1 describes an Unassigned subject before allocation. That subject differs from an assigned key; this Model does not supply a universal creation/permission graph. Other entity-domain identities and exact document editions are not additional interchangeable DF document keys.

**Evidence boundary:** Identify actual document, normalized applicability, domain, assignment/reservation history and exact examined edition. Source recognition or registration alone proves neither approval nor completed allocation.

---

## 5.2. Document Identity → Identifier

An assigned document identity has one canonical identifier representation under its governing identity-domain contract. The logical entity, Domain+Identifier key and rendered string are distinct. Alternative aliases or physical representations may interpret the same existing identity under explicit canonicalization/target rules; they do not license another document to reuse its allocation.

For this corpus, the adopted representation is **DF-SSS-NNN**: a registered stable three-letter allocation series and a positive allocated number (001–999). Current Family, Type, Component, path, Version, Revision and Status do not reconstruct or recalculate the assigned ID. 000 is not allocated; gaps do not prove availability; allocated/retired numbers are not reused. DID-001 and Review Policy own this qualified synopsis; detailed Schema/Constraints/Specification integration remains pending. No allocation, series registration or actual migration occurs here.

**Evidence boundary:** Check actual domain, representation and alias/target rules with examined records. Canonical interpretation is a requirement, not a guarantee of a running resolver or future retrievable content.

---

## 5.3. Identity Domain → Document Identity

Each assigned document identity belongs to one declared governing identity domain. The domain establishes uniqueness, allocation and preservation requirements; it does not demonstrate that every actual record is already unique merely by being defined.

Membership direction differs from domain population: one domain may have no allocated members or multiple members unless a separately applicable owner contract explicitly imposes a minimum. Documentation Framework, represented by DF, is the adopted documentary domain. Equal numeric suffixes in distinct registered series are not collisions when full qualified identifiers differ. Other-domain use requires explicit qualified owners/rules and relevant registration/context evidence rather than silent implementation-created domains.

**Evidence boundary:** Identify domain owner, scope, actual current/historical allocation and collision coverage. A partial scan or absent reservation history proves no global uniqueness or availability.

---

## 5.4. Identity Reference → Document Identity

A valid document-targeting Identity Reference identifies its intended existing qualified document identity. Exact-edition targeting additionally identifies intended coordinates/bytes and relevant context. Reference association, alias/canonical representation and assigned identity key are separate facts.

Relationships owns typed connection records and provenance; Document Identity owns document endpoint meanings. Other endpoint kinds follow their own domain contracts. A reference does not create or redefine its target identity. An assigned identity does not require an incoming reference merely to exist: selected reference population is zero or more under §6 and DID-005's explicit optionality. A dangling or ambiguous reference is an unresolved validity observation, not proof that a new target exists or permission to silently retarget it.

**Evidence boundary:** Check actual target, domain, edition/context and reference-record evidence. Historical interpretation differs from live retrieval. Required consumer→provider uses are separately typed and remain visible even when values arrive through a projection; no complete relationship catalog or globally cycle-free graph is certified.

# 4. Architectural Elements

The five original element titles and subordinate headings are retained. Conceptual element responsibility does not by itself create a Metadata Element, mandatory schema field, interface or runtime component.

---

## 4.1. Document Identity



### 4.1.1. Description

**Document Identity** is the stable same-document logical identity under a declared allocation/preservation contract. An assigned key differs from the file containing the document, its edition coordinates, descriptive records and reference associations. An unassigned documentary subject does not yet possess that assigned key.

---

### 4.1.2. Responsibility

- Identify the applicable assigned logical document within its domain.
- Preserve the same-document association across ordinary lifecycle, classification, content, edition, format and repository changes.
- Provide document endpoint meaning for qualified references without claiming a live resolution service.

Allocation, collision/reservation and preservation checks require actual records and responsible executors; registration alone proves no approval or successful allocation.

---

### 4.1.3. Characteristics

- **Unique:** a requirement within the qualified domain and examined allocation scope, not globally unique unqualified strings.
- **Immutable:** the assigned key/association under its governing contract, not every state/reference record.
- **Permanent:** allocated/retired keys are not reassigned; historical interpretation is preserved without a retrieval guarantee.
- **Canonical:** an explicitly governed interpretation/representation, not document Status, approval or automatic Baseline inclusion.

---

## 4.2. Identifier



### 4.2.1. Description

The **Identifier** represents a document identity under its domain's canonicalization/allocation rules. The logical entity, qualified key and rendered string are related but distinct. Aliases and other representations shall identify the intended existing key under explicit rules; they do not allocate another interchangeable document identity.

---

### 4.2.2. Responsibility

- Represent the assigned qualified identity under responsible domain rules.
- Support unambiguous human/machine interpretation with the necessary domain/context.
- Preserve valid allocations when Family, Type, Component, path or edition changes.

For this corpus, Documentation Framework is the domain, represented by DF. The adopted convention is **DF-SSS-NNN**: registered uppercase three-letter stable allocation series and positive three-digit allocation001–999. Current classification does not regenerate assigned IDs. Equal numeric suffixes across different series are not collisions when the full qualified IDs differ. 000 is not allocated; a gap proves no availability; allocated/retired numbers are not reused. At999, register an unused series with traceable continuation rather than widen or recycle silently. This restates DID-001/Review Policy; detailed DID-005/010/014 integration remains pending. No new allocation occurs here.

---

### 4.2.3. Characteristics

Unique within the governed domain, stable for its assigned document, deterministically interpretable under explicit representation/canonicalization rules, and semantically independent of implementation technology. Deterministic interpretation does not demonstrate an implemented generator/resolver or actual uniqueness. Logical requirements can constrain adapters and representations without choosing a storage format.

---

## 4.3. Identity Domain



### 4.3.1. Description

**Identity Domain** defines the qualified scope, responsible allocation rules and uniqueness boundary. Domain definition imposes a requirement; actual population and collision/reservation checks establish observations within a stated scope.

---

### 4.3.2. Responsibility

- Establish domain qualification, namespace and responsible allocation/preservation authority.
- Require collision and reservation checks across applicable current/historical records.
- Make non-overlap and cross-domain interpretation explicit rather than assume every bare string is globally unique.

One assigned key has one governing domain. A domain may contain0..N assigned identities unless an applicable owner contract establishes another minimum. Other domains require explicit owners/rules and qualification; this document does not create a universal external-domain registry.

---

### 4.3.3. Characteristics

Stable governing meaning, explicit architectural qualification, and implementation-independent semantics. Domain stability does not prove operational namespace separation; declared owners, actual allocations and context must support that assessment.

---

## 4.4. Identity Status



### 4.4.1. Description

**Identity Status** retains the original architectural element name for state-related facts about identity records. It is not defined here as one universal validity enum. Separate assigned-key existence/preservation/retirement, state assertions, document-edition Draft/Review/Approved/Published/Archived status, maturity and Baseline membership.

DID-003 does not make Identity Status a sixth core entity; DID-005 omits a State field; DID-014 makes Identity State mandatory. Those are real peer-contract differences, not permission to silently add or remove mandatory fields. Metadata can describe a domain-owned state without redefining its semantics; independence does not mean that no descriptive representation or required consumer contract can exist.

---

### 4.4.2. Possible States

The received labels **Active**, **Archived** and **Deprecated** are retained as historical candidate terminology, not an authoritative current state machine or proof of architectural validity. DID-006 §§4–8 and DID-014 §9 instead use Unassigned, Assigned, Preserved and Retired for their stated lifecycle subject. Unassigned is pre-allocation; it does not mean an assigned key already exists.

Do not equate Archived document status with retired identity or derive identity validity from a state word alone. Final state vocabulary, transition permissions, subject and authority require explicit DID-006/014 and Schema/Model reconciliation. This architectural clarification neither approves their complete lifecycle nor invents a merged transition graph.

---

## 4.5. Identity Reference



### 4.5.1. Description

An **Identity Reference** is a typed association whose document endpoint identifies an intended qualified logical document or exact edition. Other endpoint kinds use their own applicable identity contracts. Document Identity owns document endpoint meaning; Relationships owns connection semantics/records, and Registry owns registration/index records in their scopes. An association does not transfer those responsibilities.

---

### 4.5.2. Responsibility

- Identify an intended existing qualified target without creating/redefining its identity.
- Distinguish document-level targeting from exact-edition targeting, which additionally pins coordinates/bytes and relevant context.
- Support cross-component references with declared owner, relation kind, source/target and provenance.

An identity can exist without incoming references: document-targeting incoming population is0..N under DID-003 §6 and DID-005 §§4.3/5. A dangling or ambiguous reference is an unresolved validity observation; it does not authorize creating or silently retargeting an identity. Historical target interpretation is distinct from current retrieval.

---

# 5. Element Relationships

The second selected conceptual view preserves Document and the five original element concepts while clarifying relationship direction and subject. It is not a mandatory object layout or required-service graph.

<!-- original-section-view: 5 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §5 — Document and element associations.**

| From | Relation kind | To | Bounds / interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Applicable assigned normalized Document | assigned identity association | Document Identity | One governing key for that logical document under its declared contract |
| Document Identity | canonical representation | Identifier | One canonical representation; aliases do not allocate a different document |
| Document Identity | domain membership | Identity Domain | One governing domain; domain population0..N absent another applicable owner minimum |
| Identity Status | state-related description | Document Identity record | Separate record/subject; mandatory field and state vocabulary remain peer work |
| Identity Reference | document targeting | Document Identity / exact edition | Incoming reference population0..N; qualified target/context required |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

The original outbound arrows did not prove semantic ownership of every related record or universal one-way dependency. Preserve definition ownership while recording actual required consumer→provider contracts, associations, projections, navigation and execution separately under ARC-004 §§12–13. No mandatory dependency is concealed by a different arrow/relationship label, and no global acyclicity is claimed.

# 4. Lifecycle States

The first selected view retains the four original labels. It describes subjects/facts rather than a claim that a nonexistent key already occupies every state or that every implementation must execute a single four-box workflow.

<!-- original-section-view: 4 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §4 — Lifecycle subjects.**

| Label | Subject and meaning | Evidence / authority boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Unassigned | Applicable documentary subject before an assigned qualified key exists | No allocation inferred from recognition or a file's existence |
| Assigned | Evidenced association of a qualified key with the intended logical document | Actual domain/allocation/reservation checks and assignment provenance required |
| Preserved | Evidenced continuing same-document assignment through qualifying evolution | Supporting records may change; §7 defines the selected transition interpretation |
| Retired | Evidenced retirement of active use within the declared scope | Historical association/reservation retained; no reuse or availability guarantee |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

The source's original chain is retained in external UPDATE provenance. This selected progression omits self-loops and is not the exhaustive transition table. §§5–7 qualify the selected trace contract; §8 separates documentary statuses. DID-005§6 and DID-014§§7–9 still require owner reconciliation of state/complete-record field authority. Historical Active/Archived/Deprecated from DID-004 are not silently equated to these labels or document-edition Status. No mandatory State/Canonical Reference field is removed or invented by a diagram.

---

# 5. State Definitions

The four original state definitions and subordinate headings remain. They define the subject and evidence of a lifecycle assertion, not a running service, approval decision or complete universal permission graph. The selected transitions are interpreted consistently with §7, including its explicit limits and underspecified cases.

---

## 5.1. Unassigned



### 5.1.1. Description

Unassigned concerns a recognized applicable documentary subject that has not yet received an assigned qualified identity. It is not an existing key whose value is Unassigned. Functional-file exclusion and other entity-domain scope are applied first.

---

### 5.1.2. Characteristics

- Pre-allocation: no assigned document key is evidenced for this subject.
- Temporary describes the intended planning phase, not a guaranteed future allocation date or a mandatory path for every file.
- A valid reference claiming an already assigned document-identity target requires that intended existing key. Other associations, planned/unresolved references or physical links are separate subjects with their own rules; the received blanket phrase “no references are permitted” does not prohibit all of them by implication.

An unresolved/planned reference cannot create a target identity or be silently treated as successful allocation.

---

### 5.1.3. Allowed Transition

```text
Unassigned → Assigned
```

Under the selected trace contract, Identity Assignment changes the pre-allocation subject assertion to evidenced assignment. Establish scope, intended document, domain/series rules, actual collision/reservation/history checks and the applicable decision/executor. The transition records the resulting facts, not automatic approval, publication or Baseline selection. Its original block is preserved; §7 row1 is the same relation.

---

## 5.2. Assigned



### 5.2.1. Description

Assigned records that a governed qualified key has been associated with the intended normalized logical document. Distinguish actual allocation/association evidence from a declared string, registration or an unverified imported state. Assignment does not establish every consumer's conformance or global resolution.

---

### 5.2.2. Characteristics

- Existing assigned key under its governing domain contract, with actual provenance.
- Stable same-document association under ordinary evolution; supporting records remain separately mutable.
- Qualified referenceability under explicit domain/canonical interpretation, not universal globally retrievable content.
- Domain-scoped uniqueness and allocated-key non-reuse requirements, supported by stated checks rather than the label alone.

---

### 5.2.3. Allowed Transition

```text
Assigned → Preserved
```

The selected transition uses Document Evolution as its umbrella event (§6/§7 row2). Record a qualifying change or preservation observation, the relevant source/edition/context and verified retention of the same key. The category may cover the seven evolution examples in §5.3 when the applicable event/owner evidence establishes such an evolution; it is not a new automatic operational trigger.

Direct Assigned→Retired is not supplied by the eight received rows and is not authorized by this selected trace contract. A real retirement-before-first-evolution case requires an explicit responsible contract decision/change with impact evidence. Do not fabricate an intervening evolution solely to reach a table row or infer that such a case is impossible in every external lifecycle.

---

## 5.3. Preserved



### 5.3.1. Description

Preserved records continued assignment to the same logical document through the applicable evolution, without implying that every record, representation or consumer remains unchanged. Preserve the seven received example subjects:

- metadata updates;
- content revisions;
- edition creation;
- classification changes;
- repository migration;
- format conversion;
- governance transitions.

§6 maps event categories and §7 retains the selected named transitions. An edition creation may accompany Content Revision or another documented evolution; a format conversion may be representation-only. Do not label every edition/format action Content Revision or invent a table event. For an Assigned subject, a documented qualifying Document Evolution can support row2; for a Preserved subject, use an actual matching row/event where applicable. Merely observing unchanged assignment without a state/event transition is an observation, not an additional allowed transition. An action outside the selected table's supported event cases needs the responsible contract assessment, not a fictional event.

Ordinary changes preserve key/association meaning. If a necessary contract migration would change that governing meaning, §3.2's prior/new reconciliation and actual owner decision are required; this source executes none.

---

### 5.3.2. Allowed Transition

```text
Preserved → Retired
```

This retained block selects the retirement edge; it is not the complete list of Preserved transitions. §7 rows3–7 also retain five Preserved→Preserved event rows, with their actual event names and qualified meaning. Retirement in row8 requires the responsible decision/evidence in §5.4; a document/file status alone cannot trigger it.

---

## 5.4. Retired



### 5.4.1. Description

Retired records an evidenced decision that the key is no longer in active use for the logical document within the declared lifecycle scope. The permanent historical association and allocation reservation remain; retirement neither transfers the key to another document nor deletes evidence of prior assignment.

Retirement is terminal in the selected §7 table: no reactivation/reuse transition is supplied or authorized here. Do not infer universal external permissions from that bounded table. Changes to the responsible retirement contract require explicit owner/consumer impact and prior/new evidence before coordinated application.

Retirement preserves historical target interpretation/reservation under the governing contract, not every reference's actual validity or live retrieval. Deleting a physical representation, an edition or an index row is not by itself a retirement decision for the logical identity; exact historical Baseline members are not retargeted.

---

### 5.4.2. Characteristics

- Stable historical key and same-document association under the applicable contract.
- Non-reusable allocation; retired keys remain reserved for that document/history.
- Historically interpretable with provenance and exact target/context, rather than automatically retrievable.
- Preserved retirement and reservation evidence with actual decision/executor/coverage; the word Retired is not evidence that records were correctly updated everywhere.

---

# 12. Compliance

An actual conformance claim shall identify its exact subject/domain, artifacts/editions/bytes and context, applicable responsible mandatory rules/source editions/interfaces, executor/method, performed/unperformed checks, observations, population/coverage and limitations. Evaluate every applicable mandatory requirement of that declared claim; justify inapplicability explicitly rather than omitting requirements to manufacture success.

DID-007 distinguishes Valid, Invalid, Inconsistent and Unresolvable observations. A successful subset is narrower check evidence, not full identity/component/framework conformity. Establish an actual violation through its applicable rule, subject/context and observed nonconformance. Missing evidence or unresolved authority is neither unconditional success nor automatic Invalid/Unresolvable; preserve all supported negative observations and their limits without suppressing them through a silent precedence rule.

Actual mandatory State/Canonical Reference and complete-record/lifecycle claims in DID-014§§7–8/15/18 remain pending owner reconciliation with DID-005§6 and DID-006. The selected key/association scope does not remove mandatory peer fields, invent an accepted merged record/state machine or approve disregarding another responsible contract. Withhold broader conformity where applicable mandatory evidence/authority is unresolved; narrower unambiguous observations retain their limits. Local source correction validation does not close full peer propagation, reciprocal Metadata/Identity requirements or complete graph/implementation conformity.

The three received conditions for ordinary additional implementation constraints remain:

- do not contradict this specification;
- preserve backward compatibility;
- maintain the canonical architectural model.

These concern ordinary compatible additions under applicable responsible contracts; an implementation extension is not authority to silently amend canonical semantics. DID-014§14 also requires additive/backward-compatible extensions and states that core identity semantics are not extensible. Preserve that actual restriction and its owner-reconciliation obligation; this local correction does not waive it or assert universal agreement with the controlled-evolution protocol.

Before any necessary normative contract or identity/domain/path/representation transition:

1. Preserve original artifacts, actual observations and failed checks; identify prior/new responsible rules/editions, rationale, actual authority and intended subjects/context. A finding, local PASS or documentary authorship alone grants no mutation, allocation or approval.
2. Assess affected semantic/record owners, consumers, indispensable consumer→provider interfaces and unresolved mandatory field/state/extension/required-cycle claims. Reconcile conflicting governing authority before claiming integrated conformance; different names or projection labels cannot remove a real required edge.
3. Record compatibility, exact old→new mappings/qualification, canonical aliases, collisions/reservations/history, same-document continuity and intended references/exact-edition/pinned-snapshot context. Never reassign an allocated/retired key to another document or retarget immutable historical members.
4. Apply only the separately authorized scoped change with actual contributor/event provenance and coordinated transition evidence. For changed working documents, compatible correction retains Version, compatible additive capability increments minor, incompatible contract change increments major and resets minor to0; every persisted changed edition increments Revision monotonically across Versions. Other entity allocation/lifecycle contracts remain separate.
5. Validate resulting exact artifacts/editions in the subsequent appropriate operation and record observations/coverage/remaining conflicts. Unchanged-source validation changes neither source coordinate; later changed bytes need their own assessment. Do not rewrite previous pending events or failures as historical successes.

Evaluation is distinct from writing a result record and from authorized correction; no silent repair/allocation/migration is performed here. Normative intent, received Canonical naming, a Draft working source, local review/validation or implemented check result is not global architectural approval, operational permission, publication or Baseline selection.

## 4.2. Canonical Preservation

An ordinary implementation extension shall not silently redefine responsible canonical document-key/domain semantics. Document Identity remains the semantic owner under applicable common Architecture/Policy, while other descriptor/category/connection/registration/projection owners retain their contracts.

The canonical model is an architectural contract, distinct from mutable support records and runtime representations. Necessary assessed normative/foundational revision follows common evolution principles and §9; core definition is not made unchangeable for all future governed editions merely by calling it canonical.

DID-014§14 still states additive/backward-compatible-only extensions and that core identity semantics are not extensible. Preserve that actual peer restriction and its pending owner/authority reconciliation with the controlled-evolution approach; this source-local correction neither waives it nor claims universal agreement or implementation permission.

---

# 9. Evolution Strategy

The received five-label view is retained as a typed documentary proposal/evidence/decision view. It is not a universal operational pipeline or automatic status promotion. Original text/digest and section anchor remain external evidence; no historic view identifier is invented.

<!-- original-section-view: 9 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §9 — Evolution artifacts, checks and decision boundaries.**

| Original label | Artifact / role | Required evidence / limit |
|---|---|---|
| Current Specification | Identified actual input contract/edition | Exact rules, bytes, authority, subjects/context and known unresolved peer claims |
| Architectural Extension | Scoped proposed addition ornecessary assessed revision | Actual need, alternatives, prior/new owner/consumer/interface impact, compatibility and transition proposal; not permission from a label |
| Compatibility Verification | Actual scoped evaluation evidence | Provider/consumer/representation/reference/edition/context checks, executor, observations, coverage and limits; missing/conflicted authority withholds broader conformity |
| Constraint Verification | Actual applicable mandatory-rule evidence | Responsible constraints/editions, checks/observations and negative results under DID-007; not an allocation/repair/approval decision |
| Canonical Specification | Received name for intended governed specification outcome | A resulting working edition remains at its actual declared lifecycle; local checks do not automatically make it Canonical/Approved, publish it orselect a Baseline |

| Received transition | Typed meaning / decision boundary |
|---|---|
| Current Specification → Architectural Extension | Proposal derived from identified prior contract; not executed change orrequired consumer edge |
| Architectural Extension → Compatibility Verification | Proposed/resulting exact artifact submitted to scoped compatibility evaluation; actual phase/executor/context recorded |
| Compatibility Verification → Constraint Verification | Related evidence requirements, not a mandatory serial runtime order orsuccess inferred from earlier stage |
| Constraint Verification → Canonical Specification | Evidence informs an independently applicable governed edition/decision; no automatic canonical status, approval, publication orBaseline inclusion |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

For an actual necessary normative oridentity/domain/path/representation transition:

1. Preserve exact input artifacts/rules/editions, actual observations and failed checks. Identify the need, alternatives, rationale, prior/new governing rules, responsible authority, subjects/domains and scope. A finding, authorship orlocal PASS alone grants no allocation, mutation, ownership transfer orapproval.
2. Assess affected semantic/record owners, consumers and indispensable consumer→provider interfaces, mandatory State/Canonical Reference/lifecycle/extension requirements and actual reciprocal/cycle claims. Reconcile conflicting governing authority before asserting integrated conformity; do not relabel away a real required edge.
3. Record compatibility and exact old→new mappings, domain/canonical aliases, collisions/reservations/history, same-document continuity and intended reference/exact-edition/pinned-snapshot effects. Preserve allocated/retired non-reuse and immutable historical selections; no arbitrary key reassignment orsilent retargeting.
4. Apply only the separately authorized scoped change with actual contributor/event provenance, appropriate working Version/Revision/history and coordinated transition evidence. Preserve earlier failed/pending events and original bytes; do not invent missing allocation, field, state orapproval facts.
5. Validate the resulting exact artifacts/editions in the subsequent appropriate operation. Record actual rules, checks, executor, observations, coverage/limits and remaining owner/consumer work; later changed inputs require new assessment. Local PASS is not complete implementation rollout, architectural approval, publication orBaseline membership.

For this review, REVIEW identifies findings without source modification; UPDATE persists the justified successor and pending corrections; VALIDATE examines those exact bytes later. Retain the pause between operations. The view does not collapse these phases orsubstitute for actual approval/selection authority.

DID-014§14's additive/backward-compatible/core-not-extensible restriction remains a real peer requirement pending responsible reconciliation with common assessed evolution. This protocol is not a silent waiver or an executed migration.

A Metadata Element is an individual architectural unit of Metadata representing one specific descriptive characteristic of a document.

# 5. Definition

A Metadata Element is the smallest indivisible architectural unit used to describe a document.

Each Metadata Element represents one descriptive concept.

Its semantic meaning is stable and independent of any implementation technology.

```text
Metadata Element

                    │

                    ├── Semantics
```

Provides the canonical architectural meaning.

## 9.2. Semantics

Defines how the Metadata Element shall be interpreted.

---

## 9.3. Value

Represents the information associated with a specific document.

literal_comparison_clauses.text:
# 6. Lifecycle States

## 6.1. Proposed

A Metadata artifact has been identified as necessary but has not yet been formally defined.

Characteristics:

- architectural proposal;
- no normative status;
- subject to review.

---

## 6.2. Defined

The Metadata artifact has received a complete architectural definition.

Characteristics:

- canonical definition exists;
- semantics established;
- under architectural review.

---

## 6.3. Approved

The Metadata artifact has been formally accepted by architectural governance.

Characteristics:

- approved semantics;
- approved structure;
- eligible for publication.

---

## 6.4. Published

The Metadata artifact becomes part of the official Documentation Framework.

Characteristics:

- normative status;
- publicly referenced;
- available for use by Metadata Profiles.

---

## 6.5. Deprecated

The Metadata artifact should no longer be used for new specifications.

Characteristics:

- retained for compatibility;
- superseded by newer Metadata;
- still documented.

Existing Metadata remains valid.

---

## 6.6. Retired

The Metadata artifact has reached the end of its architectural lifecycle.

Characteristics:

- no longer recommended;
- preserved for historical traceability;
- excluded from future Metadata Profiles.

Historical Metadata Instances remain interpretable.

---

# 7. Lifecycle Transitions

The permitted lifecycle transitions are:

```text

                Proposed
                    │
                    ▼

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

                Published
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

Reverse transitions shall not occur except through formal architectural governance.

---

# 8. Lifecycle Responsibilities

The Metadata Lifecycle defines responsibilities for each stage.

| Lifecycle Stage | Responsibility |
|-----------------|----------------|
| Proposed | Identify new Metadata requirements. |
| Defined | Produce canonical architectural definitions. |
| Approved | Validate architectural consistency. |
| Published | Make Metadata available for framework use. |
| Deprecated | Preserve compatibility while discouraging new usage. |
| Retired | Preserve historical reference only. |

---

# 10. Lifecycle Constraints

The Metadata Lifecycle shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 10.1. Controlled Introduction

New Metadata shall enter the lifecycle through the Proposed state.

---

## 10.2. No Implicit Approval

Metadata shall never become normative without explicit approval.

---

## 10.3. Semantic Preservation

Lifecycle transitions shall not redefine Metadata semantics.

---

## 10.4. Controlled Deprecation

Metadata shall not be removed immediately after deprecation.

---

## 10.5. Historical Preservation

Retired Metadata shall remain documented.

---

# 13. Relationship with Metadata Profiles

Metadata Profiles evolve independently from the Metadata Lifecycle.

A Metadata Profile may:

- adopt newly published Metadata;
- continue supporting deprecated Metadata;
- migrate to newer Metadata versions.

Profiles shall not alter the lifecycle status of Metadata.

---

# 1. Introduction

The Documentation Framework relies on Metadata to provide consistent, structured and reliable descriptions of documents.

To preserve architectural integrity, Metadata shall satisfy a set of validation rules that ensure compliance with the Metadata Architecture, Metadata Model and Metadata Schema.

This document defines the architectural principles governing Metadata Validation.

---

# 4. Validation Principles

Metadata Validation follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Architectural Validation

Validation verifies architectural conformance.

It shall not introduce new Metadata.

---

## 4.2. Deterministic Validation

Given the same Metadata and the same specification, validation shall always produce the same result.

---

## 4.3. Independent Validation

Validation shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 4.4. Non-Destructive Validation

Validation shall never modify Metadata.

It only evaluates conformance.

---

## 4.5. Explicit Validation

Validation outcomes shall be explicit and reproducible.

---

# 6. Validation Model

Conceptually.

```text

            Metadata Instance
                    │
                    ▼

           Metadata Validation
                    │
                    ├──────────────────────┐
                    ▼                      ▼
             Validation Rules      Validation Results

```

Validation evaluates Metadata against a predefined set of architectural rules.

---

# 9. Validation Process

Conceptually.

```text

            Metadata Instance
                    │
                    ▼

          Structural Validation
                    │
                    ▼

           Profile Validation
                    │
                    ▼

           Semantic Validation
                    │
                    ▼

         Consistency Validation
                    │
                    ▼

            Validation Result

```

Implementations may optimize execution while preserving equivalent validation outcomes.

---

# 10. Validation Results

Validation produces explicit outcomes.

Possible outcomes include:

- Valid
- Valid with Warnings
- Invalid

Validation Results shall include sufficient information to identify the violated validation rules.

---

# 11. Validation Severity

Validation findings may possess different severity levels.

Typical severity levels include:

- Information
- Warning
- Error
- Critical

Severity classification does not modify Metadata.

It supports architectural assessment.

---

# 12. Validation Constraints

Metadata Validation shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 12.1. Technology Independence

Validation shall not depend on implementation technologies.

---

## 12.2. Repeatability

Validation shall always produce reproducible results.

---

## 12.3. Traceability

Validation Results shall identify the Validation Rules that produced them.

---

## 12.4. Non-Intrusive

Validation shall never modify Metadata.

---

## 12.5. Architectural Consistency

Validation shall preserve the Documentation Framework architecture.

---

# 14. Relationship with Other Components

Metadata Validation collaborates with multiple architectural components.

| Component | Relationship |
|-----------|--------------|
| Metadata Schema | Defines structural validation rules. |
| Metadata Profiles | Define profile-specific validation. |
| Metadata Dictionary | Provides canonical Metadata definitions. |
| Governance | Consumes validation outcomes. |
| Workflow | May invoke validation during document evolution. |
| Automation | May execute validation automatically. |

Validation consumes architectural definitions but does not own them.

---

# 16. Architectural Characteristics

Metadata Validation possesses the following characteristics.

## 16.1. Deterministic

Validation outcomes are predictable.

---

## 16.2. Independent

Validation is implementation independent.

---

## 16.3. Extensible

New Validation Rules may be introduced without changing the Validation Architecture.

---

## 16.4. Traceable

Every Validation Result can be traced to one or more Validation Rules.

---

## 16.5. Reusable

Validation Rules may be reused across Metadata Profiles.

---

## 16.6. Non-Destructive

Validation never alters Metadata.

---

## 18.2. Metadata

# 1. Introduction

Metadata is a strategic architectural asset of the Documentation Framework.

To preserve its integrity, consistency and long-term stability, Metadata shall be governed through a controlled architectural governance process.

Metadata Governance establishes the policies, responsibilities and decision mechanisms required to manage the evolution of Metadata while preserving the architectural principles of the Documentation Framework.

---

# 4. Governance Principles

Metadata Governance follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Architectural Authority

All Metadata shall be governed according to the Documentation Framework architecture.

---

## 4.2. Controlled Evolution

Metadata shall evolve only through explicit architectural decisions.

---

## 4.3. Traceability

Governance decisions shall be documented and traceable.

---

## 4.4. Consistency

Governance shall preserve conceptual consistency throughout the Metadata architecture.

---

## 4.5. Stability

Existing Metadata shall remain stable whenever possible.

---

## 4.6. Transparency

Governance decisions shall be explicit and reproducible.

---

# 6. Governance Model

Conceptually.

```text

             Metadata Change
                    │
                    ▼

          Governance Evaluation
                    │
                    ▼

         Architectural Decision
                    │
                    ├──────────────────────┐
                    ▼                      ▼
                 Approved              Rejected
                    │
                    ▼

            Metadata Evolution
```

Governance evaluates proposed changes without modifying Metadata directly.

---

# 10. Governance Process

Conceptually.

```text

                Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

          Architectural Review
                    │
                    ▼

         Consistency Assessment
                    │
                    ▼

             Impact Analysis
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision
                    │
                    ▼

               Publication

```

The governance process is technology independent.

---

# 11. Governance Outcomes

Governance produces explicit decisions.

Possible outcomes include:

- Approved
- Approved with Conditions
- Deferred
- Rejected
- Deprecated

Each decision shall include its justification.

---

# 12. Governance Constraints

Metadata Governance shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 12.1. Architectural Independence

Governance shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 12.2. Explicit Decisions

Implicit governance decisions shall not exist.

---

## 12.3. Traceable Decisions

Every governance decision shall be documented.

---

## 12.4. Controlled Authority

Only approved Metadata becomes part of the canonical Metadata architecture.

---

## 12.5. Preservation

Governance shall preserve existing Metadata whenever reasonably possible.

---

# 14. Relationship with Metadata Lifecycle

Metadata Governance controls lifecycle transitions.

Examples include:

- Proposed → Defined
- Defined → Approved
- Approved → Published
- Published → Deprecated
- Deprecated → Retired

The Metadata Lifecycle defines the states.

Metadata Governance authorizes transitions between those states.

# 15. Relationship with Metadata Validation

Metadata Validation determines whether Metadata conforms to the Metadata specification.

Metadata Governance determines whether Metadata should become part of the Documentation Framework.

Validation answers:

> "Is the Metadata compliant?"

Governance answers:

> "Should the Metadata be accepted?"

The two responsibilities are complementary but independent.

---

# 16. Relationship with Other Components

| Component | Relationship |
|-----------|--------------|
| Metadata Lifecycle | Governance authorizes lifecycle transitions. |
| Metadata Validation | Validation provides evidence for governance decisions. |
| Metadata Dictionary | Governance approves Metadata definitions. |
| Metadata Schema | Governance approves structural evolution. |
| Metadata Profiles | Governance authorizes new profiles. |
| Architecture | Governance preserves architectural consistency. |

Governance consumes architectural information but does not redefine it.

---

# 18. Architectural Characteristics

Metadata Governance possesses the following characteristics.

## 18.1. Authoritative

Governance produces authoritative architectural decisions.

---

## 18.2. Traceable

Every decision is documented.

---

## 18.3. Deterministic

Equivalent governance criteria shall produce equivalent decisions.

---

## 18.4. Independent

Governance remains independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 18.5. Extensible

New governance processes may be introduced without altering the Metadata architecture.

---

## 18.6. Stable

Governance protects the long-term stability of Metadata.

---

# 20. Related Documents

## 20.1. Architecture

- DF-ARC-001 — Architecture Overview
- DF-ARC-002 — Architectural Principles
- DF-ARC-005 — Architectural Components

## 20.2. Metadata

- DF-MTD-009 — Metadata Relationships
- DF-MTD-010 — Metadata Constraints
- DF-MTD-013 — Metadata Dictionary
- DF-MTD-014 — Metadata Specification

---

**End of Document**

# 4. Relationship Principles

Metadata Relationships follow the principles below.

## 4.1. Explicitness

Every relationship shall have an explicit architectural meaning.

---

## 4.2. Semantic Stability

Relationships shall preserve the semantics of the related concepts.

---

## 4.3. Directionality

Every relationship shall define its source and target.

---

## 4.4. Independence

Relationships shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 4.5. Non-Redundancy

Equivalent relationships shall not coexist.

---

# 5. Relationship Model

Conceptually.

```text
Metadata
                    │
                    ├──────────────────────┐
                    ▼                      ▼
                Metadata               Metadata
                 Schema                 Profile
                    │                      │
                    ▼                      ▼
                Metadata                Metadata
                 Element                Instance
                    │
                    ▼

             Metadata Value
```

The Metadata Relationship Model describes how Metadata concepts are connected while preserving their responsibilities.

---

# 8. Specialization Relationships

Specialization relationships express refinement.

Examples include:

| Source | Relationship | Target |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| Metadata Profile | specializes | Metadata Schema |
| Extended Metadata | specializes | Standard Metadata |

Specialization preserves the semantics of the parent concept while introducing controlled constraints.

---

# 9. Association Relationships

Association relationships express logical connections without ownership.

Examples include:

| Source | Relationship | Target |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| Metadata Element | is described by | Metadata Dictionary |
| Metadata Profile | references | Metadata Groups |
| Metadata Schema | organizes | Metadata Groups |

Associations preserve independence between architectural entities.

---

# 10. Dependency Relationships

Dependency relationships identify architectural reliance.

Examples include:

| Source | Depends On |
|----------|------------|
| Metadata Validation | Metadata Schema |
| Metadata Validation | Metadata Profiles |
| Metadata Governance | Metadata Lifecycle |
| Metadata Dictionary | Metadata Elements |

Dependencies shall never introduce circular architectural dependencies.

---

# 13. Relationship Constraints

Metadata Relationships shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 13.1. No Semantic Modification

Relationships shall not redefine Metadata concepts.

---

## 13.2. No Ownership Transfer

Relationships shall not transfer architectural responsibilities.

---

## 13.3. No Circular Dependencies

Architectural dependency cycles shall not exist.

---

## 13.4. Canonical Relationships

Equivalent relationships shall possess one authoritative definition.

---

## 13.5. Consistency

Relationships shall preserve Metadata architectural consistency.

---

# 4. Constraint Principles

Metadata Constraints follow the principles below.

## 4.1. Architectural Integrity

Constraints shall preserve the integrity of the Metadata architecture.

---

## 4.2. Technology Independence

Constraints shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 4.3. Stability

Constraints shall preserve long-term architectural stability.

---

## 4.4. Explicit Definition

Every constraint shall possess an explicit architectural meaning.

---

## 4.5. Verifiability

Constraints shall be objectively verifiable.

---

# 5. Constraint Categories

The Metadata component defines five categories of constraints.

- Conceptual Constraints
- Structural Constraints
- Semantic Constraints
- Evolution Constraints
- Dependency Constraints

Each category governs a specific aspect of the Metadata architecture.

---

# 7. Structural Constraints

Structural Constraints govern the organization of Metadata.

## 7.1. S-001 — Canonical Schema

There shall be one authoritative Metadata Schema.

---

## 7.2. S-002 — Element Organization

Metadata Elements shall be organized exclusively through the Metadata Schema.

---

## 7.3. S-003 — Profile Specialization

Metadata Profiles shall specialize, but never redefine, the Metadata Schema.

---

## 7.4. S-004 — Structural Consistency

Metadata organization shall remain internally consistent.

---

# 8. Semantic Constraints

Semantic Constraints preserve the meaning of Metadata.

## 8.1. M-001 — Stable Semantics

Metadata Elements shall preserve their semantic meaning throughout their lifecycle.

---

## 8.2. M-002 — No Semantic Overloading

A Metadata Element shall represent one concept only.

---

## 8.3. M-003 — Semantic Preservation

Structural organization shall never alter semantic meaning.

---

## 8.4. M-004 — Canonical Interpretation

Metadata shall possess one authoritative interpretation.

---

# 9. Evolution Constraints

Evolution Constraints preserve compatibility over time.

## 9.1. E-001 — Controlled Evolution

Metadata shall evolve only through architectural governance.

---

## 9.2. E-002 — Backward Compatibility

Metadata evolution shall preserve compatibility whenever reasonably possible.

---

## 9.3. E-003 — Controlled Deprecation

Metadata shall be deprecated before retirement.

---

## 9.4. E-004 — Historical Preservation

Deprecated and retired Metadata shall remain documented.

---

# 10. Dependency Constraints

Dependency Constraints regulate architectural dependencies.

## 10.1. D-001 — No Circular Dependencies

Circular dependencies between Metadata artifacts shall not exist.

---

## 10.2. D-002 — Explicit Dependencies

Dependencies shall be explicitly documented.

---

## 10.3. D-003 — Dependency Stability

Dependencies shall preserve architectural stability.

---

## 10.4. D-004 — Responsibility Preservation

Dependencies shall not transfer architectural responsibilities.

---

# 12. Constraint Enforcement

Metadata Constraints define architectural obligations.

Enforcement mechanisms are intentionally outside the scope of this specification.

Constraint enforcement may be performed by:

- Metadata Validation;
- Metadata Governance;
- implementation-specific mechanisms.

The architectural constraints themselves remain implementation independent.

---

# 6. Conceptual Constraints

Conceptual Constraints preserve the meaning of Metadata concepts.

## 6.1. C-001 — Unique Concept Definition

Every Metadata concept shall possess exactly one canonical definition.

---

## 6.2. C-002 — Single Responsibility

Each Metadata concept shall represent one architectural responsibility only.

---

## 6.3. C-003 — Concept Independence

Metadata concepts shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 6.4. C-004 — Non-Redundancy

Equivalent Metadata concepts shall not coexist.

---

# 11. Constraint Relationships

The different constraint categories complement one another.

```text

          Conceptual Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

          Structural Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

          Semantic Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

          Evolution Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

          Dependency Constraints

```

Together they define the architectural boundaries of the Metadata component.

---

# 14. Relationship with Other Metadata Documents

Metadata Constraints provide the architectural boundaries for the remaining Metadata specifications.

| Document | Relationship |
|----------|--------------|
| Metadata Concepts | Defines constrained concepts. |
| Metadata Model | Organizes constrained concepts. |
| Metadata Elements | Defines constrained building blocks. |
| Metadata Schema | Applies structural constraints. |
| Metadata Lifecycle | Applies evolution constraints. |
| Metadata Validation | Verifies constraint compliance. |
| Metadata Governance | Controls constraint evolution. |

---

# 15. Architectural Characteristics

Metadata Constraints possess the following characteristics.

## 15.1. Canonical

There is one authoritative set of Metadata Constraints.

---

## 15.2. Stable

Constraints evolve only through controlled governance.

---

## 15.3. Technology Independent

Constraints remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 15.4. Deterministic

Constraint evaluation shall produce consistent outcomes.

---

## 15.5. Traceable

Every constraint shall possess a stable architectural identity.

---

## 15.6. Extensible

New constraints may be introduced without invalidating existing constraints.

---

# 17. Related Documents

## 17.1. Architecture

- DF-ARC-002 — Architectural Principles
- DF-ARC-003 — Architectural Concepts
- DF-ARC-005 — Architectural Components

## 17.2. Metadata

- DF-MTD-001 — Metadata Architecture
- DF-MTD-002 — Metadata Concepts
- DF-MTD-003 — Metadata Model
- DF-MTD-004 — Metadata Elements
- DF-MTD-005 — Metadata Schema

- DF-MTD-007 — Metadata Validation
- DF-MTD-008 — Metadata Governance
- DF-MTD-009 — Metadata Relationships
- DF-MTD-011 — Metadata Extensibility
- DF-MTD-013 — Metadata Dictionary
- DF-MTD-014 — Metadata Specification

---

**End of Document**
