# 4. Extensibility Principles

Metadata Extensibility follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Architectural Stability

Extensions shall preserve the stability of the Metadata architecture.

---

## 4.2. Backward Compatibility

Extensions shall not invalidate existing Metadata.

---

## 4.3. Canonical Preservation

Extensions shall preserve canonical Metadata definitions.

---

## 4.4. Technology Independence

Extension mechanisms shall remain implementation independent.

---

## 4.5. Controlled Evolution

Extensions shall be introduced only through architectural governance.

---

# 8. Extension Categories

Metadata extensions may belong to one of the following categories.

## 8.1. Additive Extension

Introduces new Metadata without affecting existing Metadata.

Preferred extension mechanism.

---

## 8.2. Specialization Extension

Creates specialized Metadata Profiles derived from the canonical Metadata Schema.

---

## 8.3. Organizational Extension

Introduces new Metadata Groups to improve structural organization.

---

## 8.4. Evolutionary Extension

Introduces architectural refinements through controlled Metadata evolution.

---

# 9. Extension Constraints

Metadata extensions shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 9.1. E-001 — No Semantic Redefinition

Existing Metadata semantics shall not be modified.

---

## 9.2. E-002 — No Responsibility Transfer

Extensions shall not alter architectural responsibilities.

---

## 9.3. E-003 — No Architectural Fragmentation

Extensions shall preserve a single canonical Metadata architecture.

---

## 9.4. E-004 — Compatibility Preservation

Extensions shall preserve interoperability whenever reasonably possible.

---

## 9.5. E-005 — Governance Approval

Every extension shall be approved through Metadata Governance.

---

# 10. Extension Process

Conceptually.

```text

            Extension Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

           Architecture Review
                    │
                    ▼

             Impact Analysis
                    │
                    ▼

        Compatibility Assessment
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Approval
                    │
                    ▼

            Metadata Evolution

```

The extension process is independent of implementation technologies.

---

# 13. Relationship with Metadata Validation

Metadata Validation verifies that extensions conform to the Metadata architecture.

Validation does not authorize extensions.

Authorization belongs to Metadata Governance.

---

## 15.3. Compatible

Extensions maintain interoperability.

---

# 5. Conceptual Principles

## 5.1. AP-001 — Documentation as Knowledge

Documentation shall represent organized knowledge through logical entities, identified sources and applicable contracts. A file is a representation, not automatically a registered capability or a complete knowledge system. Normalized sources and functional files contribute within their respective scopes; DF defines documentary requirements while an applicable process produces/manages representations.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess purpose, actual source organization, relationships and coverage. The principle creates neither a document component nor proof that every file contributes complete or consistent knowledge.

---

## 5.2. AP-002 — Explicit Architecture

Architectural decisions shall identify the subject, scope, responsible owners, assumptions, applicable contracts and rationale explicitly. Significant allocation, classification, identity or required-contract changes require previous/new mapping and affected editions before propagation. Record unresolved decisions or missing evidence rather than treating an implicit label, arrow or directory as authority.

**Evidence boundary:** Examine actual decision/owner/reference records and limits. Explicit documentation proves neither approval nor complete implementation; derived summaries preserve authoritative provenance.

---

## 5.3. AP-003 — Technology Independence

Architectural definitions shall avoid prescribing technology unless an explicit integration constraint requires it. Logical identity, classification and domain meaning are distinct from filenames, formats, repositories and storage technology. Actual implementations still require representations, adapters, interfaces and executors under their applicable contracts.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess declared technology constraints and actual representation/adapter compatibility. Conceptual independence does not guarantee every format/tool is suitable, an implementation exists or technologies can evolve without consumer impact.

---

## 5.4. AP-004 — Single Source of Truth

Each semantic concept or authoritative record shall have one identified responsible owner within its declared domain/scope. Metadata Dictionary defines descriptor meaning while Identity, Classification and Governance retain their domain semantics. Traceable summaries, catalogs and projections may repeat derived values with source-edition provenance and refresh/state limits without acquiring competing authority.

**Evidence boundary:** Check responsible definition/record sources, derived-copy provenance and unresolved conflicts. Logical single authority does not require one physical copy, a universal Registry route or a complete canonical catalog merely from this principle.

---

## 5.5. AP-005 — Semantic Consistency

Consuming representations shall preserve applicable owner meanings and identify subjects/qualified contexts. Controlled aliases and historic vocabulary retain explicit mappings; unqualified overloads or competing meanings are recorded and reconciled. Metadata represents domain values, Schema organizes references, Profile constrains usage and Instance provides values under one effective Profile without redefining semantics.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess actual definitions, profiles, represented values and consumer scope. This principle does not manufacture missing Element/Profile records or prove consistency of unseen sources.

---

# 6. Structural Principles

## 6.1. AP-006 — Separation of Responsibilities

Each registered capability shall have a defined primary semantic responsibility and primary allocation. Explicit collaboration, cross-cutting participation, shared check domains and traceable projections are permitted while preserving owner boundaries. Reviews may use Validation/Consistency Verification results without acquiring their rule ownership or approval authority.

**Evidence boundary:** Check primary owner/consumer contracts and actual support interactions. Prevent competing semantics rather than prohibiting every overlap of supporting work; no new capability or reassignment is inferred from a concern or directory.

---

## 6.2. AP-007 — Layered Architecture

Structural allocation shall follow Architectural Layers:seven areas are Foundation, Architecture, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Automation and Integration. Foundation/Architecture supply supporting definitions; the supplied 23 capabilities retain their 4/4/5/5/5 allocation. Five conceptual concerns—Knowledge, Documentation, Governance, Discovery and Preservation—are a different view.

**Evidence boundary:** For required cross-Layer consumption, record consumer→provider contract/scope/source editions and apply the declared support order:the provider precedes its consumer. Same-Layer requirements, including Knowledge Graph→Relationships and Workflow→Policies, need explicit interfaces/ownership and cycle assessment. There is no obligation to consume every earlier provider or an adjacent serial service chain. Genuine required cycles are prohibited in the governed scope and remain visible for reconciliation; no projection/reference label hides them. Changing constraints requires assessed architectural revision, not an arbitrary upward exception. These rules certify neither a full graph nor implemented layer services.

---

## 6.3. AP-008 — Modular Design

Components shall preserve coherent boundaries and compatible provider contracts where feasible. Separate areas or documents may still require coordinated content/descriptor, owner/consumer or release changes. Independent evolution is an assessed objective under actual dependencies, not an unconditional guarantee.

**Evidence boundary:** Map affected exact editions, provider compatibility and transition evidence. A new component or module label alone proves neither independent release nor operational modularity.

---

## 6.4. AP-009 — Explicit Relationships

Applicable connections shall be explicitly typed with identified endpoints and provenance. Distinguish documentary authority references, semantic associations, representation/projection, navigation, required consumption and execution. A required edge names consumer, provider, contract, scope and responsible source editions; physical directories, names and visual order alone establish no edge.

**Evidence boundary:** Check actual connection records and resolvable endpoints. Preserve genuine requirements/cycles visibly and reconcile conflicting owner contracts; do not rename an indispensable provider as navigation to create apparent acyclicity. This principle imposes no nonempty relationship list on every file.

---

## 6.5. AP-010 — Stable Identity

Normalized documents shall preserve valid permanent logical identity under the applicable Domain+Identifier allocation/preservation contract. Identifier representation, current classification, title, Version/Revision, Status and physical location are distinct facts. Existing valid DF-SSS-NNN allocations do not automatically change with Family/Type or path; necessary migration needs a mapped assessed identity change.

**Evidence boundary:** Apply the functional-file exclusion in §3 first:README.md, CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md require no normalized ID by this principle. Assess actual uniqueness/resolution and collision evidence; no 000 functional identity, missing allocation or universal generation algorithm is invented.

---

# 8. Evolution Principles

## 8.1. AP-015 — Incremental Evolution

Prefer incremental architectural improvement where it can meet actual requirements while preserving compatible meaning. A necessary larger or foundational change can be justified when incremental alternatives cannot adequately satisfy identified responsibilities or constraints.

**Evidence boundary:** Record previous/new contracts, alternatives/rationale, affected owners/consumers, dependencies and transition/verification evidence. Avoid disruption where feasible without an absolute ban on justified incompatible reconciliation.

---

## 8.2. AP-016 — Backward Compatibility

Preserve compatible meaning and provider/consumer contracts where feasible. Necessary incompatible changes shall be explicitly justified with affected exact editions, previous/new mappings, reference/identity effects, transition evidence and verification limits. Compatibility is assessed from contracts, not from names, folder layout or a Version label alone.

**Evidence boundary:** For this working document review, compatible correction retains Version; compatible additive capability increments minor; incompatible contract change increments major and resets minor to 0. Every changed persisted edition increments Revision monotonically across Version changes. Validation of unchanged source changes neither coordinate and is tracked centrally. Domain-specific entity numbering requires its own qualified owner; no completed consumer rollout is inferred.

---

## 8.3. AP-017 — Extensibility

Introduce a new capability or source role only for a demonstrated need with defined owner responsibility, primary allocation, typed interactions and consumer impact. Reuse or extend existing contracts where feasible. Necessary changes to foundations, responsibilities or interfaces are permitted through the assessed evolution process in AP-015/016 and §14; extension-only is not an absolute prohibition on foundational revision.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess whether existing meaning/functionality changes, actual dependencies and transition evidence. A new capability is not assumed harmless and need not create another Layer. No component, Metadata Element, Profile or specification is fabricated merely to make an extension appear complete.

---

## 8.4. AP-018 — Architectural Stability

Preserve coherent conceptual boundaries and compatible owner meanings where feasible. Implementation technologies can evolve under applicable representation/provider/consumer contracts; their independence is not guaranteed by conceptual separation. Necessary semantic changes retain source history and explicit compatibility/version transition.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess actual contracts, affected editions and integration/adapter constraints. Stability is a controlled design objective, not foundation immutability, harmless extension or a guarantee of unchanged semantics for every future edition.

---

# 4. Principle Classification

The five categories organize the principles below; they are not document Type values, registered components or structural Layers. All 24 AP IDs, titles and original category membership are preserved.

| Category | Responsibility | Retained IDs |
|---|---|---|
| Conceptual Principles | Knowledge representation, explicit architecture, technology and semantic ownership | AP-001–AP-005 |
| Structural Principles | Primary responsibilities, allocation, interfaces and identity | AP-006–AP-010 |
| Governance Principles | Subject lifecycle, traceability, controlled changes and exact immutable selection | AP-011–AP-014 |
| Evolution Principles | Incremental/compatible-where-feasible evolution and assessed necessary incompatibility | AP-015–AP-018 |
| Quality Principles | Evidence-limited simplicity, consistency, maintenance, discovery, checking and reuse | AP-019–AP-024 |

---

# 5. Documentation Components

Documentation represents Knowledge through descriptive, logical-identity, classification and reusable-structure contracts. Its four capabilities retain separate semantic ownership while contributing to Governance, Discovery and Preservation.

---

## 5.1. Metadata

### 5.1.1. Purpose

Represents structured descriptors for identified documentary entities/editions under applicable owner contracts.

---

### 5.1.2. Responsibilities

Describe documents and support identity, classification, governance and discovery by represented values/references. Document Identity, Classification and Governance retain their domain meanings. Dictionary defines descriptors, Schema organizes references, Profile constrains usage and Instance supplies values under one effective Profile. Coordinated content/descriptor evolution is permitted; no catalog/Profile or mandatory absent value is invented.

---

## 5.2. Document Identity

### 5.2.1. Purpose

Defines stable logical document identity and its applicable allocation/preservation contracts.

---

### 5.2.2. Responsibilities

For normalized documents in scope, distinguish logical domain identity from exact edition, mutable Family/Type, physical location, Status and membership. Adopted corpus DF-SSS-NNN series are stable allocation namespaces independent of current classification; this overview performs no migration or allocation. The functional exclusions in §3 apply before normalized identity obligations. Traceability requires actual identified editions/references, not a guarantee inferred from this purpose.

---

## 5.3. Classification

### 5.3.1. Purpose

Defines semantic category meaning and applicable documentary assignments.

---

### 5.3.2. Responsibilities

Classify normalized documents using a canonical component or admitted documentary-area Family and exactly one responsibility-based Type from Architecture, Structure, Behavior, Reference. Optional Class requires an explicit definition. Classification supports governance/discovery without owning their state/approval or search semantics. Mutable classification is distinct from permanent identity, primary component allocation and physical storage; detailed owner reconciliation remains pending.

---

## 5.4. Templates

### 5.4.1. Purpose

Defines reusable documentary representations and their applicable structural constraints.

---

### 5.4.2. Responsibilities

Standardize structure and support creation through explicit types, schemas, elements, parameters and constraints. A Template definition differs from a concrete document instance. Templates references Metadata, Identity and Classification meanings rather than redefining them; it does not own workflow, policy, Baseline, Registry or storage semantics. Consistency and conformance require actual checks against the applicable contracts, not automatic success from using a template.

---

# 6. Governance Components

Governance defines documentary lifecycle, policy, review and immutable snapshot contracts. It does not itself prove an implemented process engine. Exact-edition review, validation, approval, publication and membership are distinct decisions/events.

---

## 6.1. Workflow

### 6.1.1. Purpose

Defines exact-edition lifecycle, transition, responsibility and evidence contracts.

---

### 6.1.2. Responsibilities

Describe documentary state transitions and publication conditions under applicable Policies. A DMS, tool or manual process executes operations; CMS governs changes in its own scope. Logical identity, Version/Revision, exact Status, approval/publication and membership are separate. Illustrative states do not create an unconditional transition graph; older approvals do not approve Draft successors.

---

## 6.2. Policies

### 6.2.1. Purpose

Defines applicable documentary governance rules and evidence requirements.

---

### 6.2.2. Responsibilities

State review, publication, approval and maintenance policies with applicability and responsible authorities. Rules govern identified editions and operations; actual author contribution, authorization, review, validation and approval remain distinct. Policy definition does not prove implementation, grant an operation automatically or replace semantic owners in other domains.

---

## 6.3. Reviews

### 6.3.1. Purpose

Defines review responsibilities and records examined scope, observations and findings.

---

### 6.3.2. Responsibilities

Technical and architectural review assess exact identified artifacts/rules and consistency within recorded coverage. Reviews may use results from Validation or Consistency Verification, whose executors record applicable checks; overlapping check domains do not create competing semantics or approval authority. A review result is evidence, not an approval, publication decision, Baseline selection or guarantee of product consequences.

---

## 6.4. Baselines

### 6.4.1. Purpose

Defines separately identified immutable selections of exact approved document editions.

---

### 6.4.2. Responsibilities

Preserve explicit selected member identity/edition coordinates and relevant pinned relationship context or traceable verification evidence. Approval eligibility, consistency and actual inclusion are separate checks. Release snapshots and historical traceability require scope and selection evidence; a current path or time label alone is insufficient. Draft successors do not retarget older members or inherit membership. This UPDATE creates no Baseline or missing historic approval.

---

# 7. Discovery Components

Discovery defines typed connections, catalog/network projections and access to identified entities/editions. Directories remain physical locations rather than semantic authority. Draft, historical and snapshot-specific discovery is allowed with explicit state and scope; discoverability does not confer approval.

---

## 7.1. Registry

### 7.1.1. Purpose

Defines catalog/lookup authority for its declared entity/edition scope.

---

### 7.1.2. Responsibilities

Support registration, lookup and discoverability through traceable authoritative source-edition records/projections. Catalog authority does not replace identity, classification, governance or relationship-record meaning. Derived copies retain provenance, refresh and current/stale/historical/snapshot context. Cataloguing does not make Registry an indispensable intermediary for every component or require physical single-copy storage.

---

## 7.2. Relationships

### 7.2.1. Purpose

Defines typed connection records for identified endpoints and their provenance.

---

### 7.2.2. Responsibilities

Map and preserve semantic reference, association, replacement, navigation and required-dependency kinds as applicable. Endpoint domains and identity contracts follow their entity kinds; not every endpoint gets a normalized document ID. Required edges use consumer→provider contract/scope and remain visible, including genuine cycles requiring reconciliation. Explicit records support traceability without fabricating a complete relation catalog.

---

## 7.3. Knowledge Graph

### 7.3.1. Purpose

Defines traceable semantic-network projections of identified entities and typed Relationships records.

---

### 7.3.2. Responsibilities

Support semantic navigation, dependency and impact analysis with authoritative source/edition provenance. Derived values do not acquire competing semantic authority; views declare refresh/freshness and current/historical/snapshot scope. No universal Registry-to-Graph routing or complete network/acyclicity is inferred from this capability.

---

## 7.4. Navigation

### 7.4.1. Purpose

Defines logical access through declared entity/edition and relationship views.

---

### 7.4.2. Responsibilities

Support hierarchical/contextual navigation and cross references with resolvable identified targets, state and relevant freshness context. Sources and relation meanings are explicit; navigation does not automatically impose a provider service dependency, confer approval or replace physical storage contracts.

---

## 7.5. Search

### 7.5.1. Purpose

Defines discovery of identified architectural entities through declared indexes/views.

---

### 7.5.2. Responsibilities

Support document, Metadata and semantic search with source-edition provenance and freshness/state limits. Draft and historical results are distinguished from approved/snapshot members. Intended search neither certifies completeness nor requires a universal Registry pipeline or new semantic owner.

---

# 8. Automation Components

Automation defines intended repeatable checking/generation capabilities. Applicable implementations consume authoritative owner contracts on identified inputs and provide execution evidence; architectural definitions alone establish neither installed tools nor verified outcomes.

---

## 8.1. Validation

### 8.1.1. Purpose

Defines scoped evaluation of identified requirements against exact artifacts/editions.

---

### 8.1.2. Responsibilities

Cover Metadata, identity, relationship and consistency requirements supplied by their responsible owners. Actual execution records inputs, rules, checks, observations, coverage, executor and limits. A PASS neither guarantees global correctness nor approves/publishes/selects a Baseline; subsequent changed bytes need their own assessment.

---

## 8.2. Metadata Generator

### 8.2.1. Purpose

Defines generation/completion/synchronization of descriptor representations under applicable owner rules.

---

### 8.2.2. Responsibilities

Identify exact inputs, output edition/representation, applicable Dictionary/Schema/Profile and provenance. Completion derives or requests values through declared rules; it is not permission to invent absent identity, category, lifecycle or approval facts. Generated values require applicable constraint assessment and synchronization/refresh evidence. Capability definition alone proves no implemented generator or successful result.

---

## 8.3. Registry Generator

### 8.3.1. Purpose

Defines creation/update of scoped Registry projections from authoritative source records/editions.

---

### 8.3.2. Responsibilities

Declare source/input and generated-output provenance, applicable catalog/owner rules and refresh/current-stale handling. Consistency checks state examined records, coverage and limits; generation does not replace domain or relationship-record authority. No implemented synchronization service or automatic complete catalog is inferred.

---

## 8.4. Documentation Generator

### 8.4.1. Purpose

Defines generation of documentary artifacts from identified definitions/inputs.

---

### 8.4.2. Responsibilities

Support table-of-contents, index and navigation artifact generation under applicable representation and owner contracts. Record input/output editions, referenced targets and provenance; verify relevant constraints/references in scope. Generated artifacts are representations, not new semantic authorities or automatically approved publications.

---

## 8.5. Consistency Verification

### 8.5.1. Purpose

Defines scoped cross-record/contract verification under applicable authoritative requirements.

---

### 8.5.2. Responsibilities

Check dependency, relationship and architectural consistency against declared records/editions and actual typed requirements. Record executor, examined scope, observations and limits. Shared check domains with Validation/Reviews do not imply competing rule ownership or global integrity; a partial matrix cannot certify the complete framework graph.

---

# 9. Integration Components

Integration defines optional use-case adapters to supported external environments and interfaces. Adapters consume owner/authorization contracts without becoming new semantic owners or approvers. Describing integration does not establish its implementation, completeness, performance or mandatory use.

---

## 9.1. Source Control Integration

### 9.1.1. Purpose

Defines an adapter to supported source-control provenance and versioned representations. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

---

## 9.2. CI/CD Integration

### 9.2.1. Purpose

Defines delivery-pipeline adapters executing scoped checks and authorized publication for identified editions. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

---

## 9.3. IDE Integration

### 9.3.1. Purpose

Defines supported authoring/development adapters under applicable representation and owner contracts. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

---

## 9.4. Documentation Platform Integration

### 9.4.1. Purpose

Defines platform publication adapters following Governance authorization for the exact edition. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

---

## 9.5. AI Integration

### 9.5.1. Purpose

Defines assisted reasoning/authoring against identified domain contracts and source evidence. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred. AI assistance does not acquire domain-semantic or approval authority. Actual contribution and examined bytes are recorded separately from user authorization; later human/tool edits require resulting-byte assessment without inherited results or product-consequence responsibility.

---

# 12. Component Dependencies

A required dependency is directed **consumer→provider** and identifies the provider contract needed in a declared scope. Documentary authority reference, semantic association, projection, navigation and execution are distinct meanings; visual position does not identify required edges.

Apply Layers V2.0 R1 §§12–13: support order is Foundation, Architecture, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Automation, Integration. A required cross-Layer provider precedes its consumer in that declared order; lower/higher means support precedence, not page position. Same-Layer contracts require explicit interfaces/ownership and cycle assessment. The rule does not require every earlier-area provider or an adjacent serial service chain; changing the constraint requires an assessed architectural revision, not an arbitrary upward exception.

<!-- original-section-view: 12 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §12 — Selected required contracts; consumer→provider.**

| Consumer | Consumer area | Provider | Provider area | Required contract | Scope/justification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | Discovery | Metadata | Documentation | Descriptive values with source-edition provenance | When indexing edition descriptors; refresh or identify stale values |
| Knowledge Graph | Discovery | Document Identity | Documentation | Entity identity for logical document nodes | When keying document nodes; other entity kinds use their own endpoint identity contracts |
| Knowledge Graph | Discovery | Relationships | Discovery | Typed connection records and provenance | When projecting the semantic network and interpreting dependency kinds |
| Workflow | Governance | Metadata | Documentation | Represented state/edition descriptors | When interpreting documentary state values for a governance transition |
| Workflow | Governance | Policies | Governance | Applicable transition and evidence rules | When deciding permitted governance operations; execution remains with the applicable process |
| Baselines | Governance | Document Identity | Documentation | Logical member identity | When selecting/preserving document-edition members |
| Baselines | Governance | Metadata | Documentation | Exact edition-reference/descriptive contract | When selecting/preserving exact editions; relevant relationship context must also be pinned or evidenced |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

These seven selected contracts preserve Concepts V2.0 R1 §8 and Layers V2.0 R1 §12, consistent with Blueprint §8.11. Knowledge Graph→Relationships and Workflow→Policies are same-Layer requirements. They are scoped architectural declarations, not a verified complete graph, implementation inventory or execution sequence.

Circular required dependencies between components, within/across areas, are prohibited in the governed contract scope. Assess actual edges and owner/consumer evidence. A genuine indispensable contract/cycle must remain visible and be reconciled; do not conceal it by changing a relationship label. Documentary definition references do not automatically require an upper-area runtime service, and semantic ownership cannot be reassigned merely to make a graph appear acyclic.

The complete graph requires detailed owner-source reconciliation and context-specific requirements beyond these rows. This source certifies neither global acyclicity nor integrated consumer compatibility.

---

# 15. Evolution Guidelines

A new component requires a demonstrated responsibility that existing capabilities cannot adequately cover, an explicit primary allocation, coherent domain ownership and typed interactions. Assess dependency constraints, intended reuse and consumers before introduction; a new component need not create a new Layer.

Existing responsibility, interface or allocation changes require previous/new mapping, rationale, affected source editions, compatibility assessment and transition evidence. Preserve compatible meaning where feasible. Necessary incompatible changes are explicitly justified; no independent-release or harmless-extension guarantee applies.

For this working review, compatible correction retains Version; compatible additive capability increments minor; incompatible contract change increments major and resets minor to 0. Every changed persisted edition increments Revision monotonically across Version changes. Validation with unchanged source retains both coordinates and is tracked centrally. A version number alone does not reconcile consuming sources or complete integrated checks.

---

# 5. Component Directory Structure

A **complete component documentation set** shall provide README.md and the four category directories below. This is an organization requirement, not proof that all required content exists or is correct. The same contract applies to every component; partial supplied sets must be identified as incomplete rather than silently exempted or certified.

<!-- original-section-view: 5 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §5 — Physical component documentation organization.**

| Entry relative to the component root | Kind | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| README.md | Non-normalized file | Entry point, source map, scope and coverage information |
| 01-Architecture/ | Directory | Conceptual foundations, principles, models and decisions |
| 02-Structure/ | Directory | Organization, schemas, composition, relationships and structural restrictions/catalogs |
| 03-Behavior/ | Directory | Subject-specific lifecycle, validation, governance, processes and extensibility |
| 04-Reference/ | Directory | Consolidated specifications, consultation, terminology, examples and recommendations |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

Applicable documents are placed according to primary responsibility. Titles such as Schema, Dictionary, Lifecycle and Specification are role names, not additional Type values or automatic placement rules. A directory does not assign semantic authority, change Family or recalculate identity.

An empty directory satisfies only its presence check, not content coverage. Do not manufacture empty documents or an implemented capability to make a set appear complete. Required source roles and unfilled responsibilities are assessed under §16. The received corpus may contain partial sets; that evidence records an unmet requirement, not an exception to this contract.

---

# 6. Component README

Every complete component documentation set shall provide README.md as its functional entry point. It remains non-normalized under §3.

Its content shall identify the component, purpose, responsibilities, scope and primary architectural position; map actual supplied documents and relevant editions; distinguish present, planned, absent and not-applicable roles with evidence; identify owner references, dependencies/related components, applicable roadmap and conformance coverage. A recommended reading order may be given where useful, with advisory meaning under §11.

Document maps and roadmap references shall resolve to actual intended targets. A canonical name may differ from its directory alias, such as Document Identity versus DocumentIdentity. Preserve the distinction and assess stale maps explicitly. A map is a representation of sources, not a competing semantic owner or proof of approval.

Required dependencies shall identify consumer, provider, contract and scope; reference/navigation associations remain separately typed. Do not conceal a genuinely indispensable provider or cycle by calling it a documentation link. No complete dependency graph is inferred from a README.

---

# 7. Architecture Documentation

The 01-Architecture category organizes conceptual foundations of the component. Typical roles include the following; they are examples, not universally mandatory filenames.

| Role | Responsibility and applicability |
|---|---|
| Architecture | Defines purpose, boundaries, principles and owner/consumer architecture |
| Concepts | Defines conceptual meaning and distinctions |
| Model | Defines the domain's conceptual entities and relationships |
| Elements | Defines conceptual elements where that is the source's primary responsibility |

Additional conceptual documents require demonstrated need and clear owner boundaries. A domain-specific Elements source may instead primarily organize a structural catalog; its content and applicable owner contract determine Type/placement. This overview does not automatically reclassify or move every similarly titled source.

---

# 8. Structure Documentation

The 02-Structure category defines composition and structural constraints without taking over domain semantic ownership.

| Role | Responsibility and applicability |
|---|---|
| Schema | Organizes/references domain definitions and structural constraints; does not independently redefine their semantics |
| Relationships | Defines structural connection organization when that is its primary responsibility; actual relation kinds and endpoint contracts remain explicit |
| Constraints | Defines structural restrictions where that is the primary responsibility |
| Dictionary or entry catalog | Organizes authoritative domain definitions/records when catalog composition is primary; not limited to terminology |

A terminology consultation document can use Type Reference and its corresponding category even when titled Dictionary. A structural entry catalog uses Type Structure when that is the demonstrated primary responsibility. Domain definitions, source composition and consultation purpose must be assessed together; title or received path alone decides neither.

Metadata Dictionary defines Metadata Elements and their semantics; Schema organizes references, Profile constrains applicable usage and Instance supplies values under one effective Profile. Identity, Classification and Governance retain their domain meanings even when Metadata represents their values. This summary creates no canonical Element record, missing Profile or automatic consistency guarantee.

The exact document set depends on the domain and declared requirements. Received README maps and actual paths can disagree; reconcile the responsible sources and consumers through their scheduled cycles rather than silently relocating files in this UPDATE.

---

# 14. Optional Documents

Not every component requires the same document count. Security, Performance, Compliance, Migration, Interoperability and Integration are example topic roles, not new Type values or obligatory files.

Introduce a role when justified by domain requirements. Assign its primary responsibility to the existing four-Type taxonomy and corresponding category. Record applicability, owner, affected consumers and references; avoid duplicating semantic authority or manufacturing missing specifications. A required responsibility may be covered by an identified consolidated source if the applicable owner contract permits that coverage and the mapping is explicit.

Optional content does not waive the complete-set organization in §5 or a declared required source responsibility in §16. Missing required content is an unmet requirement; a not-applicable role needs its reason and owner evidence.

---

# 3. Scope

The contract applies to documentation sets for existing and future registered DF components. Examples include Metadata, Document Identity, Classification, Registry, Relationships, Knowledge Graph and Baselines; that example list is not the complete register. Registration and primary allocation belong to Architectural Components and Layers, referenced in §17. Foundation/Architecture support documents are not invented components merely because they appear in directories.

Every README.md, CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md, at every corpus location, is a non-normalized functional file. Normalization requires no Document ID, Family, Type, Component, Version, Revision, Status or Baseline for those names. Applicable content, organization, reference and integrity checks remain; the exclusion creates no exceptions to the four Types for normalized documents.

For normalized sources, Type is exactly one of Architecture, Structure, Behavior or Reference, selected by primary responsibility. Family is the canonical component name for component documents; common non-component areas use their admitted Family. Component, when present, agrees with actual membership. Class is optional and requires a distinct defined meaning; it is not unrestricted or inferred from a directory. Identity is stable under reclassification and relocation unless an assessed identity migration is necessary.

DF defines documentary contracts. A DMS, tool or applicable manual process executes management/checking operations; CMS governs changes in its own scope. This organization contract establishes neither operational permissions nor a deployed repository, workflow or documentation service.

---

# 16. Conformance

Organization conformance is assessed for an identified component documentation set and exact source editions against explicit applicable requirements. It is separate from conformance to domain architecture, an implemented component, review approval, publication and Baseline selection.

| Check | Required evidence | Outcome limit |
|---|---|---|
| Scope and ownership | Identified component, primary allocation, exact sources/editions and applicable owner contracts | Registration is not completeness or implementation |
| Minimum organization | README.md and all four category directories in §5 | Presence only; empty directories do not prove required content |
| Source-role coverage | Explicit required responsibilities/sources and applicability under the domain contract, mapped to actual supplied content | Typical titles in §§7–10 are examples; no universal fifteen-file list is imposed |
| Classification and placement | Each normalized source's primary responsibility, canonical membership/Family, four-value Type and justified category | Functional files are excluded from normalization; title/path alone is insufficient |
| Maps and references | Resolving actual source/roadmap targets, declared relation kinds, relevant provenance/state and assessed stale mappings | Advisory consultation/containment is not a required service edge |
| Findings and evidence | Checks, executor, observations, exact examined bytes, coverage limits and missing/conflicting requirements | Partial sets and unresolved requirements remain visible; no automatic whole-framework PASS |

The required responsibility inventory belongs to the relevant component owner/specification; this generic standard defines organization and evidence requirements without inventing every domain's mandatory filenames. Undefined coverage cannot be assumed complete. Identify a missing owner inventory as an unresolved requirement, and record each required role as satisfied, unmet or not applicable with its actual evidence. An example role may be optional; a declared mandatory role cannot be silently waived.

A complete set must satisfy the organization checks and its declared applicable source-role requirements. A partial set is reported as incomplete or not verified for complete-set conformance. In this corpus, Metadata, Document Identity, Classification and Templates provide README and all four directories, while map/content/classification checks remain pending. The added Reviews set supplies Behavior/Reference sources only; README, Architecture and Structure are absent. This source introduces no exception for Reviews, fabricates no missing files and certifies neither that set nor all 23 registered capabilities as complete.

A result records the exact assessed editions and declared scope. A scoped successful check is not approval, implemented conformance or Baseline membership and does not automatically apply after later edits. Integration and global owner/consumer compatibility require their own evidence.

---

# 9. Behavior Documentation

The 03-Behavior category defines subject-specific processes, transitions and controlled evolution. It does not by itself establish an executing system.

| Role | Responsibility and applicability |
|---|---|
| Lifecycle | Identifies the governed entity, states, permitted transitions and scope; may govern definitions, elements, instances or document editions |
| Validation | Defines applicable rules, examined artifacts/context, coverage and result evidence |
| Governance | Defines domain responsibilities, change/decision contracts and required evidence |
| Extensibility | Defines controlled extension, owner/consumer impact and transition requirements |

A Classification-definition lifecycle is distinct from a document edition's Version/Revision/Status and Workflow governance. Component maturity, implementation state and Baseline membership are also separate facts. State lists do not imply a complete universal transition graph or permission model.

DF defines these contracts; the applicable DMS/tool/manual executor supplies actual inputs, actions and observations. CMS change evidence does not substitute for documentary approval or exact Baseline selection. Review, validation, approval, publication and membership remain separate events. A scoped check result transfers neither to unseen sources nor later changed bytes.

---

# 10. Reference Documentation

The 04-Reference category contains consultation and consolidated reference roles, which may carry explicitly scoped normative or informative statements.

| Role | Responsibility and authority limit |
|---|---|
| Specification | Consolidates identified applicable requirements, references and conformance obligations; states its normative scope explicitly |
| Best Practices | Provides recommendations, declared informative unless an applicable contract explicitly adopts particular requirements |
| Examples | Provides illustrative usage with declared scope and limits; not evidence of implementation or universal compliance |
| Terminology reference | Provides domain-term consultation when that is its primary responsibility; canonical owners remain identified |

Normative or informative authority follows explicit applicable declarations and incorporation of identified sources/editions. It does not follow directory, Type=Reference or the word Specification alone. Supporting Architecture, Structure or Behavior sources can define normative requirements, and other Reference roles can be explicitly normative in scope. The received blanket statement that all remaining documents are informative is not retained.

A consolidated specification must identify the responsible sources it incorporates and how conflicts/applicability are assessed. This organization contract does not replace those domain requirements. Presence, normative wording or successful checking does not approve or publish a Draft edition, grant Baseline membership or establish implemented conformance.

---

# 1. Introduction

Classification is the Documentation component defining semantic category meanings and applicable assignments used to organize documents as structured knowledge. Its supporting architectural role does not move it into structural Foundation or make it an operational document-management system.

A logical document has purpose and, where applicable under its declared contract, assigned identity, represented descriptors, semantic classification, relationships and lifecycle. These are distinct subjects and responsibilities, not proof that every physical file, entity or pre-allocation subject already has every value or a complete accepted schema. Apply this architecture to its stated normalized-document and classification-definition/assignment contexts. Every README.md, CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md remains a non-normalized functional file.

Classification meaning is independent of location/format as a semantic rule; actual representations, references, inputs/outputs, interfaces and consumer effects still need responsible evidence. This working architecture defines requirements, not an installed classifier, actual allocation/assignment, complete implementation or globally approved component. The genuine Architecture retains DF-CLS-001 and its exact path despite the separate nominal Model collision (§§37/39).

---

# 5. Architectural Role

**Received conceptual view retained at its original section; current meaning is qualified below.**

```text
                                      Document
                                         │
                ┌────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┐
                │                        │                        │
                ▼                        ▼                        ▼

             Metadata            Document Identity          Classification
                │                        │                        │
                │                        │                        │

            describes               identifies                organizes

```

| Original label | Current typed subject / role |
|---|---|
| Document | Applicable logical-document subject; not every file/entity automatically normalized, assigned or classified |
| Metadata | Descriptor/representation owner, including Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance roles; category semantics are not transferred by representation |
| Document Identity | Qualified assigned document-key/domain/association meaning provider; not current classification or every support record |
| Classification | Classification component/domain meaning in this view; actual category/assignment subjects and provider interfaces are qualified in the section |
| describes | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| identifies | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| organizes | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |

**Relation scope:** Three owner capabilities contribute to the document; no mandatory joined runtime object, storage layout or ownership transfer.

Metadata describes, Document Identity identifies and Classification organizes the applicable logical document, with distinct owners and actual interfaces. Metadata owns descriptor definitions/representation: Dictionary, Schema, Profile and Instance. Classification owns classification category/value/assignment meanings in their governed context; Document Identity owns qualified document-key meanings and allocation/preservation contracts. Representing an owned value or repeating it in a projection does not transfer semantic authority.

For normalized documents, the current working classification contract under common Architecture and Review Policy is:

| Dimension | Current working contract | Distinction / limit |
|---|---|---|
| Family | Canonical component name, or an explicitly admitted non-component documentary area | Foundation/Architecture/global Roadmap areas follow Policy3; not an arbitrary domain or current allocation-series code |
| Type | Exactly one primary-responsibility value: Architecture, Structure, Behavior or Reference | Uniform across Families; Behavior spelling; no extra Concepts/Base/Core/Schema/Dictionary/Lifecycle or Foundation exceptions |
| Component | Actual canonical component membership when the field is used | Matches component Family here; a framework container is not a component of itself |
| Class | Separate optional semantic dimension with explicit non-conflicting definition when used | No complete Class enumeration or universal Family→Type→Class hierarchy is invented |

Type=Reference neither creates nor removes normative authority; explicit applicable statements/clauses and source editions govern. This source's Family/Component Classification and Type Architecture were already correct and remain unchanged. The contract above reconciles this architecture locally with current ARC-003§5.6/ARC-005§5.3 and Policy3; detailed older peer meanings remain pending coordinated propagation, not silently redefined in their existing bytes (§39).

---

# 9. Classification and Documents

**Received conceptual view retained at its original section; current meaning is qualified below.**

```text
                    Document
                    │
                    ├── Purpose
                    ├── Identity
                    ├── Metadata
                    ├── Classification
                    ├── Relationships
                    └── Lifecycle

```

| Original label | Current typed subject / role |
|---|---|
| Document | Applicable logical-document subject; not every file/entity automatically normalized, assigned or classified |
| Purpose | Selected logical-document aspect under its own responsible contract; not universal mandatory field/cardinality or accepted complete record |
| Identity | Selected logical-document aspect under its own responsible contract; not universal mandatory field/cardinality or accepted complete record |
| Metadata | Descriptor/representation owner, including Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance roles; category semantics are not transferred by representation |
| Classification | Classification component/domain meaning in this view; actual category/assignment subjects and provider interfaces are qualified in the section |
| Relationships | Selected logical-document aspect under its own responsible contract; not universal mandatory field/cardinality or accepted complete record |
| Lifecycle | Selected logical-document aspect under its own responsible contract; not universal mandatory field/cardinality or accepted complete record |

**Relation scope:** Selected logical-document aspect associations; not universal fields, multiplicity or complete accepted schema.

A logical document is the documentary unit being described; the six received aspect labels express responsible subjects, not a complete schema, unconditional mandatory field set or identity allocation for every file. Applicable normalized-document and actual classification-assignment contexts determine what is required.

Classification definitions/categories, document assignments and the document's exact edition/Status are distinct entities. A category, scheme, assignment or connection uses its own identity contract; a normalized document describing it has a document identity only in that applicable documentary scope. Do not assign DF document IDs to every category/entity or infer cardinality from a tree. The detailed Model/schema/profile owners must establish their actual rules; missing authentic Model evidence remains explicit.

---

# 12. Relationship with Metadata

**Received conceptual view retained at its original section; current meaning is qualified below.**

```text
                Metadata
                    │
                describes
                    │
                    ▼

                 Document
                    │
             is organized by
                    │
                    ▼

              Classification

```

| Original label | Current typed subject / role |
|---|---|
| Metadata | Descriptor/representation owner, including Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance roles; category semantics are not transferred by representation |
| describes | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| Document | Applicable logical-document subject; not every file/entity automatically normalized, assigned or classified |
| is organized by | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| Classification | Classification component/domain meaning in this view; actual category/assignment subjects and provider interfaces are qualified in the section |

**Relation scope:** Metadata description and document classification association; actual required Classification→Metadata scope is separately stated.

Metadata and Classification are complementary: Metadata represents standardized descriptors and Classification owns their classification category/value/assignment meanings in applicable contexts. Dictionary defines descriptors; Schema organizes them; Profile constrains usage for a declared context without redefining owner semantics; Instance supplies values under one effective Profile. No canonical Element IDs, complete Profile, actual instance or accepted merged field catalog is created by these summaries.

The received Metadata→Document→Classification arrows express description and assignment/semantic organization, not a required execution sequence. Classification→Metadata is an actual required provider declaration where governed metadata representation is indispensable for the document classification in scope. Exact inputs/outputs, source editions, owner/consumer interfaces and real uses must still be assessed; merely changing the relation name cannot dissolve a genuine cycle.

The functional Classification README§10 currently states “However, the semantic meaning of `Type` remains defined by Metadata.” That actual unchanged assertion is a pending owner-source discrepancy: for normalized-document classification meaning, current ARC-003§§5.4/5.6, ARC-005§§5.1/5.3 and Policy3 retain Classification/common rule ownership while Metadata owns descriptor representation. This does not transfer every unrelated field named Type or all Metadata meanings to Classification. The README and Metadata owner-source coordination must be separately traced before integrated agreement is claimed (§39).

---

# 13. Relationship with Document Identity

**Received conceptual view retained at its original section; current meaning is qualified below.**

```text
                    Document
                    │
                    ├── Document Identity
                    │        └── identifies the document
                    │
                    └── Classification
                             └── organizes the document

```

| Original label | Current typed subject / role |
|---|---|
| Document | Applicable logical-document subject; not every file/entity automatically normalized, assigned or classified |
| Document Identity | Qualified assigned document-key/domain/association meaning provider; not current classification or every support record |
| identifies the document | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| Classification | Classification component/domain meaning in this view; actual category/assignment subjects and provider interfaces are qualified in the section |
| organizes the document | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |

**Relation scope:** Two distinct capabilities about one document; ordinary classification change does not reconstruct governing K.

Document Identity defines governing qualified Domain+Identifier and applicable assignment/preservation contracts. Ordinary reclassification changes category/assignment/descriptive context without reconstructing assigned K or its same-logical-document association. Current Family/Type/component/path/Status/Version/Revision does not recalculate a valid stable DF allocation-series code.

The Documentation Framework corpus uses DF-SSS-NNN: DF renders the governing domain, SSS is a registered stable uppercase three-letter allocation series, NNN is 001–999 and 000 is excluded. Allocated/retired numbers are not reused; a gap proves no availability; at 999, register an unused governed continuation series rather than recycle or widen syntax. Other entity/domain contracts are not automatically DF document IDs. No allocation or series reservation occurs here.

Mutable identity support records, definition/assignment states, descriptors, references and exact editions differ from K. Current DID-014 V2.0 R1 distinguishes K from complete supporting R with all five mandatory logical roles, scoped State assertion and canonical-target descriptor; incoming0..N connections remain separate. That local working decision has remaining field/interface/peer/consumer propagation and is not an approved merged classification/Metadata record.

Necessary governing normative/domain/representation change follows actual prior/new authority and §28 transition evidence; it is not arbitrary reassignment, silent historical retargeting or an inference that every effect is harmless. Preserve category/assignment identities, exact historical definition/edition/context and snapshot continuity under their own owners.

---

# 14. Relationship with Templates

**Received conceptual view retained at its original section; current meaning is qualified below.**

```text
                 Template
                    │
            provides structure
                    │
                    ▼

                 Document
                    │
     receives semantic classification
                    │
                    ▼

              Classification

```

| Original label | Current typed subject / role |
|---|---|
| Template | Reusable representation definition/constraint owner; applicable instance and required use differ from semantic category meaning |
| provides structure | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| Document | Applicable logical-document subject; not every file/entity automatically normalized, assigned or classified |
| receives semantic classification | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| Classification | Classification component/domain meaning in this view; actual category/assignment subjects and provider interfaces are qualified in the section |

**Relation scope:** Template representation and semantic assignment; no mandatory Template runtime route or classification authority transfer.

Templates defines reusable documentary representations and structural constraints. Classification owns category/assignment meanings; Metadata owns represented descriptors. A template definition differs from its concrete document instances, and an entity described by a template is not automatically a normalized document allocation.

The received Template→Document→Classification view shows representation and semantic assignment, not that Templates controls classification meaning or every assignment must pass through a template service. Classification→Templates is required only where an actual indispensable template representation contract applies; otherwise the collaboration is optional/contextual. Actual source/schema/profile/instance compatibility, authority and checks remain needed. Using a template alone does not prove conformance, approve a successor or populate a canonical classification/Metadata catalog.

---

# 15. Relationship with Governance

**Received conceptual view retained at its original section; current meaning is qualified below.**

```text
           Documentation Layer
                    │
                    ▼

              Classification
                    │
      provides semantic information
                    │
                    ▼

             Governance Layer

```

| Original label | Current typed subject / role |
|---|---|
| Documentation Layer | Declared support/allocation area; exact registered component/contract meaning applies, not mandatory page-order execution |
| Classification | Classification component/domain meaning in this view; actual category/assignment subjects and provider interfaces are qualified in the section |
| provides semantic information | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| Governance Layer | Declared support/allocation area; exact registered component/contract meaning applies, not mandatory page-order execution |

**Relation scope:** Allocation plus meaning provision to Governance area; not automatic decision/approval or implemented workflow.

Classification belongs to Documentation; Governance is the separate area containing Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines. Classification provides domain lifecycle/usage/change/constraint meanings and evidence; Governance components define common process/rule/review/exact-snapshot contracts. The received “shall not assume governance responsibilities” is qualified: it excludes takeover of those common responsibilities and their actual execution, not Classification's own domain governance requirements.

Actual authorized DMS/tool/manual processes make or execute decisions with explicit authority/rules/subject/source editions/context/observations; CMS governs changes in its own scope. Domain definition state, assignment state, document Status/edition, finding state and Milestone state differ. Classification does not install a workflow, grant permissions, approve/publish an edition or select a Baseline through authorship, custody or local PASS.

Baseline selection needs an actual decision for exact eligible approved editions and pinned relevant relationship/definition context. Draft successors inherit neither approval nor membership of a received snapshot. Preserve actual historical classifications/decisions rather than silently reinterpreting them using the latest definition.

---

# 19. Relationship with Validation

**Received conceptual view retained at its original section; current meaning is qualified below.**

```text
              Classification
                    │
       defines semantic conditions
                    │ 
                    ▼

                Validation
                    │
                verifies
                    │
                    ▼

        Classification Assignment

```

| Original label | Current typed subject / role |

**Relation scope:** Context governs value interpretation; no universal field set or mandatory serialization is imposed.

Classification Context identifies the governing interpretation of a value or assignment: the intended scheme/domain and responsible definition meanings, with source/edition/time/usage or other context required by the actual claim. It is conceptual interpretation, not a prescribed record-field catalog or universal mandatory tuple.

Identical labels in different declared contexts need not identify the same category. A label, alias, category identity, interpreted value and actual assignment are not interchangeable. Context needed for a current usage decision may differ from the evidence preserving a historical definition/assignment or pinned snapshot. Missing applicable context is an evidence/authority limitation to assess, not permission to guess a meaning.

A Classification Scheme is a governed semantic organization of categories in a declared interpretation context. Its three received subjects remain:

- the categories belonging to that domain;

# 44. Working conceptual decisions and affected-source propagation

This V2.0 R1 Concepts edition makes three local working decisions under current common Architecture and adopted Review Policy:current normalized-document Family/Type/Class and hierarchy/conformance meaning; qualified concept/owner/assignment/usage/result-coverage subjects; and ordinary compatible extension versus necessary assessed normative/foundational/role/interface/domain revision. The prior/current map is external evidence and reflected in §§7–17/20/26–33/36–42. Exact old wording remains received history, not simultaneous contradictory current definitions.

**Actual related-owner terminology.** Current unchanged CLS-013§§6.5–6.7 describes Category as a grouping represented by an Element, Value as assigned to a document/context, and Assignment as association to one or more Elements. This edition distinguishes conceptual role, governed option, interpreted value andactual assignment with declaration of context and no invented complete cardinality. ## 1. Purpose and reconstruction provenance

This document defines a working conceptual Model of Classification: the semantic roles and entities, their associations, the interpretation of documentary dimensions, assignment evidence, owner interfaces and conceptual invariants. Classification belongs to the Documentation Layer and organizes documents as knowledge independently of storage technology or physical location. Its architecture, purposes and component boundaries remain owned by DF-CLS-001; its conceptual vocabulary is developed in DF-CLS-002.

**This edition is an explicit reconstruction, not recovery of an authentic historical Model.** The received file at this path declared DF-CLS-001 — Classification Architecture, V1.0 R0, Draft, Baseline 1.0, Author Arnaldo Figueira. Its prose excluded the classification model and repeated the received Architecture. No authentic historical Model was established in the supplied corpus. The received file, original headings, complete bodies, lists, diagrams and undated Architecture history remain exact evidence attached to DF-RVW-002. Their disposition is recorded in §31. The Model sections and diagrams in this edition were newly authored by Codex — AI assistant from the reviewed sources and explicit decisions below.

The cumulative Author header preserves the evidenced original contribution to the received documentary artifact and the actual later contributor. It does not attribute all reconstructed Model text to the original author or imply either author's approval of every later change. V2.0 R1 is the working successor of the received file; it is not evidence that an authentic V1.0 Model existed. The incompatible purpose/contract replacement and monotonic Revision increment are explained in §33.

The localized identity correction is at this path only. The genuine DF-CLS-001 — Classification Architecture keeps its identifier, path and exact current bytes. DF-CLS-001 is not an alias for DF-CLS-003. There is no general replacement of Architecture references with Model references. The allocation decision and scans are attached to the review report; external allocation/reservation history remains unavailable.

## 3. Authority and explicit working decisions

Current working inputs are DF-CLS-001 V2.0 R1, DF-CLS-002 V2.0 R1, common Architecture and the adopted DF-RVW-001 V1.0 R2. They establish the current normalized-document Family/Type/optional-Class meanings, stable document identity separation, responsible owner boundaries and ordinary preservation versus necessary assessed revision. This Model integrates those decisions at conceptual-model level within its own working scope. It is Draft and has no assigned Baseline or evidence of architectural acceptance.

The actual unchanged CLS-004/005/009/010/013/014 sources retain competing terminology, hierarchy and incomplete cardinality claims. Their exact clauses, editions and hashes are recorded in the accompanying evidence and §30. This edition does not declare that those sources already agree. A source's Type, filename, title, citation or catalog presence alone confers neither normative authority nor approval. Advice, examples, historical assertions, working decisions and explicitly applicable normative requirements retain their actual roles.

| Local decision | Actual previous situation | Current working decision and limit |
|---|---|---|
| Model responsibility and provenance | Received Architecture copy explicitly excluded the Model | Supply a newly authored distinct conceptual Model; preserve the copy as evidence and delegate its Architecture subjects to genuine CLS-001 |
| Entity and association distinctions | No authentic Model; Dictionary uses broader Element/category/assignment terminology | Distinguish role, governed option, interpreted value, association and context (§§4–10); map exact peer uses rather than claim completed terminology merger |

## 4. Conceptual subjects and roles

The following distinctions are this Model's explicit working interpretation. They are conceptual subjects, not automatically separate persisted tables, classes, document records or newly registered components.

| Subject or role | Meaning | Distinct from |
|---|---|---|
| Intended documentary subject | Logical document, or explicitly selected edition, to which an assignment claim applies | File path, category, descriptor field or a drawn document box |
| Classification Scheme | Governed organization of semantic options and their interpretation under a declared context | Storage schema, complete populated dictionary or a classifier implementation |
| Classification Context | Applicable scheme, definitions, source editions and interpretation conditions necessary for the actual claim | A universal mandatory context-record tuple or arbitrary runtime setting |
| Classification Element | A conceptual role or dimension expressing a governed distinction; Family, Type and Class are current documentary examples | Automatically a particular category, Metadata Element or component |
| Classification Category | A defined semantic option within a declared scheme/context | Its label, definition document's key, current usage permission or population of assignments |
| Classification Value | Interpreted semantic value expressed for an Element in the actual context; it may select a category | Uninterpreted string, category identity or proof of assignment |
| Classification Assignment | Actual governed association between the intended documentary subject and interpreted value/category under applicable roles and context | Definition availability, a proposed value, Registry index row or validation result |
| Classification Membership | Semantic consequence of a valid applicable assignment | Physical containment or unconditional permission for future use |
| Definition edition | Selected version of the definition/meaning used to interpret an actual claim | Document Version by implication, label change or current lifecycle assertion |
| Classification relationship | Typed semantic association with defined endpoints and permitted interpretation | Every required-service edge, runtime call or general Relationships record |

Actual Dictionary §§6.1/6.5–6.7 defines Element as a semantic unit representing a category, Category as a grouping represented by an Element, Value as assigned to a document/context and Assignment as association with one or more Elements. Those umbrella uses are mapped to role/category/value/association as their actual context requires. This Model's distinctions do not retrospectively change that text, prove that every term is one-to-one, or claim an accepted merged canonical catalog. The exact owner reconciliation remains pending.

## 14. Cardinality and applicability matrix

This matrix separates adopted normalized-document obligations from unresolved general-model multiplicities. It is a local conceptual boundary; it does not replace the detailed Schema/Constraints or invent serialized field cardinalities.

| Association or question | Current justified working requirement | Remaining limit / owner |
|---|---|---|
| Applicable normalized document → Family | Use its actual canonical component or admitted documentary area; do not omit the applicable classification obligation or infer several Families from directory aliases | Exact representation and schema details remain responsible Metadata/Classification contracts |
| Applicable normalized document → Type | Exactly one primary value from the four responsibilities | No Family-specific Type enumeration or automatic Type from filename |
| Applicable normalized document → Class | Separate and optional; any value used must be explicitly defined and non-conflicting | No general maximum multiplicity or complete Class vocabulary is established here |
| Scheme → Category | Governed semantic option membership must be evidenced for the actual claim | No universal minimum/maximum population count is established |
| Element → Value / Category | Role interpretation and actual scheme rules determine the relation | No universal one-to-one or all-context mandatory mapping is established |
| Assignment → documentary subject | Every claim identifies its actual intended subject and logical-versus-edition scope | Does not forbid separately defined bulk/group operations; each actual subject association needs traceability |
| Assignment → applicable role/value/context | Actual interpretation and association evidence are required | No universal physical tuple or universal number of assigned values is established |
| Category → documentary members | Membership follows actual valid applicable assignments | No member-count bound, mandatory population or completeness claim is established |
| Semantic relationship → endpoints | Endpoint kinds, direction and actual rule scope must be explicit | Multiplicity, inverse, transitivity and acyclicity belong to the actual relation rules |
| Assigned document K → incoming external references | Population may be zero or more under the applicable DID contract | Distinct from mandatory supporting Canonical Reference descriptor for a complete assigned R |

Actual Schema §34 says complete authoritative element/cardinality rules are not established there. Relationships §20 illustrates Family1→many Type and Type1→many Class; its exact constraints are deferred to Schema/Specification. This Model does not convert those illustrations into governing uniform-Type/Class cardinalities. Specification R-013 requires the actual applicable Schema/Constraints rules, not arbitrary numbers chosen to fill a gap. Detailed missing/competing owner requirements must remain visible before a broad integrated claim.

## 16. Identity boundaries and localized documentary correction

Classification definition/category/value/assignment subjects are not all document identities. Their governing entity identity rules remain distinct from the identity of a normalized document that describes them. Labels, aliases and definition editions are not automatically identity coordinates. This Model allocates no universal DF document IDs to categories or assignments.

For applicable assigned normalized documents, the current qualified key K is the governing identity domain plus allocated identifier, associated with the same logical document. In this corpus the domain is Documentation Framework with prefix DF and the representation DF-SSS-NNN: registered stable three-letter uppercase allocation series and positive three-digit number 001–999. 000 is excluded. Series origin is recorded historically; current Family, Type, Component, path, Status, Version or Revision does not recalculate K.

An ordinary classification correction or repository move preserves the same document's assigned K. Allocated/retired numbers are not reused; a gap proves no availability. At 999, a traceable unused continuation series must be registered rather than widening the syntax or silently recycling. A new domain is a separate semantic decision. Historical META-DCL-001 Family/Type decomposition is not the current key-generation contract.

Those historical assertions establish intended naming, not authentic Model content, approval or exhaustive external reservation history. Genuine CLS001 is preserved. No document that legitimately owns CLS001 is rekeyed, and no CLS001→CLS003 alias is registered. Original evidence continues to identify the received wrong declaration by its exact path and edition.
