## 2. Applicability and boundaries

This Model applies to the semantic organization of the actual intended documentary subjects in their declared scheme and rule context. Its normalized-document Family/Type/Class rules apply to normalized documents under the current working corpus convention. Every file named README.md, CHANGELOG.md or ArchitecturalMilestones.md, at any location, remains a non-normalized functional file; this Model does not mandate normalized fields or allocate identities to those files. They remain subject to applicable content, reference, evidence and consistency checks.

A logical document, a particular document edition, a classification definition, a semantic value, an assignment and a representation of that assignment are distinct subjects. A pre-allocation draft can be discussed without pretending it already has an assigned document key. A diagram, example or descriptor field does not establish that an assignment actually occurred. Applicable owner rules govern whether a draft may receive a classification and what subject evidence is required.

This Model defines conceptual meaning and local working invariants. It does not prescribe a database schema, serialization language, mandatory physical record, executable classifier, complete vocabulary population, general cardinality catalog, lifecycle engine, permission system or implemented integration. Detailed structural, lifecycle, validation, governance, relationship and extension rules retain their responsible sources. Missing or conflicting mandatory owner evidence prevents a broad conformance claim; it is not silently filled by a diagram or treated as an observed violation.

## 6. Scheme and context

A scheme identifies how its semantic options are defined and interpreted. The governing context supplies the distinctions needed by the actual claim: which scheme and definition sources apply, which edition or effective conditions are intended, and any relevant domain, time or usage scope. The required context is claim-dependent. This is not a new universally mandatory list of physical fields or an authorization mechanism.

The same textual label in different schemes or source editions does not prove the same category, value or meaning. Conversely, two representations can express the same governed semantic option when an actual definition/mapping establishes that equivalence. Interpretation requires the applicable definitions and authority, not string equality alone.

A scheme's documented availability is not evidence that all possible options are populated, approved or currently assignable. Actual scheme membership, definition edition and lifecycle/usage rules must be checked where material. This Model does not fill an unavailable Class vocabulary or invent categories from illustrative placeholders.

## 7. Classification Element as a dimension

An Element is the conceptual role in which a classification distinction is expressed. For normalized documents, Family identifies actual component/admitted documentary-area membership, Type identifies primary documentary responsibility and Class can express an additional defined non-conflicting distinction. A role's meaning and the value represented in that role are separate.

Received Elements §36 calls its Family/Type/Class view a complete conceptual element model, while its §§6–7 preserve earlier role meanings. That is actual received peer evidence, not proof that the current role/category/assignment distinctions and every cardinality are integrated. Family, Type and Class here are neither three automatically created Metadata Elements nor three architectural components.

Other dimensions require explicit responsible definitions, applicability, relationships and compatible or justified incompatible change assessment. A new dimension does not extend the permitted Type enumeration or waive mandatory existing rules. Naming and population belong to actual definition owners; this Model does not allocate their identifiers.

## 8. Category and definition

A Category is a defined semantic option within its actual scheme/context. Its identity, definition, label, lifecycle assertion and usage are separate concerns. A definition states the option's governed meaning and scope; a readable label represents that meaning in a context and need not be its identity.

Definition evidence must be adequate for the actual interpretation claim. A category placeholder, a title in a catalog or an unqualified term is not automatically an admitted category. When a definition changes, preserve the exact prior meaning/source edition and determine whether the current change is a compatible clarification, an additive capability or an incompatible semantic revision. Neither historical interpretation nor present assignment permission follows from a label remaining unchanged.

This working distinction supports source-qualified category relationships and usage evidence without prescribing a universal category object structure, globally unique category-ID syntax or normative population of all schemes. Those require their responsible definition/schema/constraint decisions.

## 9. Value, representation and interpretation

A Value expresses a classification meaning in an Element role under an applicable context. A representation such as the string `Architecture` is interpreted as the current Type responsibility only when the governing role/context establishes that meaning. The same word in a title, directory or historical citation is not necessarily a current Type assignment.

A value may select a governed category; that relationship is not assumed to be universal one-to-one. Actual scheme/schema definitions decide whether alternate representations, combinations or additional semantic relationships are permitted. Identity, synonymy, formatting, label equivalence and semantic compatibility require their actual rules and evidence.

Representations in a Markdown header, Metadata Instance, template output, index or graph projection do not acquire authority to redefine Classification. A correction to rendering must be distinguished from a correction to assignment meaning. Meaning changes require responsible owner/consumer and compatibility assessment even when the lexical value is unchanged.

## 10. Assignment and membership

An Assignment is an actual governed association concerning an intended document and an interpreted value/category under its Element role and applicable context. For an assigned normalized document, the governing qualified document key identifies the logical subject. An edition-specific assertion also identifies the intended edition/bytes/context. Pre-allocation claims must identify their real temporary subject and limitations without inventing an assigned K.

Evidence for an actual assignment must establish the intended subject, the represented role/value and governing definition/rules/source editions, together with the authority, usage/time or decision context required by the claim. These are semantic evidence obligations, not a prescribed universal persisted tuple. The mere presence of a classification definition, a label in an example or a validation log does not establish that the association was authorized or performed.

Membership is the semantic consequence of an actual valid applicable assignment. A category's member list is not physical containment or evidence of complete population coverage. Current membership and current permission to create another assignment may differ from preserved historical membership under an earlier definition. Actual applicability and responsible rules decide the claim.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  D["Intended document / selected edition"] -->|subject of evidence| A["Actual assignment claim"]
  R["Role, value and governing definition context"] -->|interprets| A
  U["Applicable authority and usage rules"] -->|constrains| A
  A -->|supports when valid for the claim| M["Semantic membership"]
```

This newly authored view represents evidence and semantics. It neither performs an assignment nor equates evaluation, authorization and historical interpretation.

## 11. Family

For an applicable normalized document, Family identifies the actual canonical component or explicitly admitted non-component documentary area under current common Architecture and Review Policy §3. Component documents use the canonical name of their component; when Component is present it matches that actual membership. Current component names include Metadata, Document Identity, Classification and Templates. `DocumentIdentity` is a directory spelling, not a separate canonical component.

Foundation, Architecture and global Roadmap are admitted non-component documentary areas in their actual policy scope. The framework container is not its own component. Component roadmaps use the Family of the component they plan even when physically stored under Roadmaps. A path or allocation-series prefix does not determine Family.

Earlier broad-domain Family definitions remain exact historical or pending peer evidence. They are not an alternative simultaneous governing rule for this current normalized-document operation. This Model establishes no universal category cardinality for every other scheme or arbitrary entity from this corpus rule.

## 12. Type

Type identifies exactly one primary documentary responsibility for each applicable normalized document. Its meaning is uniform across Families.

| Type | Primary responsibility |
|---|---|
| Architecture | Foundations, principles, concepts, conceptual models/elements and architectural decisions |
| Structure | Organization, composition, schemas, structural relationships, restrictions and element catalogs |
| Behavior | Processes, lifecycle, validation, governance, extensibility and planned evolution |
| Reference | Consultation, terminology, consolidated specifications, examples, recommendations and historical records |

Use the spelling Behavior. Concepts, Model, Elements, Schema, Dictionary, Lifecycle, Base and Core are not extra Type values merely because they occur in titles or directories. Content and primary responsibility determine Type. Historical consultation is Reference; a process or planned evolution is Behavior. An applicable mixed-content document still identifies its actual primary responsibility.

Family does not create a separate Type vocabulary or redefine a Type's responsibility. Actual contextual applicability constraints may limit a particular use without redefining the meaning of the four Type values. Type=Reference alone neither grants nor removes normative authority, formal approval or publication status.

## 13. Class

Class is a separate optional semantic dimension. Its use requires an explicit definition and applicability that does not conflict with the governing Family/Type meanings or merely duplicate Type without an actual additional distinction. Absence of Class is not a defect solely because a received conceptual tuple lists it.

This Model does not establish a complete Class enumeration, universal Type→Class hierarchy, mandatory Class value or physical field. If the actual context needs a Class vocabulary or permitted combinations, the responsible definition/schema/constraint decisions must specify them with evidence. Optional does not mean an unrestricted string or a fifth Type.

Current Concepts §14 preserves the received nature/role subject but qualifies its present interpretation. Actual unchanged peers that place Class under Type remain pending source-qualified reconciliation. Neither an illustrative diagram nor this acknowledgment approves those relationships for every current assignment.

## 15. Semantic relationships and hierarchies

Relationships within Classification have actual semantic endpoint kinds and direction. Role/value interpretation, category membership, category specialization, documentary assignment, label equivalence, supersession and deprecation are different relations. Their names or arrows are not interchangeable evidence of the same constraint.

The current normalized-document Family and Type dimensions do not form the earlier universal specialization hierarchy. Class is not universally subordinate to Type. Actual category schemes can define hierarchical or non-hierarchical relations when their responsible definitions, scope and constraints do so. There is no prohibition on every hierarchy merely because the old Family-dependent Type hierarchy is replaced.

Acyclicity applies only where the actual relation/schema rules require it. Received Relationships §43 explicitly qualifies invalid cycles by relationship type and applicable Schema. It is not proof that all semantic graphs, general Relationships, navigation or required-service dependencies are one DAG. Source/target meaning, inverse, symmetry and transitivity require their own rules; they do not follow from arrow appearance.

Where the general Relationships component records a connection, it owns connection/endpoints/provenance contracts; Classification owns the classification meaning of the connection. Projection into a Knowledge Graph cannot redefine either authority. No connection record or graph node is created by publishing this conceptual view.

## 17. Labels, aliases and historical interpretation

A label can change without changing category identity when the responsible definition permits it; a semantic change can occur while a label stays unchanged. An alias or synonym needs actual scoped equivalence evidence and source/edition applicability. A textual resemblance or matching numeric suffix is not sufficient.

Historical labels and examples retain their original interpretation context. They must not silently resolve to another category, document or edition following a current correction. A current reference can target a logical document or an explicitly pinned edition; a pinned historical member retains its original bytes/context even when a later working successor exists.

The wrong received CLS001 header at this path is not legitimized as a semantic or documentary alias. History records the error and localized correction. Actual external integrations, consumers or caches with ambiguous unqualified CLS001 references require intended-target investigation; a global substitution would corrupt genuine Architecture references. Current operational ambiguity must be resolved before those consumers are claimed integrated.

## 18. Definition editions, usage and physical independence

A definition edition identifies the governed interpretation used by the actual assignment claim. It is not automatically the governing document's Version coordinate or a new universal record type. Applicable sources must establish the real linkage where documentary editions carry definition meaning.

Preserving an assignment's historical meaning does not automatically authorize its present use. Deprecated/retired definition evidence, current assignment permission, current membership, historical membership, reference validity and observed live retrieval are separate questions. Repositories, Registry entries, graph projections and Metadata representations may become stale while historical intended meaning remains interpretable.

Moving a file does not by itself change category identity, assigned document K or semantic membership. It can affect references, representations, indexes, adapter interfaces or access. Those actual effects require their responsible checks. Technology/format/storage independence preserves semantic ownership; it is not evidence that every representation or provider contract is unaffected by a physical change.

## 19. Metadata projection and ownership

Classification owns the meaning of its categories, roles, interpreted values, assignments and applicable classification conditions. Metadata owns descriptive element definitions and its Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance contracts. Representation of classification in Metadata does not transfer semantic authority to Metadata, Templates, Registry or a header parser.

For an actual applicable Metadata Instance, its governing effective Profile must be identified under the responsible Metadata contract. This Model creates neither a complete Profile nor a Classification field catalog. Family, Type, Class, scheme/context or assignment evidence here is conceptual meaning; it is not proof that corresponding Metadata Elements have canonical identifiers, complete descriptor schemas or publication/lifecycle records.

An actual projection needs intended semantic subject, source definition/rules/edition, representation mapping, applicable descriptor/profile/interface, cardinality/omission handling, provenance and checks required by that claim. Compatible rendering and semantic correction are assessed separately. An indispensable governed representation creates an actual Classification→Metadata requirement in that scope; calling it a projection does not remove the required provider.

## 20. Document Identity interfaces

Classification consumes Document Identity when an applicable assigned normalized-document subject or document endpoint must be identified. A logical-document claim uses its governing K; an exact-edition claim adds the actual edition/bytes/context. A category's identity and the key of a document describing that category remain distinct.

Current DID014 V2.0 R1 makes a local working distinction between K and complete supporting assigned record R. Complete R retains five mandatory roles: Document Identity, Identifier, Identity Domain, Identity State and Canonical Reference. Identity State/Lifecycle State is a scoped R assertion, not document Status or generic Metadata State. Canonical Reference is the intended qualified canonical target/edition descriptor, not a required incoming Relationships edge or a promise of live retrieval. K-only evidence is not full R conformity.

That exact DID specification decision is not globally accepted or fully propagated field/interface agreement. Current DID005/003/004/006/013 meanings and DF-DID-005 §11, DF-DID-010 §12, DF-DID-011 §§4.2/9 and DF-DID-013 §9 earlier-restriction references retain actual source-specific reconciliation limits. This Model consumes the needed meaning without claiming complete merged DID/Metadata schemas or silently changing those sources.

## 21. Templates, Governance and other consumers

Templates owns reusable structural definitions and applicable instance contracts. When a Classification representation actually requires a Template contract, identify that conditional Classification→Templates interface; not every assignment requires Templates. A template may expose governed fields but cannot redefine category meaning or manufacture an assignment merely by including a placeholder.

Classification owns its domain-specific conditions, definition changes and assignment semantics. Common Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines retain governance contracts; actual management/approval/publication or permission execution belongs to the authorized executor and applicable DMS/tool/manual process. A CMS may manage the actual change process. This Model neither implements those systems nor transfers owner responsibility through a diagram.

Discovery consumes semantic information for organization, navigation and search. Registry catalogs registrations/index records with source/freshness evidence; it does not create entity existence or allocate document identity. Relationships records governed connections and endpoints; Knowledge Graph projects actual authoritative subjects/connections. Automation capabilities and Integration adapters need actual inputs, outputs, mapping, authorization and checks. Semantic support is not blanket permission to create, migrate, publish or retire anything.

## 23. Lifecycle boundaries

Definition lifecycle and documentary usage are separate subjects. Actual CLS006 §20 proposes Defined, Active, Deprecated and Retired for classification definitions; its §§7–8 distinguishes definition lifecycle from usage. This Model preserves those source roles and does not promote a proposal to approved/implemented state machinery. The word introduced can describe an action without being a canonical state or automatic alias for Defined.

Document Status, definition lifecycle, assignment usage/current permission, identity R state assertion, review-finding state and Milestone state are distinct. No shared word makes them aliases. State/transition applicability requires actual intended subject, event/rule, authority, decision and evidence under the responsible owner contract.

Deprecation can preserve historical meaning while discouraging or restricting new usage under actual rules. It does not automatically warn, invalidate, migrate or erase every prior assignment. Retirement similarly does not silently retarget pinned definitions or document editions. Actual usage decisions and transition evidence must be preserved separately from historical interpretation.

## 24. Validation and result semantics

A Model claim identifies intended subject/population, semantic/representation/interface scope, exact source editions/artifacts/bytes/context, applicable responsible rules, authority/executor, performed and unperformed checks, observations, coverage and limits. Validation compares actual observations with applicable rules and is nonmutating; correction, assignment, permission, acceptance and formal approval require their own authorization/evidence.

Actual CLS007 §§39–42 provides Valid, Valid with Warnings and Invalid. Valid with Warnings requires no blocking rule violation and actual non-blocking findings; deprecated usage is not automatically a warning or universally invalid. Invalid requires an actual applicable blocking violation. Rule-dependent outcome meaning is not replaced by an imported DID outcome vocabulary or a selected binary diagram.

Missing, unperformed or conflicting mandatory evidence withholds a broader success claim without fabricating an observed blocking violation. Incomplete assessment and an actual invalid assignment are different conclusions. Narrow documentary checks can succeed while Model implementation, authoritative category population, full Schema/Constraints compliance or global owner integration remains unestablished.

No classification assignment, lifecycle transition or source correction is performed by a validation result. Result recording and reproducible evidence retain their actual executor and date; changing a source after a completed check requires an appropriate successor and later check rather than extending an earlier PASS to new bytes.

## 25. Governance, change authority and traceability

A proposed classification definition, association or rule change identifies its actual owner, need, rationale, alternatives, prior/new meaning, consumers, applicable authority, compatibility and transition. Actual decisions and implemented effects are recorded separately. A review command authorizes its declared documentary operation; it does not approve an architecture globally or grant operational permissions by implication.

Maintain traceability between semantic definitions, applicable source editions, intended documentary subjects, actual assignments, descriptor projections, relationship endpoints, decisions and later checks where relevant to the claim. A complete traceability claim requires actual population/coverage evidence; this conceptual list is not proof that all connections exist.

No component may silently redefine another owner's responsibility. Common Governance contracts and an actual CMS/DMS/tool/manual executor retain their own scope. This Model creates no lifecycle record, publication state, Baseline membership, category allocation or mandatory all-term consultation rule merely by listing those subjects.

## 26. Evolution and compatibility

Ordinary compatible evolution preserves applicable definitions, assigned same-document continuity and historical interpretation where feasible. Necessary assessed normative/foundational/responsibility/interface/domain revision is permitted under actual common Architecture AP-015–018 and responsible change authority; it is not automatically compatible because it is called an extension.

The received Architecture copy's §§28/31.4/35 asserted evolution without changing foundations, preservation of existing semantic meaning and unqualified architectural compatibility. Those exact previous clauses remain in the old body/view/map evidence. They are not simultaneous current rules in this reconstructed Model. Current genuine Architecture §28 explicitly replaces those absolute restrictions with ordinary preservation versus necessary assessed revision.

A necessary revision must preserve actual prior artifacts/failed checks and identify old/new rules, subject/domain/context, need, alternatives, rationale, responsible authority, owners, consumers and indispensable interfaces. Assess old→new definition/category/value/alias/assignment/reference mappings, key/domain/collision/reservation history and exact snapshot continuity. Resolve actual reciprocal requirements and transition effects rather than conceal them with relation names. Apply only the authorized scoped change with actual contributor/history evidence and later checks.

Under the working Review Policy, compatible correction retains Version; compatible additive capability increments minor; incompatible contract/convention change increments major and resets minor to0. Revision increments monotonically across Version changes. Unchanged-source validation increments neither. Real compatibility depends on permitted meaning and interfaces, not a filename correction or number alone. No arbitrary semantic mutation, allocated/retired key reuse, silent historical retargeting or automatic assignment migration follows from this evolution rule.

# 1. Introduction

The Classification component organizes documents according to governed semantic characteristics. This document defines the conceptual roles and meanings of three principal documentary dimensions: Family, Type and Class. It distinguishes those roles from category definitions, interpreted values, actual assignments and descriptor representations.

The three received dimension subjects remain:

- **Family**;
- **Type**;
- **Class**.

Current working Architecture DF-CLS-001, Concepts DF-CLS-002 and Model DF-CLS-003 are V2.0 R1 Draft editions. The Model is an explicit newly authored reconstruction, not recovery of authentic historical Model text. Its Step4.31 documentary validation does not establish global architectural acceptance, complete owner/cardinality/schema integration or implemented conformity. This edition consumes its scoped conceptual distinctions and records actual unchanged peer differences in §42.

The primary responsibility here is conceptual semantics and element definitions, not formal representation. Type is therefore Architecture under the adopted Review Policy. The legitimate DF-CLS-004 identity and current physical path are retained; physical placement under 02-Structure remains an explicit M13 coordination issue, not a claim of ARC007 placement conformity. Formal structural representation remains owned by DF-CLS-005 and applicable Metadata contracts.

| **Class** | Identifies the nature or role of the document | Separate optional explicitly defined non-conflicting distinction, without duplicating Type or assuming a complete vocabulary |

This is an explicit prior/current semantic decision under the adopted working rules and current Architecture/Concepts/Model. ## 6.1. Definition

For an applicable normalized document, Family identifies its actual canonical component or an explicitly admitted non-component documentary area. A component document uses the actual canonical component name; Component, when present, matches that membership. Foundation, Architecture and global Roadmap are admitted non-component areas in their stated policy scope; the framework container is not a component of itself.

The received broad-domain/highest-level definition and Family→Type specialization view are prior meanings. They are replaced for the current operation by the component/admitted-area responsibility above. Family does not define a Family-specific Type vocabulary or a mandatory parent relation. Its directory alias, allocation-series origin, filename and physical path do not determine membership.

Actual Elements/Schema/Dictionary/Constraints peers retain earlier terminology pending coordinated reconciliation; this local decision does not claim all sources already agree.

## 7.1. Definition

Type identifies exactly one primary responsibility for each applicable normalized document, uniformly across Families. Its values are Architecture, Structure, Behavior and Reference. Architecture covers foundations, principles, concepts, conceptual models/elements and decisions; Structure covers organization, composition, schemas, structural relationships/restrictions/catalogs; Behavior covers processes, lifecycle, validation, governance and planned evolution; Reference covers consultation, terminology, specifications, examples, recommendations and history.

The received specific-category-within-Family definition is replaced as a current rule. A Family does not specialize or redefine Type meaning. A title such as Model, Elements, Schema, Dictionary or Lifecycle is not a fifth Type or automatic classification merely because it appears in a filename. Assess actual primary content. # Classification Component

> **Documentation Framework — Documentation Component**

> The architectural component responsible for defining, organizing, assigning and governing the semantic classification of documents within the Documentation Framework.

# 1. Overview

The **Classification** component defines how documents are organized into semantic categories according to a defined classification model.

Classification provides a semantic mechanism for organizing documents within the Documentation Framework while remaining independent of their physical representation.

The component establishes the concepts, models, elements, structures, rules and governance required to define and maintain classification systems.

---

# 2. Purpose

The purpose of the Classification component is to provide a consistent and controlled mechanism for classifying documentation.

Classification enables documents to be organized according to their semantic characteristics rather than according to their physical location.

The component provides the architectural foundation required for:

- semantic organization;
- document discovery;
- document grouping;
- classification-based relationships;
- validation;
- governance;
- automation.

---

# 3. Architectural Position

Classification belongs to the **Documentation Layer** of the Documentation Framework.

Conceptually:

```text

                         Documentation Layer

                    ┌───────────────────────────┐
                    │ Metadata                  │
                    │ Document Identity         │
                    │ Classification            │
                    │ Templates                 │
                    └───────────────────────────┘

```

Classification works together with Metadata and Document Identity while maintaining its own architectural responsibility.

---

# 4. Responsibility

The Classification component is responsible for:

- defining classification concepts;
- defining classification models;
- defining classification elements;
- defining classification schemas;
- defining classification assignments;
- defining classification relationships;
- defining classification constraints;
- defining classification lifecycle;
- defining classification validation;
- defining classification governance;
- defining classification extensibility;
- defining authoritative classification terminology.

Classification does not define:

- document identity;
- document metadata in general;
- document templates;
- document workflows;
- physical repository organization.

Those responsibilities belong to other components of the Documentation Framework.

---

# 5. Architectural Independence

Classification is independent of the physical representation of documentation.

The semantic organization defined by Classification shall not depend on:

- directory structures;
- filenames;
- repositories;
- storage technologies;
- document formats;
- implementation technologies.

A physical organization may reflect conceptual distinctions established by Classification, but the physical representation does not define those distinctions.

The relationship is therefore:

```text

         Classification Semantics
                    │
                    ▼

       Architectural Representation
                    │
                    ▼

          Physical Representation

```

and not:

```text

          Physical Representation
                    │
                    ▼

         Classification Semantics

```

---

# 6. Relationship with Other Components

## 6.1. Metadata

Metadata provides descriptive information about documents that may participate in classification.

Classification uses that information without redefining the responsibility of Metadata.

---

## 6.2. Document Identity

Document Identity provides the logical identity of the documents to which classifications may be assigned.

Classification does not establish document identity.

---

## 6.3. Templates

Templates may define standardized structures for representing classification information.

Classification defines the semantic classification model rather than the template used to represent it.

---

## 6.4. Workflow

Workflow may use classification information when determining or controlling document processes.

Classification does not define workflow behavior.

---

## 6.5. Policies

Policies may establish rules governing the use or administration of classifications.

Classification provides the classification structures to which such policies may apply.

---

## 6.6. Registry and Discovery

Classification may provide semantic information used by Registry and Discovery mechanisms to organize and locate documentation.

---

## 6.7. Knowledge Graph

Classification concepts and relationships may contribute semantic information to the Knowledge Graph.

---

# 7. Documentation Structure

The Classification component is defined through the following documents:

| Order | Document | Description |
|------:|----------|-------------|
| 1 | DF-CLS-001 — Classification Architecture | Defines the architectural position, responsibility and boundaries of Classification. |
| 2 | DF-CLS-002 — Classification Concepts | Defines the fundamental concepts of Classification. |
| 3 | DF-CLS-003 — Classification Model | Defines the conceptual model governing classification. |
| 4 | DF-CLS-004 — Classification Elements | Defines the elements that constitute a classification system. |
| 5 | DF-CLS-005 — Classification Schema | Defines the formal structure of classification systems. |
| 6 | DF-CLS-006 — Classification Lifecycle | Defines the lifecycle of classification structures and assignments. |
| 7 | DF-CLS-007 — Classification Validation | Defines classification validation and conformance rules. |
| 8 | DF-CLS-008 — Classification Governance | Defines governance and control of classification systems. |
| 9 | DF-CLS-009 — Classification Relationships | Defines relationships between classification elements and related entities. |
| 10 | DF-CLS-010 — Classification Constraints | Defines constraints that preserve classification integrity. |
| 11 | DF-CLS-011 — Classification Extensibility | Defines mechanisms for extending classification systems. |
| 12 | DF-CLS-012 — Classification Best Practices | Documents recommended practices for classification design and maintenance. |
| 13 | DF-CLS-013 — Classification Dictionary | Defines authoritative Classification terminology. |
| 14 | DF-CLS-014 — Classification Specification | Consolidates the normative Classification specification. |
| 15 | DF-CLS-015 — Classification Examples | Provides representative examples of Classification usage. |

---

# 8. Documentation Progression

The documentation follows four major stages.

## 8.1. Conceptual Foundation

```text

    DF-CLS-001
    DF-CLS-002
    DF-CLS-003

```

Defines the architectural and conceptual foundations of Classification.

## 8.2. Structural Definition

```text

    DF-CLS-004
    DF-CLS-005

```

Defines the elements and structures used to represent classifications.

## 8.3. Operational Definition

```text

    DF-CLS-006
    DF-CLS-007
    DF-CLS-008
    DF-CLS-009
    DF-CLS-010
    DF-CLS-011

```

Defines lifecycle, validation, governance, relationships, constraints and extensibility.

## 8.4. Consolidation and Reference

```text

    DF-CLS-012
    DF-CLS-013
    DF-CLS-014
    DF-CLS-015

```

Provides best practices, terminology, normative specification and examples.

---

# 9. Classification Model

The Classification component establishes a conceptual distinction between:

```text

                    Classification System
                    │
                    ├── Classification Model
                    │
                    ├── Classification Elements
                    │
                    ├── Classification Relationships
                    │
                    ├── Classification Constraints
                    │
                    └── Classification Assignments

```

The detailed definitions of these concepts belong to the respective Classification specifications.

---

# 10. Classification and Metadata Type

Metadata `Type` may participate in classification.

However, the semantic meaning of `Type` remains defined by Metadata.

Classification shall not redefine Metadata `Type` merely to support its own model.

The relationship between `Type`, semantic classification and physical organization shall be addressed consistently across the Documentation Framework.

In particular, the existence of physical directory distinctions shall not be interpreted as evidence that those directories define the semantics of `Type`.

---

# 11. Validation

Classification shall support validation at multiple levels:

1. element existence;
2. structural validity;
3. value validity;
4. semantic validity;
5. cross-element consistency;
6. cross-document consistency;
7. architectural consistency.

The detailed validation rules are defined by **DF-CLS-007 — Classification Validation**.

---

# 12. Governance

Classification systems shall be subject to controlled governance.

Governance concerns include:

- ownership;
- responsibility;
- approval;
- change control;
- review;
- publication;
- deprecation;
- retirement.

The detailed governance model is defined by **DF-CLS-008 — Classification Governance**.

---

# 13. Extensibility

Classification shall support controlled evolution.

Extensions may include:

- new classification categories;
- new classification elements;
- new attributes;
- schema extensions;
- new relationships;
- additional classification models.

Extensions shall preserve established semantics and maintain compatibility with existing classification definitions where required.

The detailed extensibility model is defined by **DF-CLS-011 — Classification Extensibility**.

---

# 14. Authoritative Specification

The complete normative definition of Classification is consolidated in:

**DF-CLS-014 — Classification Specification**

The other Classification documents provide the concepts, models, structures, rules and supporting material from which the specification is established.

The specification is therefore the authoritative reference for the complete Classification component.

---

# 15. Examples

Representative examples are maintained separately in:

**DF-CLS-015 — Classification Examples**

Examples are intended to demonstrate the application of the Classification specification without becoming normative definitions themselves.

---

# 16. Roadmap

The development sequence of the Classification component is defined by:

**DF-RDM-030 — Classification Roadmap**

The roadmap describes the progressive development of the component but does not itself define the Classification architecture.

---

# 17. Design Principles

The Classification component follows the following principles:

- **Semantic Independence** — Classification represents semantic organization rather than physical storage.
- **Architectural Separation** — Classification maintains clear boundaries with other Documentation Framework components.
- **Explicit Semantics** — classification concepts shall have explicit and unambiguous meanings.
- **Consistency** — classification definitions shall remain internally and cross-component consistent.
- **Traceability** — classification changes shall remain traceable.
- **Controlled Evolution** — classification systems shall evolve through defined lifecycle and governance mechanisms.
- **Extensibility** — classification shall support controlled extension.
- **Single Source of Truth** — authoritative classification concepts shall have a single canonical definition.
- **Technology Independence** — classification shall not depend on implementation technologies.

---

# 18. Component Completion

The Classification component is considered architecturally complete when its documentation establishes:

- the architectural responsibility of Classification;
- its fundamental concepts;
- its conceptual model;
- its elements;
- its schema;
- its lifecycle;
- its validation rules;
- its governance;
- its relationships;
- its constraints;
- its extensibility mechanisms;
- its best practices;
- its authoritative terminology;
- its normative specification;
- representative examples.

---

# 19. Future Evolution

Future versions of the Classification component may introduce additional capabilities such as:

- advanced taxonomy models;
- ontology-based classification;
- semantic classification;
- automated classification;
- AI-assisted classification;
- classification quality metrics;
- interoperability mechanisms;
- semantic impact analysis.

Such extensions shall preserve the architectural boundaries and principles established by the Documentation Framework.

---

# 20. Change History

| Date | Version | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| 2026-08-09 | 1.0 | Initial Classification component README. |

---

**End of Document**

### 5.1.1. Dependency

Metadata→Document Identity remains the required declaration for identification of the applicable assigned normalized document described.

The functional DID README also states: “The Document Identity component depends on the Metadata component for the canonical definition of metadata concepts used to describe document identity.” Retain Document Identity→Metadata as an actual reciprocal required claim, not optional navigation. The exact README bytes/edition evidence and comparison source hashes are in the REVIEW/UPDATE map.

Responsible owners must reconcile which indispensable concepts/interfaces are required by identity core versus descriptive records, their exact governing editions and actual use. Different scope names alone do not dissolve a real required cycle. This UPDATE corrects the blanket denial of consumer dependencies; it does not certify that these reciprocal requirements are independent or globally reconciled.

---

## 5.2. Classification

Classification owns category meaning, distinct from the key of a classified normalized document.

---

### 5.2.1. Dependency

Classification→Document Identity is the required document-identification contract for an applicable assigned normalized document receiving classification. It is not a requirement that each category/definition/assignment entity has a DF document key.

---

### 5.2.2. Purpose

Classification categorizes the intended document under its own contracts. Family/Type/Component changes do not regenerate the stable allocated series/key. A category entity's identity and a normalized document describing that category are different subjects. Classification does not redefine document-key meaning.

---

# 7. Relationships with Discovery Components

The five original Discovery responsibilities remain separate from identity allocation and actual runtime delivery. Logical contracts may constrain projections and interfaces; actual availability, freshness and results need observations.

---

## 7.1. Registry

Registry→Document Identity is the required identification contract for document registrations. Registry owns registration/index records; Document Identity owns the underlying document-key meaning. Registry→Metadata is a selected descriptor contract in ARC-005§12. Repeated records/copies do not alone prove duplicate allocation. Record exact source editions, intended target/context, provenance and freshness. Registration is not allocation, approval or a mandatory intermediary for every consumer.

---

## 7.2. Relationships

Relationships owns connection type, direction, endpoints and connection records. For a document endpoint use the intended qualified document or exact edition/context under §4.4; other typed endpoints follow their own contracts. No rule here forces all possible associations to be document-to-document. Mutable connections do not redefine the key, and canonical endpoints alone do not prove a valid connection or permanently available target.

---

## 7.3. Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph owns logical node/edge projection and representation contracts; storage/runtime technologies remain implementation choices. Knowledge Graph→Document Identity for document-node meaning and Knowledge Graph→Relationships for typed connections are selected required contracts in ARC-005§12. Neither is eliminated by calling the graph a projection.

Keep authoritative keys/connection sources distinct from projected records/properties. Nodes and properties may change while preserving intended qualified identity. Retain source edition/context, derivation, provenance, freshness and observed limitations. Projection does not allocate a new document identity, acquire connection authority or prove every peer representation is synchronized.

---

## 7.4. Navigation

Navigation uses intended identity and context to locate an applicable document or edition under its navigation contract. It can derive links and presentation records while preserving authoritative target meaning; the received prohibition on creating identity information means no competing allocation/semantic invention, not a ban on derived representation. Navigation does not guarantee successful current retrieval, require a universal Registry route or authorize silent retargeting.

---

## 7.5. Search

Search→Document Identity is the required identification contract for document-targeting search results. Other indexed entities retain their own endpoint contracts. Search owns query/result behavior, not document-key meaning. Record actual indexed source editions/context, target interpretation, freshness and result/retrieval observations. An index match does not prove allocation, complete population coverage, full identity validity or future availability.

---

# 10. Dependency Overview

The received overview mixed semantic provision, component collaboration and area order. Replace its untyped arrows with this typed view while preserving all nine original labels. It is not a mandatory serial pipeline.

<!-- original-section-view: 10 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §10 — Scoped dependency and collaboration overview.**

| Original subject | Kind / relation to Document Identity | Direction / boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Document Identity | Semantic owner/provider and actual declared consumer | Provides document-key meaning; reciprocal Metadata requirement remains unresolved |
| Metadata | Descriptor owner / required consumer and provider claims | Metadata→Document Identity (§5.1.1); Document Identity→Metadata (functional README) |
| Classification | Category owner / required document-key consumer | Classification→Document Identity for applicable classified document (§5.2.1) |
| Registry | Registration owner / required document-key consumer | Registry→Document Identity for document registrations (§7.1) |
| Relationships | Connection owner / document endpoint consumption | Relationship semantics remain with Relationships; intended document endpoints use identity contracts (§7.2) |
| Knowledge Graph | Logical projection owner / required document-node consumer | Knowledge Graph→Document Identity; typed connections also require Relationships (§7.3) |
| Governance | Area: Workflow, Policies, Reviews, Baselines | Documentary state/rule/review/exact-snapshot contracts, not one component or an executor (§6) |
| Automation | Area: five registered components | Applicable checking/generation/verification contracts, not obligatory routing (§8) |
| Integration | Area: five registered components | Actual scoped exchange/adapter contracts, not an obligatory final stage (§9) |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

Required dependency direction is consumer→provider. Foundation, Architecture, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Automation and Integration form the architectural support order under ARC-004/005; they are not a universal serial chain. Same-Layer required contracts need explicit scope/interfaces and no required cycles. Semantic ownership, documentary reference, projection, data flow and operational execution are different relations.

Selected actual requirements also include Registry→Metadata (descriptors), Knowledge Graph→Relationships (typed connections), Workflow→Metadata (state/edition), Workflow→Policies (rules), Baselines→Document Identity (logical member) and Baselines→Metadata (exact edition/pinned context), under ARC-004§§12–13 and ARC-005§12/selected component clauses. These are selected declarations, not a complete graph or supplied implementation interfaces.

The former blanket claim “Document Identity has no dependency on the consuming components” is not accepted as the current general rule: the actual README declares the reciprocal Metadata requirement. Preserve both claims and exact source evidence; responsible owner/interface reconciliation is pending. Core-versus-descriptor naming, changing relation labels or omitting an indispensable edge does not prove acyclicity. No global DAG certification follows from this source-local correction. Received view text/digest remains external evidence at this original section.

# 1. Purpose

This is the working normative specification of Document Identity for its explicitly declared documentary/domain subjects and applicable owner contracts. It consolidates scoped requirements and source roles without replacing every detailed owner definition or claiming an implemented, approved or globally reconciled component.

Two conformance subjects are distinguished. **K — assigned document key** is the governing qualified Domain+Identifier and its same-logical-document association. **R — supporting assigned identity record** represents that assigned subject with the five mandatory roles in §7, including a responsible lifecycle assertion and canonical-target descriptor. K is not a container of every mutable record or connection; R is not a new allocated document identity. Pre-allocation is a separate subject, not an assigned R whose key is absent.

This edition makes an explicit local normative decision about the previously unqualified mandatory-record and evolution clauses; the prior/new map and exact affected peer editions are retained externally and in §§7/14/20. It does not silently delete received State/Canonical Reference requirements or equate them with optional incoming relationships. Detailed serialization, canonical Metadata Element/Profile registration and complete owner/consumer propagation are not fabricated.

Normative authority follows actual applicable source declarations, subject/context and common Architecture/Policy, not Type Reference, a title, citation or received Canonical naming. DID-012 remains non-normative advice; current DID-011 architectural/evolution requirements and DID-013 qualified definitions have their own applicable roles (§§15/17). A local source correction or validation is distinct from implemented conformity, formal approval, publication and exact Baseline inclusion.

---

# 7. Canonical Elements

The five received rows remain mandatory for a **complete supporting assigned identity record R** claimed under this V2.0 R1 working specification. This is an explicit correction of the received unqualified every-identity composition: it separates the logical assigned key K from supporting record/assertion/descriptor roles. It does not make State or Canonical Reference optional to pass a complete-R claim, nor add them as immutable coordinates of K.

| Element | Qualified description / subject | Mandatory for complete assigned R |
|---|---|---|
| Document Identity | Intended assigned logical document K and same-document association represented by this record; not a second allocated identity or required recursive object field | Yes |
| Identifier | Canonical identifier interpretation/representation qualifying the intended K under responsible rules | Yes |
| Identity Domain | Governing semantic/allocation/preservation scope qualifying K | Yes |
| Identity State | Supporting actual lifecycle assertion for the assigned subject, mapped to Lifecycle State in §8 with responsible event/decision/source evidence | Yes |
| Canonical Reference | Supporting descriptor identifying the intended canonical qualified document target, or declared exact edition with required coordinates/bytes/context; it may reuse governed key rendering without an additional runtime locator | Yes |

**State role.** Identity State and Lifecycle State are controlled names for the same R assertion role here, not universal aliases for Metadata State or document Status. In assigned-R scope, Assigned, Preserved or Retired is interpreted under actual DID-006 subject/event/decision rules and its selected eight-transition contract. Unassigned denotes pre-allocation and is not an assigned R with a nonexistent K. No global permission graph or undocumented edge is granted. Supporting assertion records can change while K remains stable.

**Canonical-target role.** Canonical Reference states the intended target/interpretation and applicable source/context evidence; it is not a promised permanently available URL or a new independent identity allocation. It can concern K as a logical document, or an explicitly selected edition with additional context. A complete R needs this descriptor role, but it does not require an incoming Relationships record: external incoming document-reference population remains0..N under DID-003/005. Descriptor presence, connection validity and observed retrieval are separate checks; a historical intended target can remain interpretable while live content is unavailable. Never silently create/retarget K or immutable snapshot members.

A consumer checking only K can report that narrower coverage; it cannot call a missing-State/Canonical-Reference record a fully conformant R or infer full implementation conformance. Conversely, a pre-allocation or non-document subject is not an invalid assigned R merely because it is outside that declared claim. Full conformance needs explicit applicable subject/rule inventory (§§15/18), actual checks and unresolved-authority limits.

No implementation claiming complete R may remove an applicable mandatory role. These are logical record responsibilities, not a newly registered Metadata Element/Profile, prescribed serialization, actual populated record or approved merged implementation schema. The current working contract uses existing DID-006 assertion and DID-009/013 document-target meanings; it does not manufacture missing canonical catalogs or imply peer rollout.

**Prior/new authority and affected sources.** V1.0 R0 §§6–8 declared universal composition/mandatory State/Canonical Reference without these subjects. V2.0 R1 retains all five Yes requirements but qualifies complete assigned-R scope, Identity State↔Lifecycle State and canonical descriptor versus incoming association. DID-003/004/005/006/013 and affected consumers require comparison/propagation at their exact recorded editions. DID-005§6's selected key/association view is not silently overwritten or a waiver of R obligations. Their prior references and unresolved-field notes remain historical/current source evidence until a separately traced update qualifies them. This local decision is explicit; full owner-source agreement, canonical field registration and implementation transition are not certified.

---

# 12. Relationship Specification

All nine received subjects remain with actual semantic/record and area/component roles. Required dependencies mean consumer→provider with explicit contract/scope, source editions and interfaces; documentary authority reference, semantic association, projection, navigation and execution are different relations.

| Original subject | Kind | Qualified relationship / owner boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Metadata | Component | Descriptor/model/schema/profile/instance owner; Metadata→Document Identity for identity of the applicable normalized document described; reciprocal requirement below remains |
| Classification | Component | Category/assignment owner; applicable classified-document key consumption does not allocate DF IDs to every category/entity |
| Templates | Component | Template definition/instance contracts; applicable normalized Template-document key consumption differs from every template entity/output |
| Registry | Component | Registration/index owner; intended qualified key/edition/context and source/freshness evidence; registration is not allocation or a mandatory intermediary |
| Relationships | Component | Typed connection/endpoint/provenance owner; document endpoints consume identity meanings, other endpoint kinds retain theirs |
| Knowledge Graph | Component | Logical node/edge projection/properties with authoritative identity/connection source/context and refresh limits; no competing authority or complete graph proof |
| Governance | Area | Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines documentary contracts; actual management/decision executor and CMS scope separate |
| Automation | Area | Validation, Metadata Generator, Registry Generator, Documentation Generator and Consistency Verification capabilities; actual input/output/rule/observation/executor evidence |
| Integration | Area | Source Control Integration, CI/CD Integration, IDE Integration, Documentation Platform Integration and AI Integration optional adapters; actual authorization/mappings/contributors/checks required |

The functional DID README states: “The Document Identity component depends on the Metadata component for the canonical definition of metadata concepts used to describe document identity.” Current DID-009§5.1.1/§10 retains Document Identity→Metadata alongside Metadata→Document Identity. Preserve both actual required declarations pending responsible core-versus-descriptor/interface/source-edition reconciliation. Different scope names, projection or navigation relabelling do not dissolve a genuine required cycle.

The received all-relationships-unidirectional-towards-Identity claim is replaced, not accepted as the current general rule. Ownership/authority and typed association are not required edges; actual indispensable providers remain required even through projections. Apply ARC-004/005 support order and same-Layer explicit-interface/cycle rules; these do not require every earlier provider or a serial pipeline. No complete globally acyclic graph or integrated consumer compatibility is certified. Repeated descriptors, aliases, copies/editions and projection records are not alone duplicate allocations or semantic ownership transfer.

---

# 14. Extensibility Specification

**Current V2.0 R1 decision.** Ordinary compatible implementation extensions preserve applicable owner meanings, mandatory requirements and assigned same-document continuity. Necessary normative/foundational/responsibility/interface revision is permitted only through actual assessed common Architecture AP-015–018 and responsible change authority; it is not falsely labelled compatible merely because it is called an extension.

All five received extension subjects remain:

| Original condition | Current qualified application |
|---|---|
| preserve backward compatibility | Preserve compatible meaning where feasible for ordinary extension; necessary incompatibility requires explicit actual prior/new authority/rationale/consumer and transition evidence |
| preserve canonical identity semantics | Ordinary implementations do not silently replace owner meaning; necessary normative revision is separately assessed, not an arbitrary key reassignment |
| preserve interoperability | Evaluate actual provider/consumer/adapter/source editions and transition checks; no completed global rollout inferred |
| preserve mandatory constraints | Ordinary additions do not waive applicable requirements; necessary normative changes explicitly identify old/new mandates, authority, compatibility and affected exact sources before propagation |
| remain additive | Prefer additive compatible change when it meets the actual need; not an absolute prohibition on necessary justified normative revision |

**Received restriction and affected sources.** V1.0 R0 required every extension to be additive/backward-compatible and stated “Core identity semantics are not extensible.” That exact prior claim remains in original/map/diff/history evidence. This V2.0 R1 replaces this specification's absolute extension-only prohibition with the scoped ordinary-extension/necessary-revision contract above under common architecture. It does not leave the old absolute clause simultaneously governing the same current operation, silently rewrite the past or grant arbitrary mutation of an assigned K.

DID-005§11, DID-010§12, DID-011§§4.2/9 and DID-013§9 currently cite that received restrictive claim or its unresolved authority. Their exact current bytes/editions/hashes are in the affected-source map. They are not edited or automatically revalidated here; their prior-source references and pending notes must be qualified through a separately traced propagation step before claiming integrated agreement. Other K/R field/interface and consumer decisions likewise need actual reconciliation. The current local decision and remaining propagation are separate facts.

For any necessary term/mandate/owner/normative/domain/path/representation transition:

1. Preserve original exact artifacts, rules/editions, actual observations and failed checks. Identify prior/new meaning or mandate, actual responsible authority, intended subject/domain/context, need, alternatives and rationale.
2. Assess exact semantic/record owners, consumers and indispensable consumer→provider interfaces, mandatory field/state/reference/lifecycle effects and actual reciprocal/cycle claims. Resolve governing authority for the actual operation before asserting broader conformity; do not rename away a real required edge.
3. Record compatibility and exact old→new role/term/key/alias mappings, domain qualification, collisions/reservations/history, same-document continuity and intended reference/exact-edition/pinned-snapshot effects. Never reassign allocated/retired K to another document or silently retarget immutable historical members.
4. Apply only the separately authorized scoped change with actual contributor/event provenance, coordinated transition evidence and working edition/history. Compatible correction retains Version; compatible additive capability increments minor; incompatible contract/convention change increments major and resets minor to0. Every persisted changed document edition increments Revision monotonically across Versions; other entity allocation/lifecycle contracts remain separate.
5. Validate resulting exact artifacts/editions in the subsequent appropriate operation, recording actual checks/executor/observations/coverage/remaining peer work. Unchanged-source validation increments neither source coordinate; later changed bytes need their own assessment. Preserve earlier pending/failed events rather than rewriting them as historical success.

This UPDATE changes documentary requirements only. It executes no identity/domain migration, owner transfer, allocation, retirement, implementation rollout, formal approval, publication or Baseline selection.

---

# 15. Compliance Requirements

Conformance is a declared actual claim, not a property inferred from specification presence or a list of citations. Identify implementation/record/population scope, K/R/operation subjects/domain, exact artifacts/editions/bytes/context, applicable responsible mandatory clauses/source editions/interfaces, authority/executor, performed/unperformed checks, observations, coverage and limits before deciding the result.

The ten original owner-source subjects remain, with applicability governed by their exact responsible clauses (§17). Their requirements are not all interchangeable universal rules for every entity/context. A complete supporting-R claim retains all five §7 roles; K-only or pre-allocation observations do not imply full R/implementation conformity. Implementation conformance here includes every applicable current specification requirement and actual applicable independent owner requirements, not just a convenient subset.

# 10. Architectural Principles

The Metadata component shall conform to the following principles.

## 10.1. Technology Independence

Metadata shall not depend on implementation technologies.

---

## 10.2. Content Independence

Metadata shall remain independent of document content.

---

## 10.3. Repository Independence

Metadata shall not depend on repository organization.

---

## 10.4. Storage Independence

Metadata shall not depend on storage technologies.

---

## 10.5. Format Independence

Metadata shall not depend on document formats.

---

## 10.6. Explicit Semantics

Every Metadata element shall possess a single, well-defined meaning.

---

## 10.7. Single Source of Truth

Each Metadata concept shall possess one authoritative definition.

---

## 10.8. Extensibility

The Metadata architecture shall support future Metadata extensions without compromising existing Metadata definitions.

---

## 10.9. Backward Compatibility

Metadata evolution shall preserve compatibility with previously established Metadata whenever possible.

---

# 11. Architectural Constraints

The Metadata component shall satisfy the following architectural constraints.

- Metadata shall remain independent of implementation.
- Metadata shall remain independent of programming languages.
- Metadata shall remain independent of tooling.
- Metadata shall remain independent of repositories.
- Metadata shall remain independent of storage mechanisms.
- Metadata shall remain independent of serialization formats.
- Metadata shall not duplicate responsibilities belonging to other architectural components.

---

# 12. Relationship with Other Components

Metadata collaborates with other components while preserving strict responsibility boundaries.

| Component | Relationship |
|-----------|--------------|
| Document Identity | Consumes Metadata to describe document identity. |
| Classification | Consumes Metadata to organize documents. |
| Templates | Define how Metadata is represented in documents. |
| Workflow | Consumes Metadata during lifecycle management. |
| Policies | Uses Metadata for governance decisions. |
| Baselines | Preserve Metadata across framework evolution. |
| Registry | Indexes Metadata for document discovery. |
| Relationships | Connect Metadata across architectural entities. |
| Knowledge Graph | Uses Metadata as semantic nodes and properties. |
| Validation | Verifies Metadata compliance. |
| Automation | Produces and consumes Metadata during automated processes. |

---

# 13. Architectural Evolution

The Metadata component evolves incrementally according to the Metadata Roadmap.

Its evolution follows the progression:

1. Core Metadata
2. Structural Metadata
3. Lifecycle Metadata
4. Governance Metadata
5. Traceability Metadata
6. Discovery Metadata
7. Automation Metadata

Each stage extends the Metadata architecture without redefining previously established concepts.

---

A Metadata Element is an individual architectural unit of Metadata representing one specific descriptive characteristic of a document.

Each Metadata Element has a single architectural meaning.

# 7. Conceptual Entities

The Metadata Model is composed of the following conceptual entities.

## 7.1 Metadata

Represents the complete descriptive information associated with a document.

Metadata is composed of Metadata Elements.

---

## 7.2 Metadata Element

Represents one descriptive property of Metadata.

Each Metadata Element has one semantic meaning.

Metadata Elements are defined independently.

---

## 7.3 Metadata Value

Represents the value assigned to a Metadata Element for a specific document.

Values instantiate Metadata Elements.

---

## 7.4 Metadata Schema

Represents the formal organization of Metadata Elements.

The Schema determines which Metadata Elements may appear within a Metadata instance.

---

## 7.5 Metadata Profile

Represents a specialization of a Metadata Schema for a particular category of documents.

Profiles constrain, but do not redefine, the underlying Metadata Schema.

---

## 7.6 Metadata Instance

Represents the complete Metadata associated with one individual document.

Each Metadata Instance conforms to exactly one Metadata Profile.

---

# 8. Conceptual Relationships

The Metadata Model defines the following relationships.

| Source | Relationship | Target |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| Metadata | is composed of | Metadata Elements |
| Metadata Element | possesses | Metadata Value |
| Metadata Schema | defines | Metadata Elements |
| Metadata Profile | specializes | Metadata Schema |
| Metadata Instance | conforms to | Metadata Profile |

# 5. Definition

A Metadata Schema is the canonical structural definition of Metadata.

It defines how Metadata Elements are organized, grouped and composed.

The Schema establishes structural consistency while remaining independent of implementation.

---

# 7. Schema Composition

The Metadata Schema is composed of Metadata Elements organized into logical groups.

```text

                    Metadata Schema
                    │
                    ├── Metadata Group
                    │   ├── Metadata Element
                    │   ├── Metadata Element
                    │   └── Metadata Element
                    │
                    ├── Metadata Group
                    │   ├── Metadata Element
                    │   └── Metadata Element
                    │
                    └── Metadata Group
                        ├── Metadata Element
                        ├── Metadata Element
                        └── Metadata Element

```

Grouping exists solely to organize Metadata.

Groups do not modify the semantics of Metadata Elements.

---

# 8. Metadata Groups

Metadata Elements may be organized into conceptual groups.

Typical groups include:

- Identity Metadata
- Descriptive Metadata
- Structural Metadata
- Lifecycle Metadata
- Governance Metadata
- Traceability Metadata
- Discovery Metadata
- Automation Metadata

The Metadata Schema defines the grouping mechanism.

Individual Metadata Profiles determine which groups are applicable.

---

# 13. Structural Constraints

The Metadata Schema shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 13.1. Canonical Organization

There shall be one authoritative Metadata Schema.

---

## 13.2. Structural Independence

The Schema shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 13.3. Semantic Preservation

Structural organization shall not modify Metadata semantics.

---

## 13.4. Extensibility

The Schema shall permit new Metadata Elements without restructuring the existing architecture.

---

## 13.5. Stability

The Schema shall evolve incrementally while preserving compatibility.

---

# 15. Metadata Instance Conformance

Every Metadata Instance shall conform to exactly one Metadata Profile.

A Metadata Instance is considered structurally valid when:

- all required Metadata Elements are present;
- no prohibited Metadata Elements are present;
- structural rules defined by the Metadata Profile are respected.

Semantic validation is outside the scope of this document.

---

# 4. Relationship Principles

Metadata Relationships follow the principles below.

## 4.1. Explicitness

Every relationship shall have an explicit architectural meaning.

---

## 4.2. Semantic Stability

Relationships shall preserve the semantics of the related concepts.

---

## 4.3. Directionality

Every relationship shall define its source and target.

---

## 4.4. Independence

Relationships shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 4.5. Non-Redundancy

Equivalent relationships shall not coexist.

---

# 5. Relationship Model

Conceptually.

```text
Metadata
                    │
                    ├──────────────────────┐
                    ▼                      ▼
                Metadata               Metadata
                 Schema                 Profile
                    │                      │
                    ▼                      ▼
                Metadata                Metadata
                 Element                Instance
                    │
                    ▼

             Metadata Value
```

The Metadata Relationship Model describes how Metadata concepts are connected while preserving their responsibilities.

---

# 8. Specialization Relationships

Specialization relationships express refinement.

Examples include:

| Source | Relationship | Target |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| Metadata Profile | specializes | Metadata Schema |
| Extended Metadata | specializes | Standard Metadata |

Specialization preserves the semantics of the parent concept while introducing controlled constraints.

---

# 9. Association Relationships

Association relationships express logical connections without ownership.

Examples include:

| Source | Relationship | Target |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| Metadata Element | is described by | Metadata Dictionary |
| Metadata Profile | references | Metadata Groups |
| Metadata Schema | organizes | Metadata Groups |

Associations preserve independence between architectural entities.

---

# 10. Dependency Relationships

Dependency relationships identify architectural reliance.

Examples include:

| Source | Depends On |
|----------|------------|
| Metadata Validation | Metadata Schema |
| Metadata Validation | Metadata Profiles |
| Metadata Governance | Metadata Lifecycle |
| Metadata Dictionary | Metadata Elements |

Dependencies shall never introduce circular architectural dependencies.

---

# 13. Relationship Constraints

Metadata Relationships shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 13.1. No Semantic Modification

Relationships shall not redefine Metadata concepts.

---

## 13.2. No Ownership Transfer

Relationships shall not transfer architectural responsibilities.

---

## 13.3. No Circular Dependencies

Architectural dependency cycles shall not exist.

---

## 13.4. Canonical Relationships

Equivalent relationships shall possess one authoritative definition.

---

## 13.5. Consistency

Relationships shall preserve Metadata architectural consistency.

---
