# 4. Constraint Principles

Metadata Constraints follow the principles below.

## 4.1. Architectural Integrity

Constraints shall preserve the integrity of the Metadata architecture.

---

## 4.2. Technology Independence

Constraints shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 4.3. Stability

Constraints shall preserve long-term architectural stability.

---

## 4.4. Explicit Definition

Every constraint shall possess an explicit architectural meaning.

---

## 4.5. Verifiability

Constraints shall be objectively verifiable.

---

# 5. Constraint Categories

The Metadata component defines five categories of constraints.

- Conceptual Constraints
- Structural Constraints
- Semantic Constraints
- Evolution Constraints
- Dependency Constraints

Each category governs a specific aspect of the Metadata architecture.

---

# 7. Structural Constraints

Structural Constraints govern the organization of Metadata.

## 7.1. S-001 — Canonical Schema

There shall be one authoritative Metadata Schema.

---

## 7.2. S-002 — Element Organization

Metadata Elements shall be organized exclusively through the Metadata Schema.

---

## 7.3. S-003 — Profile Specialization

Metadata Profiles shall specialize, but never redefine, the Metadata Schema.

---

## 7.4. S-004 — Structural Consistency

Metadata organization shall remain internally consistent.

---

# 8. Semantic Constraints

Semantic Constraints preserve the meaning of Metadata.

## 8.1. M-001 — Stable Semantics

Metadata Elements shall preserve their semantic meaning throughout their lifecycle.

---

## 8.2. M-002 — No Semantic Overloading

A Metadata Element shall represent one concept only.

---

## 8.3. M-003 — Semantic Preservation

Structural organization shall never alter semantic meaning.

---

## 8.4. M-004 — Canonical Interpretation

Metadata shall possess one authoritative interpretation.

---

# 9. Evolution Constraints

Evolution Constraints preserve compatibility over time.

## 9.1. E-001 — Controlled Evolution

Metadata shall evolve only through architectural governance.

---

## 9.2. E-002 — Backward Compatibility

Metadata evolution shall preserve compatibility whenever reasonably possible.

---

## 9.3. E-003 — Controlled Deprecation

Metadata shall be deprecated before retirement.

---

## 9.4. E-004 — Historical Preservation

Deprecated and retired Metadata shall remain documented.

---

# 10. Dependency Constraints

Dependency Constraints regulate architectural dependencies.

## 10.1. D-001 — No Circular Dependencies

Circular dependencies between Metadata artifacts shall not exist.

---

## 10.2. D-002 — Explicit Dependencies

Dependencies shall be explicitly documented.

---

## 10.3. D-003 — Dependency Stability

Dependencies shall preserve architectural stability.

---

## 10.4. D-004 — Responsibility Preservation

Dependencies shall not transfer architectural responsibilities.

---

# 12. Constraint Enforcement

Metadata Constraints define architectural obligations.

Enforcement mechanisms are intentionally outside the scope of this specification.

Constraint enforcement may be performed by:

- Metadata Validation;
- Metadata Governance;
- implementation-specific mechanisms.

The architectural constraints themselves remain implementation independent.

---

# 6. Conceptual Constraints

Conceptual Constraints preserve the meaning of Metadata concepts.

## 6.1. C-001 — Unique Concept Definition

Every Metadata concept shall possess exactly one canonical definition.

---

## 6.2. C-002 — Single Responsibility

Each Metadata concept shall represent one architectural responsibility only.

---

## 6.3. C-003 — Concept Independence

Metadata concepts shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 6.4. C-004 — Non-Redundancy

Equivalent Metadata concepts shall not coexist.

---

# 11. Constraint Relationships

The different constraint categories complement one another.

```text

          Conceptual Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

          Structural Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

          Semantic Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

          Evolution Constraints
                    │
                    ▼

          Dependency Constraints

```

Together they define the architectural boundaries of the Metadata component.

---

# 14. Relationship with Other Metadata Documents

Metadata Constraints provide the architectural boundaries for the remaining Metadata specifications.

| Document | Relationship |
|----------|--------------|
| Metadata Concepts | Defines constrained concepts. |
| Metadata Model | Organizes constrained concepts. |
| Metadata Elements | Defines constrained building blocks. |
| Metadata Schema | Applies structural constraints. |
| Metadata Lifecycle | Applies evolution constraints. |
| Metadata Validation | Verifies constraint compliance. |
| Metadata Governance | Controls constraint evolution. |

---

# 15. Architectural Characteristics

Metadata Constraints possess the following characteristics.

## 15.1. Canonical

There is one authoritative set of Metadata Constraints.

---

## 15.2. Stable

Constraints evolve only through controlled governance.

---

## 15.3. Technology Independent

Constraints remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 15.4. Deterministic

Constraint evaluation shall produce consistent outcomes.

---

## 15.5. Traceable

Every constraint shall possess a stable architectural identity.

---

## 15.6. Extensible

New constraints may be introduced without invalidating existing constraints.

---

# 17. Related Documents

## 17.1. Architecture

- DF-ARC-002 — Architectural Principles
- DF-ARC-003 — Architectural Concepts
- DF-ARC-005 — Architectural Components

## 17.2. Metadata

- DF-MTD-001 — Metadata Architecture

- DF-MTD-004 — Metadata Elements
- DF-MTD-005 — Metadata Schema

- DF-MTD-009 — Metadata Relationships

- DF-MTD-013 — Metadata Dictionary
- DF-MTD-014 — Metadata Specification

---

**End of Document**

# 6. Lifecycle States

## 6.1. Proposed

A Metadata artifact has been identified as necessary but has not yet been formally defined.

Characteristics:

- architectural proposal;
- no normative status;
- subject to review.

---

## 6.2. Defined

The Metadata artifact has received a complete architectural definition.

Characteristics:

- canonical definition exists;
- semantics established;
- under architectural review.

---

## 6.3. Approved

The Metadata artifact has been formally accepted by architectural governance.

Characteristics:

- approved semantics;
- approved structure;
- eligible for publication.

---

## 6.4. Published

The Metadata artifact becomes part of the official Documentation Framework.

Characteristics:

- normative status;
- publicly referenced;
- available for use by Metadata Profiles.

---

## 6.5. Deprecated

The Metadata artifact should no longer be used for new specifications.

Characteristics:

- retained for compatibility;
- superseded by newer Metadata;
- still documented.

Existing Metadata remains valid.

---

## 6.6. Retired

The Metadata artifact has reached the end of its architectural lifecycle.

Characteristics:

- no longer recommended;
- preserved for historical traceability;
- excluded from future Metadata Profiles.

Historical Metadata Instances remain interpretable.

---

# 7. Lifecycle Transitions

The permitted lifecycle transitions are:

```text

                Proposed
                    │
                    ▼

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

                Published
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

Reverse transitions shall not occur except through formal architectural governance.

---

# 8. Lifecycle Responsibilities

The Metadata Lifecycle defines responsibilities for each stage.

| Lifecycle Stage | Responsibility |
|-----------------|----------------|
| Proposed | Identify new Metadata requirements. |
| Defined | Produce canonical architectural definitions. |
| Approved | Validate architectural consistency. |
| Published | Make Metadata available for framework use. |
| Deprecated | Preserve compatibility while discouraging new usage. |
| Retired | Preserve historical reference only. |

---

# 10. Lifecycle Constraints

The Metadata Lifecycle shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 10.1. Controlled Introduction

New Metadata shall enter the lifecycle through the Proposed state.

---

## 10.2. No Implicit Approval

Metadata shall never become normative without explicit approval.

---

## 10.3. Semantic Preservation

Lifecycle transitions shall not redefine Metadata semantics.

---

## 10.4. Controlled Deprecation

Metadata shall not be removed immediately after deprecation.

---

## 10.5. Historical Preservation

Retired Metadata shall remain documented.

---

# 13. Relationship with Metadata Profiles

Metadata Profiles evolve independently from the Metadata Lifecycle.

A Metadata Profile may:

- adopt newly published Metadata;
- continue supporting deprecated Metadata;
- migrate to newer Metadata versions.

Profiles shall not alter the lifecycle status of Metadata.

---

# 1. Introduction

The Documentation Framework relies on Metadata to provide consistent, structured and reliable descriptions of documents.

To preserve architectural integrity, Metadata shall satisfy a set of validation rules that ensure compliance with the Metadata Architecture, Metadata Model and Metadata Schema.

This document defines the architectural principles governing Metadata Validation.

---

# 4. Validation Principles

Metadata Validation follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Architectural Validation

Validation verifies architectural conformance.

It shall not introduce new Metadata.

---

## 4.2. Deterministic Validation

Given the same Metadata and the same specification, validation shall always produce the same result.

---

## 4.3. Independent Validation

Validation shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 4.4. Non-Destructive Validation

Validation shall never modify Metadata.

It only evaluates conformance.

---

## 4.5. Explicit Validation

Validation outcomes shall be explicit and reproducible.

---

# 6. Validation Model

Conceptually.

```text

            Metadata Instance
                    │
                    ▼

           Metadata Validation
                    │
                    ├──────────────────────┐
                    ▼                      ▼
             Validation Rules      Validation Results

```

Validation evaluates Metadata against a predefined set of architectural rules.

---

# 9. Validation Process

Conceptually.

```text

            Metadata Instance
                    │
                    ▼

          Structural Validation
                    │
                    ▼

           Profile Validation
                    │
                    ▼

           Semantic Validation
                    │
                    ▼

         Consistency Validation
                    │
                    ▼

            Validation Result

```

Implementations may optimize execution while preserving equivalent validation outcomes.

---

# 10. Validation Results

Validation produces explicit outcomes.

Possible outcomes include:

- Valid
- Valid with Warnings
- Invalid

Validation Results shall include sufficient information to identify the violated validation rules.

---

# 11. Validation Severity

Validation findings may possess different severity levels.

Typical severity levels include:

- Information
- Warning
- Error
- Critical

Severity classification does not modify Metadata.

It supports architectural assessment.

---

# 12. Validation Constraints

Metadata Validation shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 12.1. Technology Independence

Validation shall not depend on implementation technologies.

---

## 12.2. Repeatability

Validation shall always produce reproducible results.

---

## 12.3. Traceability

Validation Results shall identify the Validation Rules that produced them.

---

## 12.4. Non-Intrusive

Validation shall never modify Metadata.

---

## 12.5. Architectural Consistency

Validation shall preserve the Documentation Framework architecture.

---

# 14. Relationship with Other Components

Metadata Validation collaborates with multiple architectural components.

| Component | Relationship |
|-----------|--------------|
| Metadata Schema | Defines structural validation rules. |
| Metadata Profiles | Define profile-specific validation. |
| Metadata Dictionary | Provides canonical Metadata definitions. |
| Governance | Consumes validation outcomes. |
| Workflow | May invoke validation during document evolution. |
| Automation | May execute validation automatically. |

Validation consumes architectural definitions but does not own them.

---

# 16. Architectural Characteristics

Metadata Validation possesses the following characteristics.

## 16.1. Deterministic

Validation outcomes are predictable.

---

## 16.2. Independent

Validation is implementation independent.

---

## 16.3. Extensible

New Validation Rules may be introduced without changing the Validation Architecture.

---

## 16.4. Traceable

Every Validation Result can be traced to one or more Validation Rules.

---

## 16.5. Reusable

Validation Rules may be reused across Metadata Profiles.

---

## 16.6. Non-Destructive

Validation never alters Metadata.

---

# 18. Related Documents

## 18.1. Architecture

- DF-ARC-002 — Architectural Principles
- DF-ARC-005 — Architectural Components

## 18.2. Metadata

- DF-MTD-001 — Metadata Architecture
- DF-MTD-002 — Metadata Concepts

- DF-MTD-009 — Metadata Relationships
- DF-MTD-013 — Metadata Dictionary
- DF-MTD-014 — Metadata Specification

**End of Document**

# 1. Introduction

Metadata is a strategic architectural asset of the Documentation Framework.

To preserve its integrity, consistency and long-term stability, Metadata shall be governed through a controlled architectural governance process.

Metadata Governance establishes the policies, responsibilities and decision mechanisms required to manage the evolution of Metadata while preserving the architectural principles of the Documentation Framework.

---

# 4. Governance Principles

Metadata Governance follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Architectural Authority

All Metadata shall be governed according to the Documentation Framework architecture.

---

## 4.2. Controlled Evolution

Metadata shall evolve only through explicit architectural decisions.

---

## 4.3. Traceability

Governance decisions shall be documented and traceable.

---

## 4.4. Consistency

Governance shall preserve conceptual consistency throughout the Metadata architecture.

---

## 4.5. Stability

Existing Metadata shall remain stable whenever possible.

---

## 4.6. Transparency

Governance decisions shall be explicit and reproducible.

---

# 6. Governance Model

Conceptually.

```text

             Metadata Change
                    │
                    ▼

          Governance Evaluation
                    │
                    ▼

         Architectural Decision
                    │
                    ├──────────────────────┐
                    ▼                      ▼
                 Approved              Rejected
                    │
                    ▼

            Metadata Evolution
```

Governance evaluates proposed changes without modifying Metadata directly.

---

# 10. Governance Process

Conceptually.

```text

                Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

          Architectural Review
                    │
                    ▼

         Consistency Assessment
                    │
                    ▼

             Impact Analysis
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision
                    │
                    ▼

               Publication

```

The governance process is technology independent.

---

# 11. Governance Outcomes

Governance produces explicit decisions.

Possible outcomes include:

- Approved
- Approved with Conditions
- Deferred
- Rejected
- Deprecated

Each decision shall include its justification.

---

# 12. Governance Constraints

Metadata Governance shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 12.1. Architectural Independence

Governance shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 12.2. Explicit Decisions

Implicit governance decisions shall not exist.

---

## 12.3. Traceable Decisions

Every governance decision shall be documented.

---

## 12.4. Controlled Authority

Only approved Metadata becomes part of the canonical Metadata architecture.

---

## 12.5. Preservation

Governance shall preserve existing Metadata whenever reasonably possible.

---

# 14. Relationship with Metadata Lifecycle

Metadata Governance controls lifecycle transitions.

Examples include:

- Proposed → Defined
- Defined → Approved
- Approved → Published
- Published → Deprecated
- Deprecated → Retired

The Metadata Lifecycle defines the states.

Metadata Governance authorizes transitions between those states.

# 15. Relationship with Metadata Validation

Metadata Validation determines whether Metadata conforms to the Metadata specification.

Metadata Governance determines whether Metadata should become part of the Documentation Framework.

Validation answers:

> "Is the Metadata compliant?"

Governance answers:

> "Should the Metadata be accepted?"

The two responsibilities are complementary but independent.

---

# 16. Relationship with Other Components

| Component | Relationship |
|-----------|--------------|
| Metadata Lifecycle | Governance authorizes lifecycle transitions. |
| Metadata Validation | Validation provides evidence for governance decisions. |
| Metadata Dictionary | Governance approves Metadata definitions. |
| Metadata Schema | Governance approves structural evolution. |
| Metadata Profiles | Governance authorizes new profiles. |
| Architecture | Governance preserves architectural consistency. |

Governance consumes architectural information but does not redefine it.

---

# 18. Architectural Characteristics

Metadata Governance possesses the following characteristics.

## 18.1. Authoritative

Governance produces authoritative architectural decisions.

---

## 18.2. Traceable

Every decision is documented.

---

## 18.3. Deterministic

Equivalent governance criteria shall produce equivalent decisions.

---

## 18.4. Independent

Governance remains independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 18.5. Extensible

New governance processes may be introduced without altering the Metadata architecture.

---

## 18.6. Stable

Governance protects the long-term stability of Metadata.

---

# 20. Related Documents

## 20.1. Architecture

- DF-ARC-001 — Architecture Overview
- DF-ARC-002 — Architectural Principles
- DF-ARC-005 — Architectural Components

## 20.2. Metadata

- DF-MTD-001 — Metadata Architecture
- DF-MTD-002 — Metadata Concepts
- DF-MTD-003 — Metadata Model
- DF-MTD-004 — Metadata Elements
- DF-MTD-005 — Metadata Schema
- DF-MTD-006 — Metadata Lifecycle
- DF-MTD-007 — Metadata Validation
- DF-MTD-009 — Metadata Relationships
- DF-MTD-010 — Metadata Constraints
- DF-MTD-013 — Metadata Dictionary
- DF-MTD-014 — Metadata Specification

---

**End of Document**

---

# 4. Extensibility Principles

Metadata Extensibility follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Architectural Stability

Extensions shall preserve the stability of the Metadata architecture.

---

## 4.2. Backward Compatibility

Extensions shall not invalidate existing Metadata.

---

## 4.3. Canonical Preservation

Extensions shall preserve canonical Metadata definitions.

---

## 4.4. Technology Independence

Extension mechanisms shall remain implementation independent.

---

## 4.5. Controlled Evolution

Extensions shall be introduced only through architectural governance.

---

# 8. Extension Categories

Metadata extensions may belong to one of the following categories.

## 8.1. Additive Extension

Introduces new Metadata without affecting existing Metadata.

Preferred extension mechanism.

---

## 8.2. Specialization Extension

Creates specialized Metadata Profiles derived from the canonical Metadata Schema.

---

## 8.3. Organizational Extension

Introduces new Metadata Groups to improve structural organization.

---

## 8.4. Evolutionary Extension

Introduces architectural refinements through controlled Metadata evolution.

---

# 9. Extension Constraints

Metadata extensions shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 9.1. E-001 — No Semantic Redefinition

Existing Metadata semantics shall not be modified.

---

## 9.2. E-002 — No Responsibility Transfer

Extensions shall not alter architectural responsibilities.

---

## 9.3. E-003 — No Architectural Fragmentation

Extensions shall preserve a single canonical Metadata architecture.

---

## 9.4. E-004 — Compatibility Preservation

Extensions shall preserve interoperability whenever reasonably possible.

---

## 9.5. E-005 — Governance Approval

Every extension shall be approved through Metadata Governance.

---

# 10. Extension Process

Conceptually.

```text

            Extension Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

           Architecture Review
                    │
                    ▼

             Impact Analysis
                    │
                    ▼

        Compatibility Assessment
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Approval
                    │
                    ▼

            Metadata Evolution

```

The extension process is independent of implementation technologies.

---

# 13. Relationship with Metadata Validation

Metadata Validation verifies that extensions conform to the Metadata architecture.

Validation does not authorize extensions.

Authorization belongs to Metadata Governance.

---

## 15.3. Compatible

Extensions maintain interoperability.

---

## 6.5. R-005 — Profile Compliance

Metadata shall satisfy the requirements of the applicable Metadata Profile.

---

# 7. Structural Requirements

Metadata shall satisfy the following structural requirements.

- Metadata shall be organized through Metadata Schemas.
- Metadata Profiles shall specialize Metadata Schemas.
- Metadata Instances shall conform to Metadata Profiles.
- Metadata Elements shall be defined by the Metadata Dictionary.
- Metadata relationships shall preserve architectural consistency.

---

# 8. Semantic Requirements

Metadata shall satisfy the following semantic requirements.

- Every Metadata Element shall possess one canonical meaning.
- Semantic definitions shall remain stable.
- Equivalent Metadata Elements shall not coexist.
- Metadata terminology shall remain consistent.
- Metadata interpretation shall be deterministic.

---

## 2. Normalized documents and functional files

Every file named README.md, CHANGELOG.md or ArchitecturalMilestones.md in this corpus is a non-normalized functional file. It retains its name and does not require Document ID, Family, Type, Component, Version, Revision, Status or Baseline by virtue of document normalization. Do not infer a finding from absence of those fields. Do not automatically delete legitimate existing information.

These files remain in inventories, SHA-256 manifests, content reviews and applicable structural, terminology, reference and consistency checks. CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md retain their own entry/milestone IDs, states, dates and historical conventions. Their maintenance is not conditional on normalized document metadata.

The input corpus comprises 79 documents within normalization scope and 8 non-normalized files. Two normalized review documents are introduced by Step 3. Machine-readable exports attached to DF-RVW-002 are representations of its inventories and matrices, not independent normalized documents or new authorities. Each export identifies its parent document and edition in its manifest or accompanying report.

## 3. Classification contract

### 3.1. Uniform Type

Type identifies the primary responsibility of every normalized document and uses exactly one value from {Architecture, Structure, Behavior, Reference}. There are no special Type values for Foundation, Architecture, global roadmaps or review artifacts.

| Type | Primary responsibility |
|---|---|
| Architecture | Foundations, principles, concepts, conceptual models/elements and architectural decisions. |
| Structure | Organization, composition, schemas, structural relationships, restrictions and element catalogs. |
| Behavior | Processes, lifecycle, validation, governance, extensibility and planned evolution. |
| Reference | Consultation, terminology, consolidated specifications, examples, recommendations and historical records. |

Use the spelling Behavior. Base, Core, Schema, Dictionary and Lifecycle are not additional Type values. A historical evolution account is Reference; a process or evolution plan is Behavior. Assess content and primary responsibility rather than filename or directory alone. Normative or informative authority is established by explicit statements/references, never by Type=Reference alone. Validation is not approval.

### 3.2. Family and Component

| Document category | Family | Component |
|---|---|---|
| Belongs to a component | Canonical component name | Same canonical name, when the field is used. |
| Foundation without a component | Foundation | Absent/not applicable. |
| Architecture without a component | Architecture | Absent/not applicable. |
| Global roadmap or global implementation strategy | Roadmap | Absent/not applicable. |
| This review's policy/report | Reviews | Reviews. |

Roadmap is an explicitly scoped documentary planning area for global, non-component plans. It reuses the received Family value in DF-RDM-001/002, not an invented component or Layer. These two documents use Type=Behavior. The existing Component=Documentation Framework in DF-RDM-002 must be assessed and removed from its working header in the scheduled UPDATE: the framework is the container, not a component of itself.

Component roadmaps belong to the component they plan and therefore use Family=component, Type=Behavior and matching Component, regardless of central storage under Roadmaps. Current component names are Metadata, Document Identity, Classification and Templates. DocumentIdentity is a directory alias, not a competing canonical component name.

Do not remove Component indiscriminately. The global roadmap decision is localized and does not remove it from component documents. Family/Type changes do not determine document identity or structural Layer allocation.

### 3.3. Class

Class remains a separate, optional semantic dimension. This policy does not create a complete Class vocabulary or make it mandatory. Retain received values as evidence, then assess each use in its document cycle. A value that merely repeats Type or misstates authority must be reconciled with evidence. New review artifacts omit Class because no additional distinction is needed. Optional does not mean unrestricted: any value used must have an explicit, non-conflicting definition.

## 4. Identity convention for this corpus and review artifacts

### 4.1. Representation and uniqueness

The identity domain is Documentation Framework. Its representation prefix is DF. A working normalized document identifier follows DF-SSS-NNN, where SSS is a registered three-letter uppercase allocation-series code and NNN is a three-digit positive allocation number, 001–999. The full identifier is unique within the domain. Numbers are allocated within a series; equal numeric suffixes across different series are not collisions.

Series codes are stable allocation namespaces, not the document's current Family, Type, component, location, version or revision. Preserve existing valid identifiers when those characteristics change. A series' original purpose is recorded for traceability, but it does not recalculate an existing document ID after reassignment/reclassification.

| Series | Received origin/purpose | Step 3 action |
|---|---|---|
| FND | Foundation documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| ARC | Framework Architecture documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| MTD | Metadata documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| DID | Document Identity documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| CLS | Classification documents | Preserve unambiguous allocations; resolve the nominal CLS-003 collision. |
| TPL | Templates documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| RDM | Planning documents | Preserve allocations even when Family becomes a component name. |
| RVW | Review policy and consolidated review report | Allocate 001 to this policy and 002 to DF-RVW-002 after collision checks. |

This is a corpus convention, not a format imposed on identities in other domains or an identifier-generation implementation. Scheduled reconciliation of DF-DID-005/010/014 owns its integration into the identity contract. Foundation and Classification must qualify the earlier Family/Type-based convention accordingly.

### 4.2. Allocation, reservations and retirement

New allocation requires an explicit series record and collision scan of headers, filenames, references, historical/reserved records and this review's allocation register. Do not reuse allocated/retired numbers. A gap does not prove availability; when allocation history is unavailable, record that limitation and use a documented allocation decision rather than infer a historical reservation. Missing IDs are not assigned to the eight functional files excluded in §2.

000 is not allocated under this working convention; it is not implicitly a README code. RVW-001/002 are the only new allocations at Step 3; no future numbers are reserved. At 999, do not widen the syntax or silently recycle: register another unused three-letter series with traceable continuation and preserve all old IDs. A new domain is a separate semantic decision, not a shortcut for renumbering this corpus.

Maintain an allocation register in DF-RVW-002's exports, including series, number, identifier, path, allocation status and evidence. Retired IDs remain reserved. The source archive and the input manifest preserve received declarations, including invalid ones; preservation is evidence, not acceptance of a collision.

### 4.3. Localized correction and historical syntax

No general ID migration is required by the adopted classification change. The nominal DF-CLS-003-ClassificationModel.md wrongly declares DF-CLS-001 and repeats the Architecture prose. Its correction is pending a distinct document recovery/update and path-scoped map. It is not a global DF-CLS-001→DF-CLS-003 replacement or an alias that makes one identifier resolve to two documents.

Operational references must resolve to the intended final identity/path after a coordinated correction. Historical examples such as META-DCL-001, or earlier roadmap forms containing RDM as an extra segment, must be explicitly qualified where historical or revised where they purport to prescribe the current working convention. Do not rewrite history as if the new convention had always existed.

Metadata Element IDs, document IDs, finding IDs, CHANGELOG numbers and Milestone IDs are separate entities. Creating this policy does not assign Metadata Element IDs or create element lifecycle/publication records.

## 5. Version, Revision, Status and Baseline

### 5.1. Received evidence

The 79 in-scope input documents declare Version 1.0 and Baseline 1.0; 73 declare Revision 0 and six Foundation documents do not declare Revision. Historical sources distinguish significant Version evolution from backward-compatible Revision changes: DF-FND-002 §6.6 and DF-FND-004 §§4.10/6.8. Neither establishes a complete numerical successor contract for this review. The following working rule formalizes that gap while preserving input evidence.

### 5.2. Edition successors

Version uses the observed major.minor numeric form. Revision is a monotonic integer per document across version changes during this review.

| Change | Version action | Revision action |
|---|---|---|
| Compatible correction/clarification/reclassification preserving contractual meaning | Keep Version. | Increment declared Revision by one; use 1 when absent. |
| Compatible additive contract capability | Increment minor by one. | Increment declared Revision by one; use 1 when absent. |
| Incompatible contract/convention change | Increment major by one and set minor to 0. | Increment declared Revision by one; use 1 when absent. |
| Validation/reporting with no source content change | Keep Version. | Keep Revision; track the event centrally. |
| New normalized review document | Initial Version 1.0. | Initial Revision 1; no invented Revision 0 history. |

Explain compatibility per UPDATE. Changing a classification label does not automatically change Version; replacing what a classification/schema contract permits may be incompatible even if no IDs change. Assess changes to identity syntax/resolution separately from a filename correction. Do not reset an existing Revision counter on Version changes during this review. Future alternative numbering requires a traceable policy change, not an implied reset.

Each completed persisted working edition with changed content receives its successor. Draft editing before an edition is finalized is preparation, not evidence of completed intermediate editions. If a validated/finalized edition needs a correction, create another successor and retain the failed validation event. No source revision is incremented merely to record this policy's adoption.

### 5.3. Working lifecycle and Baseline

Edited working documents start at Status=Draft, including successors of received Approved/Canonical documents. A subsequent explicit submission may use Review; formal approval/publication requires its own decision/evidence. Leave untouched source statuses unchanged. Canonical in a received header is preserved as historical evidence, not automatically granted to a successor or silently converted into Approved.

A newly created or modified working edition has Baseline=Not assigned unless its exact inclusion is evidenced. Record original Status and Baseline in the edition history and input manifest. Do not change the original Baseline snapshot. Draft is a lifecycle state; Not assigned is an explicit absence marker in the human-readable working header, not a new Baseline identifier.

At Step 3 creation, this policy and DF-RVW-002 were Draft, Version 1.0, Revision 1, Baseline Not assigned. Current working coordinates follow their headers and exact edition histories. Passing their scoped checks does not approve/publish them or place them in a Baseline. The conventions for these working headers do not populate the canonical Metadata Dictionary or create a Metadata Profile lifecycle event by implication.

## 6. REVIEW, UPDATE, VALIDATE and evidence

Keep Step 1–7 and document substep numbers 4.01–4.87 stable. Step 3.1 identifies this policy; Step 3.2 identifies the consolidated report. The eight functional files keep their scheduled content/reference substeps but have no normalization requirement.

REVIEW reports findings, sections, severity, proposed correction and closure evidence without modifying the reviewed source. UPDATE shows exact material before/after, compatibility assessment, full updated source, diff, edition history, central CHANGELOG entry and Milestone. Mark source corrections pending validation. VALIDATE compares the exact updated edition with its input and affected sources, checks related occurrences and records outcome/limits with SHA-256 evidence. A failure creates a traceable corrective step.

Before any cross-document normative change or path/ID migration, identify the batch, rationale, affected documents and previous/new mapping. Do not claim integrated consistency during partial rollout. Resolve semantic references and actual dependencies separately; do not use a renamed relationship type to conceal a mandatory dependency cycle.

Finding states used for this review are Open, Corrected—pending validation, Closed—verified and Not applicable—scope decision. These tracking states are not document Status, element lifecycle or Milestone Status. Closure requires evidence; scope exclusion requires the specific decision. INV-02 is Not applicable because the user excluded the eight functional files, not because IDs were assigned or validation passed.

The input/final/validated manifests record paths, identity and edition where applicable, SHA-256 and scope. Evidence exports are attached to DF-RVW-002. A manifest's own hash belongs in its delivery receipt/enclosing package, not recursively inside its own contents. A document's hash is recorded outside the document itself. Validation logs do not force recursive revisions of themselves.

## 7. Central CHANGELOG and Milestones

Reuse CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md, retaining their historical content. They remain non-normalized. Keep the CHANGELOG's sequential #, reverse chronology, Author, Type, Document, Impact and Description columns. Add Reviewed and Validated event types to distinguish executed reviews/checks from document content updates; these event Types are not document Type values. Existing Created/Updated/etc. and impact values remain in force.

### 7.1. Cumulative documentary authorship

The normalized document header's **Author** field lists all evidenced authors who contributed to the document, including its original author and contributors to later editions. Use **semicolon followed by a space (`; `)** between distinct authors. Preserve established names and role qualifications; retain first evidenced contribution order and do not duplicate an author for each revision. Example: `Arnaldo Figueira; Codex — AI assistant`.

Carry forward evidenced original/prior authors when preparing a successor. Record each later contributor when that contribution is supported by source history, exact edition/diff evidence or explicit reliable attribution. Preserve edition history separately so the cumulative header does not imply that every listed author performed every change. When original authorship is absent or unknown, list only known contributors and retain that limitation; do not guess an author from ownership, filename, user identity or authorization. A later substantiated attribution receives a traceable correction.

A user who actually edits document content is recorded as an author when that contribution and identity are established. Permission, instructions, approval or file custody alone do not prove an authored contribution. Later disk changes must be examined as resulting bytes with attribution evidence; earlier validation results do not automatically apply. The author list is provenance, not a blanket assignment of approval or responsibility for consequences of every later final product.

### 7.2. Event-specific CHANGELOG authorship

The CHANGELOG **Author** column records the evidenced contributors who performed that particular event, using the same `; ` separator when the event has multiple authors. It is not copied automatically from the cumulative document header. Use `Codex — AI assistant` for events performed solely by this assistant; do not attribute the event to the user merely because the user authorized it. # 4. Governance Principles

Classification Governance follows the principles below.

---

## 4.1 Architectural Authority

Classification shall be governed according to the Documentation Framework architecture.

Governance decisions shall preserve the responsibilities assigned to Classification.

**Current governing scope.** Authority must be established for the actual subject, source edition, scope and decision. Architecture citations do not identify every authorized actor or delegation. Known owner mandates remain binding while missing actor/guard/evidence is recorded as a real limit, not filled by an invented organizational role.

---

## 4.2 Controlled Evolution

Classification shall evolve only through explicit architectural decisions.

Uncontrolled modification of canonical Classification definitions is prohibited.

The corresponding Metadata principle establishes that architectural evolution occurs only through explicit decisions.

**Current governing scope.** Ordinary compatible preservation and necessary assessed normative, foundational, role, interface or domain revision follow §§15/30/65.5/72. Explicit decision requirements do not imply that this documentary UPDATE performs a canonical decision or prohibit the authorized Draft correction.

---

## 4.3 Traceability

Classification governance decisions shall be documented and traceable.

Every approved, rejected, deferred, deprecated or retired Classification change shall have an identifiable governance decision.

**Current governing scope.** Traceability includes Approved with Conditions and every actual outcome, with actual proposal, subject/edition, authority, evidence, conditions and rationale. Preserve earlier rejected, deferred and pending events as such; a later success is a new event, not a rewrite of earlier history.

---

## 4.4 Consistency

Governance shall preserve conceptual consistency throughout the Classification architecture.

Family, Type and Class must continue to retain their established responsibilities.

**Current governing scope.** The established current responsibilities are the working roles in §§1/11–13. Received broad-domain Family and Family-specializing Type are historical meanings, not competing current rules. Context may constrain applicable uses without redefining uniform primary responsibility or creating a Family-owned Type vocabulary.

---

## 4.5 Stability

Existing Classification definitions shall remain stable whenever reasonably possible.

Evolution should avoid unnecessary disruption to existing documents and Classification consumers.

**Current governing scope.** The reasonable-possibility qualification permits necessary assessed change; it does not waive required historical interpretation or independent applicable rules. Assess actual compatibility, disruption and alternatives rather than promising unchanged semantics for an incompatible replacement.

---

## 4.6 Transparency

Governance decisions shall be explicit and reproducible.

Implicit governance decisions shall not form part of the canonical Classification architecture.

These principles directly reflect the established Metadata Governance principles of architectural authority, controlled evolution, traceability, consistency, stability and transparency.

**Current governing scope.** Reproducible means an actual decision and its basis can be examined and compared under the identified context (§65.3). Equivalent labels alone do not prove equivalent authority, evidence, conditions, judgment or effects, nor an implemented deterministic algorithm.

---

# 6. Governance Model

The conceptual governance model is:

**Received unnamed visual in §6 (span 1 in original order).** Exact received text below is evidence, not a second governing rule.

```text

          Classification Change
                    │
                    ▼

          Governance Evaluation
                    │
                    ▼

          Architectural Decision
                    │
                    ├───────────────────┬───────────────────┐
                    ▼                   ▼                   ▼

                 Approved            Deferred            Rejected
                    │
                    ▼

         Classification Evolution

```

**Current relation scope:** Selected three-outcome conceptual evaluation/decision/change relation; §43 supplies actual five labels, scoped retirement and conditions. No performed runtime, direct evaluation mutation or automatic approved evolution.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation |
|---|---|
| Classification Change | Actual proposed or effected domain/source/definition change must be identified with prior/new editions, scope, authority, conditions, compatibility/history and separate execution evidence. A conceptual arrow performs no change or approval. |
| Governance Evaluation | Actual scoped evaluation concern under identified owner criteria/source editions, authority, evidence and coverage. It does not mutate the subject or prove a completed review/runtime, decision, condition fulfillment or actual operation. |
| Architectural Decision | Actual responsible decision for an identified proposal/subject/edition, scope and authority with criteria/evidence, conditions and rationale. A decision label or local phase command is not itself effective adoption, permission for all operations, publication or Baseline membership. |
| Approved | Actual scoped approval decision, not a fifth definition state, proof conditions fulfilled, performed activation/adoption/publication or exact Baseline inclusion. Independent actual requirements and evidence remain. |
| Deferred | Actual decision has not authorized the change at this time; unresolved rather than rejected. Missing decision/evidence does not automatically create Deferred. Preserve actual rationale/history; no approval or operation implied. |
| Rejected | Actual justified nonauthorization decision under its identified scope/authority/evidence. A conditional duplication branch is not proof that an actual rejection occurred; missing evidence is not fabricated rejection. |
| Classification Evolution | Actual proposed or effected domain/source/definition change must be identified with prior/new editions, scope, authority, conditions, compatibility/history and separate execution evidence. A conceptual arrow performs no change or approval. |


Governance evaluates proposed changes without directly modifying the Classification architecture.

This follows the established governance model in which a proposed Metadata change is evaluated before an architectural decision is made.

**Current governing scope.** The received view selects three outcomes; §43 retains all five actual decision labels and separately scoped retirement consequences. Its arrows describe conditional conceptual relations, not a performed pipeline or complete outcome/transition machine. Evaluation itself remains nonmutating; actual authorized operation and effect evidence are separate.

---

# 15. Semantic Preservation

Existing Classification semantics shall be preserved whenever possible.

A proposed change that materially changes the meaning of an existing Family, Type or Class shall be treated as a semantic architectural change.

Conceptually:

**Received unnamed visual in §15 (span 3 in original order).** Exact received text below is evidence, not a second governing rule.

```text

           Existing Definition
                    │
                    ▼

             Proposed Change
                    │
                    ▼

         Semantic Impact Analysis
         │
         ├── No semantic change
         │
         └── Semantic change

```

**Current relation scope:** Actual prior/new meaning-impact assessment with preserved conditional semantics and separately authorized necessary revision; no observed branch or completed change.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation |
|---|---|
| Existing Definition | Actual identified prior/new domain definition or assignment subject and source/definition edition. Historical interpretation, original validity, current use and retrieval differ; replacement is not automatic equivalence, rekeying or migration. |
| Proposed Change | Actual proposed or effected domain/source/definition change must be identified with prior/new editions, scope, authority, conditions, compatibility/history and separate execution evidence. A conceptual arrow performs no change or approval. |
| Semantic Impact Analysis | Actual scoped evaluation concern under identified owner criteria/source editions, authority, evidence and coverage. It does not mutate the subject or prove a completed review/runtime, decision, condition fulfillment or actual operation. |
| No semantic change | Actual evidence-dependent compatibility/meaning assessment branch, not observed result. Material change requires explicit actual authority, prior/new mandate, rationale/alternatives, concrete interfaces, history and later checks. |
| Semantic change | Actual evidence-dependent compatibility/meaning assessment branch, not observed result. Material change requires explicit actual authority, prior/new mandate, rationale/alternatives, concrete interfaces, history and later checks. |


Semantic redefinition requires explicit governance.

The Metadata Specification establishes the general requirement that every canonical element have one canonical meaning and that semantic definitions remain stable.

**Current governing scope.** This explicit semantic-change path remains valid. The received conditional preservation is retained, not converted to an absolute freeze. Material changes need honest compatibility and edition assessment; preserve the meaning of prior editions and decisions rather than silently reinterpreting history. Metadata owner stability clauses retain their real source-specific scope and any unreconciled owner differences.

---

# 19. Classification Lifecycle Governance

The Classification Lifecycle defines the conceptual states:

**Received unnamed visual in §19 (span 6 in original order).** Exact received text below is evidence, not a second governing rule.

```text

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

**Current relation scope:** Bounded state/use meanings and Lifecycle/Governance responsibility comparison; not complete transition routes/guards, invented actor, alias or implemented machine.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation |
|---|---|
| Defined | Actual bounded Classification definition-state/edition/use context under Lifecycle V2R1 matrices19/20/48 and independent mandates. Distinct from decision outcome, document Status, term/extension status, R assertion, result/finding and Milestone state. No automatic transition, deletion, exception or full route machine. |
| Active | Actual bounded Classification definition-state/edition/use context under Lifecycle V2R1 matrices19/20/48 and independent mandates. Distinct from decision outcome, document Status, term/extension status, R assertion, result/finding and Milestone state. No automatic transition, deletion, exception or full route machine. |
| Deprecated | Actual bounded Classification definition-state/edition/use context under Lifecycle V2R1 matrices19/20/48 and independent mandates. Distinct from decision outcome, document Status, term/extension status, R assertion, result/finding and Milestone state. No automatic transition, deletion, exception or full route machine. |
| Retired | Actual bounded Classification definition-state/edition/use context under Lifecycle V2R1 matrices19/20/48 and independent mandates. Distinct from decision outcome, document Status, term/extension status, R assertion, result/finding and Milestone state. No automatic transition, deletion, exception or full route machine. |


Governance authorizes transitions between these states.

Therefore:

**Received unnamed visual in §19 (span 7 in original order).** Exact received text below is evidence, not a second governing rule.

```text

            Lifecycle
            │
            └── defines states

            Governance
            │
            └── authorizes transitions

```

**Current relation scope:** Bounded state/use meanings and Lifecycle/Governance responsibility comparison; not complete transition routes/guards, invented actor, alias or implemented machine.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation |
|---|---|
| Lifecycle | Actual Lifecycle owner supplies bounded definition-state/use meaning and known requirements alongside genuine exact route/guard/actor/record gaps; not automatic aliases with Metadata artifact states or a complete implemented machine. |
| defines states | Actual Lifecycle owner supplies bounded definition-state/use meaning and known requirements alongside genuine exact route/guard/actor/record gaps; not automatic aliases with Metadata artifact states or a complete implemented machine. |
| Governance | Classification domain semantic/change conditions and need for an actual scoped responsible decision, distinct from common Workflow/Policies/Reviews/Baselines, Metadata representation authority and actual authorized operational executor. No organizational actor is invented. |
| authorizes transitions | Domain decision requirement for an actual governed transition; actual subject/edition, authority, applicable conditions and separately authorized execution/effect evidence remain. Source or diagram performs no transition. |


This distinction follows the established Metadata architecture: the Lifecycle defines states while Governance authorizes transitions.

**Current governing scope.** Use actual Lifecycle V2.0 R1 matrices19/20/48 and its independent Constraints/Specification obligations. Defined, Active, Deprecated and Retired are bounded working definition-state meanings, not document Status, local R assertion, term status, extension status, finding/result or Milestone state. Actual definition identity/edition, current/historical state assertion, authority, conditions and executor must be identified. The chain is not a complete route/guard machine; genuine exact actor/route/guard/record gaps are retained without waiving known governed-transition mandates.

| Subject | Known domain requirement | Actual evidence / remaining boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Definition and state | Lifecycle supplies bounded state/use meaning; Governance supplies required domain decision | Identify actual definition/source edition, prior/target assertion, scope, authority and applicable rules; complete guards/routes/actors are not established by this source |
| Activation | Existence is insufficient; governed transition requirements apply | Approved is a decision, not a fifth definition state; required conditions and actual activation evidence remain separate |
| Deprecation / retirement | Explicit applicable decisions, ordinary-new-use restrictions and required historical interpretation remain | Decision label is not a performed transition, universal severity, permission, deletion or automatic reassignment |
| Independent mandates | Constraints31–36 and Specification R019/R021/R022 retain actual scope | Missing exact integration/evidence does not waive a real mandatory requirement or prove a complete accepted machine |

---

# 20. Activation Governance

A Classification definition shall not become Active merely because it exists.

Activation requires a governance decision.

Conceptually:

**Received unnamed visual in §20 (span 8 in original order).** Exact received text below is evidence, not a second governing rule.

```text

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

          Governance Evaluation
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active

```

**Current relation scope:** Approved is an actual decision label between definition-state concerns, not a fifth state or automatic activation; actual conditions/authority/execution evidence required.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation |
|---|---|
| Defined | Actual bounded Classification definition-state/edition/use context under Lifecycle V2R1 matrices19/20/48 and independent mandates. Distinct from decision outcome, document Status, term/extension status, R assertion, result/finding and Milestone state. No automatic transition, deletion, exception or full route machine. |
| Governance Evaluation | Actual scoped evaluation concern under identified owner criteria/source editions, authority, evidence and coverage. It does not mutate the subject or prove a completed review/runtime, decision, condition fulfillment or actual operation. |
| Approved | Actual scoped approval decision, not a fifth definition state, proof conditions fulfilled, performed activation/adoption/publication or exact Baseline inclusion. Independent actual requirements and evidence remain. |
| Active | Actual bounded Classification definition-state/edition/use context under Lifecycle V2R1 matrices19/20/48 and independent mandates. Distinct from decision outcome, document Status, term/extension status, R assertion, result/finding and Milestone state. No automatic transition, deletion, exception or full route machine. |


The approval criteria depend on the nature and impact of the Classification definition.

**Current governing scope.** Approved in the exact received span is an approval decision, not a fifth definition state or automatic transition to Active. Actual authority, subject/definition edition, scope, applicable Lifecycle/Constraints conditions, evidence and authorized execution must establish any actual activation. No decision or operation is performed by retaining the diagram.

---

# 22. Retirement Governance

Retirement represents the end of normal active use.

A Classification shall only be Retired through an explicit governance decision.

Retirement shall not automatically imply deletion of historical references.

Conceptually:

**Received unnamed visual in §22 (span 9 in original order).** Exact received text below is evidence, not a second governing rule.

```text

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

**Current relation scope:** Conditional actual explicit retirement decision and resulting state concern; history remains required and no transition/deletion is performed.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation |
|---|---|
| Deprecated | Actual bounded Classification definition-state/edition/use context under Lifecycle V2R1 matrices19/20/48 and independent mandates. Distinct from decision outcome, document Status, term/extension status, R assertion, result/finding and Milestone state. No automatic transition, deletion, exception or full route machine. |
| Governance Decision | Actual responsible decision for an identified proposal/subject/edition, scope and authority with criteria/evidence, conditions and rationale. A decision label or local phase command is not itself effective adoption, permission for all operations, publication or Baseline membership. |
| Retired | Actual bounded Classification definition-state/edition/use context under Lifecycle V2R1 matrices19/20/48 and independent mandates. Distinct from decision outcome, document Status, term/extension status, R assertion, result/finding and Milestone state. No automatic transition, deletion, exception or full route machine. |

**Current governing scope.** Explicit retirement cannot silently erase history required by Lifecycle/Specification R021/R022 or convert earlier meaning into unknown meaning. Preserve actual definitions, relationships, assignments, decisions, source editions and needed pinned context. Retirement does not establish a performed migration or destroy references; live retrieval and archival preservation still need actual evidence.

---

# 24. Classification Replacement

When a Classification is superseded, Governance may authorize a replacement relationship.

Conceptually:

**Received unnamed visual in §24 (span 10 in original order).** Exact received text below is evidence, not a second governing rule.

```text

            Old Classification
                    │
              superseded by
                    │
                    ▼

            New Classification

```

**Current relation scope:** Scoped supersession relationship, not automatic equivalence, reclassification, migration, rekeying or changed pinned approval.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation |
|---|---|
| Old Classification | Actual identified prior/new domain definition or assignment subject and source/definition edition. Historical interpretation, original validity, current use and retrieval differ; replacement is not automatic equivalence, rekeying or migration. |
| superseded by | Scoped authorized replacement/supersession relation between identified old/new subjects/editions. Not automatic equivalence, reassignment, migration, history deletion or retargeting pinned approvals. |
| New Classification | Actual identified prior/new domain definition or assignment subject and source/definition edition. Historical interpretation, original validity, current use and retrieval differ; replacement is not automatic equivalence, rekeying or migration. |


The existence of a replacement does not automatically require historical documents to be reclassified.

Migration decisions must be separately governed.

**Current governing scope.** Supersession is not necessarily semantic equivalence. Establish actual old/new identities and editions, relationship authority, impact and preserved history. A replacement decision alone does not reclassify documents, retarget pinned approvals, regenerate document IDs or perform migration.

---

# 25. Classification Migration Governance

Classification migration is a governance concern when it changes the Classification assigned to existing documents.

Governance shall evaluate:

- semantic equivalence;
- historical preservation;
- migration scope;
- impact;
- compatibility;
- validation requirements.

Conceptually:

**Received unnamed visual in §25 (span 11 in original order).** Exact received text below is evidence, not a second governing rule.

```text

                    │
                    ▼

                    │
                    ▼

                    │
                    ▼

```

**Current relation scope:** Conditional separately authorized migration concern with concrete prior/new batch/history/conditions/target checks; no operation or blanket permission.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation |
|---|---|

# 4. Extensibility Principles

Classification Extensibility follows the principles below.

---

## 4.1. Architectural Stability

Ordinary extensions shall preserve applicable Classification stability;necessary assessed mandate revision follows§79.

An extension shall not silently undermine foundations;any necessary foundational change requires explicit actual prior/new authority,need,impact,compatibility/history and transition evidence.

---

## 4.2. Semantic Preservation

Ordinary extensions shall preserve the established meaning of existing Classification Elements;necessary explicitly assessed semantic revision follows§79.

An extension shall not silently redefine an existing Family, Type or Class.

**Current governing scope.** No silent redefinition is mandatory. Necessary explicit revision identifies actual prior/new meaning,need,authority,alternatives,rationale,batch,compatibility/mappings/history,pinned continuity,authorized transition and later checks. Existing owner restrictions remain actual pending differences until separately reconciled;the word extension grants no permission.

---

## 4.3. Structural Preservation

Ordinary extensions shall remain compatible with applicable canonical Classification structure;necessary structural incompatibility is explicitly assessed and governed.

New elements shall occupy positions permitted by the Classification Schema.

**Current governing scope.** Actual Schema34 known duties versus genuine general multiplicity/field/population gaps remain. Documentary roles do not impose a universal tree;actual defined scheme positions/properties still require real authority. Necessary change does not leave simultaneous contradictory same-context canonical demands.

---

## 4.4. Backward Compatibility

Extensions should preserve the validity and interpretation of existing Classification whenever reasonably possible.

Existing documents should not become semantically ambiguous merely because Classification evolves.

**Current governing scope.** Interpretation,original validity,current compliance/use and retrieval differ. Preserve compatible ordinary use where feasible;necessary incompatibility must be explicit and governed for actual affected editions/consumers. New rules are not backdated and required history is not discretionary.

---

## 4.5. Canonical Preservation

Extensions shall remain part of one canonical Classification architecture.

Independent competing Classification models shall not be introduced as extensions.

**Current governing scope.** One canonical architecture is a requirement,not a complete populated accepted model or proof every proposal is canonical. Actual Drafts and scoped experiments may exist without competing canonical authority;changed successors inherit no earlier approval or exact Baseline membership.

---

## 4.6. Technology Independence

Extension mechanisms shall remain independent of:

- programming languages;
- databases;
- repositories;
- serialization formats;
- implementation frameworks.

**Current governing scope.** Meaning independence preserves actual owner duties for descriptor/Schema/effective Profile/Instance,physical placement,references,indexes,interfaces,access/retrieval/freshness,usage and required history. It does not prove installed capability or no effects from changing representation.

---

## 4.7. Controlled Evolution

Classification extensions shall be introduced through the applicable governance process.

Actual scoped approval is necessary for canonical extension;required conditions must be fulfilled and effective adoption evidenced under§§35/37/39/79.

**Current governing scope.** Necessary actual approval must identify proposal/subject/edition,scope,authority,criteria/evidence,rationale and conditions. Actual required fulfillment,effective adoption/activation and separate publication/Baseline claims follow§§34–39. CONTINUAR authorizes this working phase,not canonical permission.

---

# 7. Extensible Classification Elements

The following Classification artifacts may be extended.

---

## 7.1. Classification Families

An actual Family membership option may be introduced only for a real canonical component or admitted documentary area under responsible authority;it is not automatic allocation of a new component or Type-owning high-level domain.

An existing Family membership meaning shall not be silently redefined;necessary assessed revision requires the actual prior/new authority and continuity evidence in§79.

**Current governing scope.** Membership options require actual component/admitted-area existence and authorization;directory alias,role label or a Family A/B/C picture creates no component,key,series,population or new primary Type. Actual scope/definition/history remains identifiable.

---

## 7.2. Classification Types

Primary document Type is exactly one uniform Architecture,Structure,Behavior or Reference responsibility across Families;ordinary extension does not add Family-owned Types or a fifth primary responsibility.

Actual Family-context valid-use restrictions may apply without owning/redefining that vocabulary. Necessary revision of the governing responsibility mandate requires explicit assessed prior/new authority under§79.

**Current governing scope.** Exactly one primary responsibility is known for every applicable normalized document. Context may restrict valid use without redefining the four-value vocabulary or authorizing all pairs. Generic Type/kind examples and relationship types are separate from primary documentary Type;no automatic rekey on classification change.

---

## 7.3. Classification Classes

Class is a separate optional explicitly defined non-conflicting dimension;new defined values need actual responsible scope,not a universal Type-child level.

Any Class used shall respect its actual defined meaning and applicable semantic/structural scheme constraints,without mandatory third field,value or complete population being implied.

**Current governing scope.** Optional does not mean unrestricted. Actual category/value/definition/assignment and responsible scheme relation/meaning differ;no general maximum,mandatory third field or complete vocabulary is invented. Preserve known Schema34 duties despite genuine unrelated general-rule gaps.

---

## 7.4. Classification Relationships

New relationship types may be introduced when an architectural requirement cannot be adequately represented by the existing relationship vocabulary.

Relationship extensions shall define:

- semantics;
- direction;
- source;
- target;
- cardinality;
- constraints;
- lifecycle implications.

**Current governing scope.** All seven received relationship-definition subjects remain real.

| Actual extension concern | Known obligation | Genuine detail / evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Family / Type / Class | Actual membership,exactly one uniform four-value primary Type,optional explicitly defined nonconflicting Class | No universal Family-owned role hierarchy,mandatory Class or complete population/count/field catalog |
| Kind / definition / association / assertion / endpoint | Actual responsible semantics,typed source/target,direction,cardinality,constraints and lifecycle context | Selected kind names or a Source–kind–target illustration allocate no universal tuple key/Metadata fields or DF identity to every endpoint |
| Properties / hierarchy / cycles | Retain actually defined direction,inverse,symmetry,transitivity,permitted hierarchical/acyclic/ancestor and no-undefined-reference duties | No arbitrary property values,global all-relations DAG or reverse stored record;actual semantic graphs and indispensable provider dependencies differ |
| Cardinality / required or optional links | Actual known Schema34/Relationships20/Constraints28 and defined rule obligations remain | Genuine general minima/maxima/parent/child/assignment/population gaps grant no all-pairs permission or blanket known-duty deferral |
| Integrity / identity / evidence | Apply actual subject/kind/definition/source editions,uniqueness/explicit exceptions,applicability and supported observations | Existing endpoints alone are not full validity;lookup/authority/check gaps are not fabricated orphan/Invalid;historical/current use and retrieval differ |

No kind,association,assignment,record or provider migration is performed here.

---

## 7.5. Classification Schema

The Classification Schema may evolve through the controlled introduction of new structural capabilities.

Existing structural definitions shall remain valid whenever reasonably possible.

**Current governing scope.** Ordinary compatible additions and necessary assessed structural revision differ. Real existing valid structures,defined capabilities/constraints/validation/governance requirements remain;no Schema/Profile/Instance representation duty is waived or complete new representation allocated.

---

## 7.6. Classification Dictionary

The Classification Dictionary may be extended through the addition of newly approved Classification definitions.

Existing canonical definitions remain authoritative unless explicitly changed through governance.

**Current governing scope.** Actual responsible approved definition/edition,applicable fulfilled conditions and authoritative incorporation where required must be evidenced. Dictionary entry naming is not automatic term/Element/document-state alias or proof a complete approved vocabulary already exists.

---

## 7.7. Classification Specification

The Classification Specification may evolve to incorporate approved Classification extensions.

The Specification remains the normative integration point for the resulting Classification architecture.

**Current governing scope.** Actual explicit normative integration remains owned by Specification;Type Reference alone neither grants nor removes authority. Identified approved changes with fulfilled required conditions do not by themselves prove effective publication,activation,complete merged precedence/catalog or Core implementation.

---

# 8. Extension Categories

Classification extensions may belong to one of the following categories.

**Current governing scope.** All seven extension categories remain selected concerns,not universal mutually exclusive physical fields,closed decision outcomes or automatic severity. An actual proposal can touch several concerns while retaining exact scope,need,authority and assessed compatibility/history.

---

## 8.1. Additive Extension

Introduces new Classification Elements without changing the meaning of existing elements.

Example:

**Received unnamed visual in §8.1 (span 2 in original order).** Exact received wording is evidence,not a second governing rule.

```text

            Existing Classification
            │
            ├── Family A
            │
            └── Family B

```

**Current relation scope:** Unallocated Family membership addition illustrations;actual area/component authority and assessed impact needed,no allocated population or no-effects guarantee.

| Received label / relation | Current typed interpretation |

| Existing Classification | Actual authoritative domain model/source-edition concern,or received organization placeholder;not proof accepted complete population,canonical adoption,activation or implemented engine/provider DAG. Actual approval/fulfilled conditions/effective adoption and independent owner duties remain. |
| Family A | Unallocated illustrative membership-option label;actual canonical component/admitted-area authority required. Not new component,key/series,populated vocabulary or Family-owned primary Type. |
| Family B | Unallocated illustrative membership-option label;actual canonical component/admitted-area authority required. Not new component,key/series,populated vocabulary or Family-owned primary Type. |

## 8.2. Specialization Extension

**Current governing scope.** Specialization belongs to actual explicitly defined context/relationship/scheme semantics. Current Family,primary Type and optional Class are complementary roles;the exact received hierarchy is historical evidence,not a concurrent current rule.

## 8.3. Structural Extension

Necessary structural incompatibility requires actual assessed prior/new mandate authority,need,alternatives,batch,compatibility/history and authorized transition;approval alone permits no erasure of required meaning.
